pr.title: Add a reboot to firmware option to the System menu
pr.body: Getting into the BIOS usually means mashing `F2`, `F12` or `Del` at boot, and on a lot of machines the window's gone before the monitor even wakes up. If you're anything like me, you also forget which key to use most of the time. This adds _System > Reboot to Firmware_, which reboots you straight into the firmware setup screen. It asks logind to set the UEFI one-shot flag, then runs the normal `omarchy-system-reboot`, so it behaves just like Reboot. The flag goes on before any window closes, so if the firmware says no you keep your session and get a notification telling you why. The row only shows up if logind says the firmware supports it (`omarchy-hw-firmware-setup`), so legacy BIOS machines never see it. There's also a FAQ entry, and searching the menu for "bios" or "uefi" finds it. I called the command `omarchy system firmware setup` rather than `omarchy system reboot firmware`. The router falls back to the longest match, so with the second name a typo like `reboot firmwre` would just reboot and close all your windows. One known gap: if the scheduled `systemctl reboot` fails after that, the flag stays set and your next reboot goes into setup once. ## Preview

pr.title: Show elapsed time beside each usage meter in the agents panel
pr.body: Each limit meter now shows the cycle it is measuring, so you can see at a glance whether the spend is ahead of the clock or behind it. ## The mechanism `windowSpanMs()` already parsed a window's length out of a collector's label, and `resetMsFor()` already gave the time left — but `limitWindow()` threw the length away, keeping only the display `title`, and "Session" (which is what a 5-hour window is called on screen) carries no duration. So the fix keeps `spanMs` on the window, read from the raw label *before* the title is derived from it, and `LimitRow` derives the elapsed fraction as `1 - remaining / span`, clamped, with `-1` meaning the length is unknown. Rendering it in the existing bar: the spent fill is unchanged, a dim band under it is the elapsed fraction of the cycle, and a notch at the band's edge marks where the clock stands. Fill past the notch is ahead of the cycle, short of it is behind. The row repeats the comparison in words beside the reset countdown — "33% behind", "on pace" — and stays as quiet as the countdown unless the window is ahead. pr.title: Keep Bluetooth power-on usable for Chromium phone passkeys
pr.body: ## TL;DR Power Bluetooth down through BlueZ instead of rfkill so Chromium can turn it back on for phone passkeys. Preserve the power preference separately and restore it in the graphical session. ## Why Omarchy’s current off path sets an rfkill software block. Chromium only requests `org.bluez.Adapter1.Powered=true`, which BlueZ rejects while blocked; another unblock step is required even though the browser offers a power-on button. ## What The changed off path permits application power-on: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Omarchy off] -->|"Powered=false, was rfkill block"| B[Adapter off and unblocked] B -->|"Chromium: Powered=true"| C[Bluetooth on for phone passkey] ``` - Replace boot-persistent blocking with a saved preference restored at graphical login, waiting through delayed Bluetooth availability. Snapshot actual power at logout, including changes made by other clients. - Preserve existing radio blocks during migration and login restoration. pr.body: ## Problem The bar clock widget always shows weekday/month names (`dddd`, `MMMM`, etc.) in English, even when the system locale (`LANG`) is set to another language (e.g. German). Confirmed with `localectl`/`locale -a` correctly reporting `de_DE.UTF-8`, other apps (GTK file picker, CLI `date`) rendering correctly in German, yet the bar kept showing "Wednesday" instead of "Mittwoch". ## Root cause `shell/plugins/panels/clock/BarWidget.qml`'s `formatted()` uses the global `Qt.formatDateTime(date, format)`, which renders locale-dependent tokens like `dddd`/`MMMM` in English regardless of the system locale. Verified directly with a minimal Quickshell reproduction: ``` LANG=de_DE.UTF-8 quickshell -p /tmp/qstest DEBUG qml: Qt.locale().name = de_DE DEBUG qml: formatDateTime dddd = Wednesday // wrong ``` Whereas `Qt.locale().toString(date, format)` correctly honors the locale: ``` DEBUG qml: dayName(3, Long): Mittwoch DEBUG qml: loc.toString(date, "dddd"): Mittwoch // correct ``` ## Fix Swap `Qt.formatDateTime(date, ...)` for `Qt.locale().toString(date, ...)` in the clock widget's `formatted()` function. pr.body: A toast is a layer-shell surface on the **Overlay** layer, so a fullscreen client can never cover one — it lands on top of the fullscreen video or game it should be staying out of the way of. This is the same defect with a trigger the idle service cannot see: any fullscreen toplevel. ## What it does A fullscreen window covers **its own output**, so that is the only surface held back: - **the screens that are free keep showing toasts**, with the lifetime they have always had — a film fullscreen on the main screen no longer costs you notifications on the laptop screen next to it; - the covered output draws nothing: `visible: popupModel.count > 0 && !popupWindow.covered`, resolved per monitor's active workspace; - **when every output is covered** there is nowhere left to deliver a toast, so the notification is silenced the way DND silences it — no toast, a `writeSilenced` history entry for the notification centre — instead of being created to queue up behind the fullscreen window. pr.title: Warn when a plugin's service or id lookup is denied
pr.body: Addresses the first half of #13794. Scoped plugin shells return `null` (or `""`) for lookups a plugin isn't allowed to make, which looks the same as a service that hasn't loaded yet. pr.title: Add opt-in request-dispatch hook before agent launch
pr.body: Prompted `omarchy agent` launches may hand the request to a user-owned executable at `~/.config/omarchy/agents/request-dispatch` before starting the default agent. The prompt travels on stdin; `--fallback-agent` and `--cwd` remain on argv. Exit 0 accepts responsibility for the request. Exit 3 explicitly declines before starting work and permits fallback. Every other failure stops and preserves its status, avoiding duplicate execution after a crash or signal. An accepting dispatcher works even when the configured fallback is not installed. Promptless launches do not use the hook. Fixes #12621. Validation: the focused dispatch fixture passes, including missing-fallback acceptance, explicit decline, statuses 1/127/143, promptless launches, non-executable hooks, and exact NUL-separated fallback arguments. Restoring the original implementation or generic nonzero fallback fails the regressions. Other-owned hooks and a real desktop session were not exercised.

pr.title: Let PipeWire follow the source's sample rate
pr.body: Part 2 of the pro-audio proposal in #13832. It's a draft until the discussion settles whether this should be on by default. ## Problem PipeWire's `clock.allowed-rates` is `[ 48000 ]` on a stock install, so every 44.1 kHz track and 88.2/96 kHz recording is resampled on its way to the device. On macOS, CoreAudio follows the source's rate. ## Change - **`config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/10-sample-rates.conf`** sets `default.clock.allowed-rates = [ 44100 48000 88200 96000 ]`. When a stream starts on an idle device, PipeWire switches the device to that stream's rate if the hardware supports it. Otherwise it resamples exactly as it does today. New installs get the file through `config/`. - **Migration `1790745839`** installs the drop-in for existing users with `omarchy-refresh-config`. It also applies the same rates to the running graph with `pw-metadata`, since PipeWire only reads `conf.d` at startup. So the change takes effect on update without restarting PipeWire or interrupting playback. If the user already has the file, the migration leaves it and the running rates alone. #11092 pins *screen recording* audio at 48 kHz, which is a separate setting. pr.body: At login the menu checks the default browser (Defaults > Browser) through `omarchy-default-browser`, which asks `xdg-settings`. xdg-utils doesn't know `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=Hyprland`, so it falls back to probing for XFCE with `xprop -root`, twice in `xdg-settings` and twice more in the `xdg-mime` it calls: ``` Hyprland └─ omarchy-launch-shell └─ quickshell └─ bash (menu guard batch, MenuModel.js) └─ omarchy-default-browser └─ xdg-settings get default-web-browser └─ xprop -root ``` This reads the browser with `omarchy-cmd-default-browser` instead, the lookup the browser launchers already use. pr.title: Add a delayed screenshot to the capture menu
pr.body: Some things disappear the moment you reach for a screenshot. Hover tooltips, dropdowns and right click menus all close when a key goes down, so there's no way to get them into a shot today. Windows solved this years ago with a delay option in the Snipping Tool, and this adds the same thing. Capture now has a Delayed Screenshot submenu with 3, 5 and 10 second options. Pick one, set up whatever you need on screen, and Omasnap opens when the countdown hits zero. The countdown uses the existing OSD, so it looks like the volume and brightness popups. From the terminal it's a flag on the existing command: ``` omarchy capture screenshot --delay=5 ``` It works with the other arguments too, so `omarchy capture screenshot region save --delay=3` does what you'd expect. A delay that isn't a whole number of seconds is rejected with exit code 2 before anything opens. ### Multiple monitors Omasnap captures whichever monitor has focus, so the countdown sits on that monitor. pr.title: Bound fingerprint retry attempts with exponential backoff (#13748)
pr.body: ### Summary Fixes #13748. When the lock screen is left locked on machines with fingerprint readers configured, `Service.qml` previously retried authentication unconditionally on every failure and PAM error every 250ms with no retry ceiling and no backoff. When sensors report persistent errors (such as Broadcom or libfprint-tod thermal protection), this created an unbounded retry storm (e.g. over 100,000 attempts overnight) that overheated and disabled the sensor. ### Changes - Bound consecutive fingerprint retry attempts to a maximum of 15 attempts. - Apply exponential backoff to `fingerprintRetryTimer.interval` from 250ms doubling up to 4000ms. - Guard `fingerprintPam.onError` and `handleFingerprintFinished()` failure branches with `fingerprintRetryTimer.attempts < 15`. - Reset attempt counts and backoff interval to baseline (250ms) on: - Fresh lock initiation (`resetAuthenticationState()`) - Successful fingerprint unlock (`result === PamResult.Success`) - Screen wake / user interaction (`runWake()`) if attempts were previously exhausted, re-enabling authentication when the user returns to the machine. - Add regression test coverage in `test/shell.d/lock-blank-fingerprint-test.sh`

pr.title: Stop the dictation indicator from making voxtype run nvidia-smi
pr.body: ## Problem On hybrid laptops with the dGPU off, the bar's dictation indicator wakes the NVIDIA GPU and loads the NVIDIA driver every time the bar is built: at login, on shell restart, and on every resume. It runs twice each time, because `Indicators.qml` creates `Dictation` for both the horizontal and the vertical bar. On an ASUS G14 (GA403WR) with supergfxd in Integrated mode, the NVIDIA driver deadlocked during supergfxd's post-resume teardown. The next suspend then hung and froze the laptop. ## Root cause `bin/omarchy-voxtype-status` runs `voxtype status --follow --extended --format json`. With `--extended`, voxtype 1.1.0 runs `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name --format=csv,noheader` once at process start ([`detect_nvidia_gpu`]( reached via `ExtendedStatusInfo::from_config` -> `inventory()`). The real `nvidia-smi` goes through libnvidia-ml, which runs the setuid `nvidia-modprobe`. That loads `nvidia.ko` by name, so supergfxd's `blacklist nvidia` doesn't stop it. The load wakes the dGPU. pr.title: Smooth out battery time
pr.body: ## Summary Two looks at the battery a few seconds apart now show the same hours. Before, those hours were the charge left divided by one short power sample, so a sample that doubled cut the hours in half while the battery barely moved. ## Why this estimate UPower sets time to empty to `3600 * energy / energy_rate` in [`src/up-device-battery.c`]( On a pack with about 65 Wh left, a sample moving from about 5.6 W to about 11 W moves the printed time from about 11 hours to about 6 hours. The battery did not lose half its charge. The replacement is the same relation, charge left divided by how fast charge is leaving, taken from the battery's own counter: - Between looks, `new = old × charge_now / charge_then`. An 11-hour reading (39600 seconds) at 6,000,000 µAh, after the counter falls to 5,997,000, is 39580 seconds, printed as 10h 59m. Half the charge left prints as 5h 30m. A power sample that says 3 hours, with the counter unmoved, changes this term by zero. Time asleep changes it by zero, because sleep did not remove charge. - A new rate is `charge_now × seconds / charge_used`, and only when the span is 60–180 seconds and the charge used is more than one counter step (1000 µAh). pr.title: Keep an early polkit Enter and submit it when PAM asks
pr.body: The polkit dialog shows its password field as soon as a request starts, but PAM only asks for the password once `polkit-agent-helper-1` is running. On polkit 127 that helper is a socket-activated, sandboxed systemd service (`polkit-agent-helper@.service`), and starting it can take seconds. If you press Enter before PAM asks, `submitResponse()` returns early because `flow.isResponseRequired` is still false. The keypress is dropped without any feedback, the password is never sent, and users end up pressing Enter repeatedly. If nobody presses Enter again, polkit gives up with: ``` pam_unix(polkit-1:auth): conversation failed pam_unix(polkit-1:auth): auth could not identify password for [user] polkit-agent-helper-1: pam_authenticate failed: Authentication token manipulation error ``` This matches the "conversation failed" shape reported in #8924. ## Change - Pressing Enter with a non-empty field before PAM asks now queues the submit. The typed text stays in the field, which is read-only while queued, and is submitted as soon as `isResponseRequired` turns true. When that lookup comes back empty — because the real output was destroyed and recreated (observed on suspend/resume; some drivers do this even on a plain DPMS cycle), or because Hyprland is briefly reporting its own placeholder `"FALLBACK"` monitor name while the real one is unavailable — the `|| targetScreen` fallback keeps whatever `targetScreen` already held. If the old value was a reference to a screen object that no longer exists, the window silently fails to (re)map on the next open. pr.title: Preserve docked lid policy across logout and DPMS
pr.body: With an external monitor connected and the laptop lid closed, logging out can suspend the machine before SDDM has finished starting. logind counts enabled DRM outputs when deciding whether the laptop is docked, so compositor teardown or DPMS can temporarily defeat `HandleLidSwitchDocked=ignore` even though the display remains physically connected. On the affected machine (Omarchy 4.0.4, systemd 261.2, Intel Panther Lake/xe), the journal shows logout, SDDM startup, and logind's "Suspending..." in the same second. Resume then produced external DisplayPort link-training failures. This is the same underlying distinction described in systemd/systemd#41898. Specific laptop model is an X1 Carbon gen 14 but I don't know that that would matter. This change uses Omarchy's existing physical-connector detector to hold a `handle-lid-switch` inhibitor while an external monitor is connected. A system service keeps it alive between user sessions and at the greeter. pr.title: Stop mise wrappers recursing when mise's activation variables are missing
pr.body: A wrapper from `omarchy-mise-install` ends in `exec mise x <package> -- <bin>`, and `mise x` looks `<bin>` up by name. It puts the directories it added ahead of the rest of PATH, and it knows which those are from the variables `mise activate` exports (`__MISE_DIFF`). A process that starts a wrapper with an activated PATH but a reduced environment (a service, a sandbox, or a launcher that passes only a safe set of variables) leaves those out. `mise x` then treats the package's directory as an ordinary entry behind `~/.local/bin`, finds the wrapper again, and the wrapper runs itself until something kills it, holding a CPU core the whole time. pr.title: iMac 12,2 - Disable Chromium GPU compositing on legacy radeon GPUs
pr.body: Fixes #13760. Related: #3603 / #6274. ## Problem On pre-GCN AMD GPUs driven by the legacy `radeon` kernel driver, Chromium's GPU compositor draws artifacts and glitches (#13760, iMac12,2 with Radeon HD 6770M), or hard-freezes the system (#3603 / #6274, Radeon HD 5xxx). These GPUs have no Vulkan support, and `omarchy-hw-vulkan` can't tell, because the RADV ICD is installed even though RADV refuses non-amdgpu devices. `--disable-gpu-compositing` fixes it; `--use-angle=gl --disable-features=Vulkan,SkiaGraphite` does not. The flag must not become a global default: #13174 shows it makes Intel Iris Xe worse. ## Change - `omarchy-hw-radeon`: new detector. It succeeds when a display-class PCI device is bound to `radeon`, reading sysfs driver links like `omarchy-hw-nvidia` does, so it doesn't wake runtime-suspended GPUs. - `omarchy-install-chromium-legacy-gpu [flags-file]`: appends `--disable-gpu-compositing` to the Chromium flags file on that hardware only. pr.title: Walk the calendar grid at noon so a midnight DST start can't repeat a day
pr.body: `monthGrid()` walked the calendar from local midnight. Where DST starts at midnight (America/Santiago on 2026-09-06), that midnight doesn't exist, and QML's JS engine resolves it to 23:00 the day before. The cursor stayed on the 5th, the 5th was drawn twice, and every later day sat under the wrong weekday. This walks the grid at noon, which a DST change never skips. The first-of-month weekday lookup gets the same change. V8 resolves a missing midnight forward instead, so this bug doesn't reproduce under the Node test runner. I checked the fix by running the old and new `Model.js` against a `Date` that falls back like QML's engine: the old code gives `4 5 5 6 7` and the new code gives `4 5 6 7 8`. pr.title: Clear setgid when hardening Windows VM mount sources
pr.body: The dockurr/windows container runs `chmod 2777 /shared` on an empty share, which lands on `~/Windows`. For directories, GNU chmod keeps setuid/setgid when given a 3 or 4 digit octal mode, so `chmod 0700` left it at `2700`. `mounted_leaf_matches` and the post-chmod check in `prepare_caller_mounts` require exactly `700`, so every later launch failed with the generic "Failed to start Windows VM!". This uses `chmod 00700` in the two places that harden the mount sources. The five-digit mode is the documented way to clear those bits numerically. It adds a case to `windows-vm-compose-test.sh` that starts from a `2777` share and checks that it ends up at `700` and still verifies. I couldn't run `windows-vm-compose-test.sh` myself: it needs unprivileged mount namespaces, and I only had a Windows machine. `bash -n` passes on both files. pr.title: move screen recording from `Alt + Print Screen` to preserve SysRq keys
pr.body: ## Brief The default `Alt + Print Screen` screen-recording binding conflicts with Linux Magic SysRq, which uses the same chord as the prefix for emergency and diagnostic commands. SysRq can help recover from an unresponsive system and inspect or debug kernel state during crashes and it is quite an important Linux feature. ## Config Unless the key chord is actually available, then this would be naught; but if so, then here's how you configure them to access more commands. The available commands can be restricted through the kernel.sysrq sysctl: 0 disables keyboard access, 1 enables every command, and a bitmask enables selected categories such as diagnostic dumps, filesystem sync, read-only remounting, process signaling, or reboot. See the [Linux kernel SysRq documentation]( ## Solution Move screen recording to `Ctrl + Print Screen`. The Hyprland binding-conflicts test passes.

pr.title: Open the captive portal sign-in page on detection when asked to
pr.body: Phones open a hotel Wi-Fi's sign-in page by themselves. On a laptop you notice that nothing loads first, then go looking for the panel and its button. This adds an opt-in for the network widget: ```json { "id": "omarchy.network", "autoSignIn": true } ``` With it set, the panel runs the same action as its button the moment NetworkManager reports a portal: the same fixed http URL, launched as argv, nothing taken from the portal itself, so the constraints the button already follows stay in place. The connectivity state flips once per portal, so the page opens once. Off by default, nothing changes unless it is asked for. The fixture now reconnects behind a portal with the setting on, and the runner expects two launches, the button's and the automatic one. The manual's networking page gets a short section on portals. One repair on the way: the fixture emitted `textKey("r")` while the signal has taken a modifiers argument since the Elsewhen keyboard work, so on a machine with a compositor the runtime half of this test errored out with "Insufficient arguments" before any assertion ran. It passes again with the argument.

pr.title: Keep RPC method names out of the Codex limits help text
pr.body: Follow-up to #13733. ## Problem When a Codex limits read fails, `fetch_codex_rpc()` writes `str(exc)` into `authHelpText`. `rpc_request` raises `TimeoutError(method)`, so the Agents panel's help card shows the bare RPC method name. Before #13733 that was `account/read`; now it's `account/rateLimits/read`. The panel shows `authHelpText` as guidance under "Codex limits unavailable", so a method name that looks like a permission reads as a sign-in or authorization problem. It sent me looking for a Codex sign-out/sign-in option, even though Codex was signed in and working the whole time. ## Change - A timeout now says Codex didn't answer the usage request in time and that it will retry on the next refresh. pr.title: Detect NEXT Biometrics readers as fingerprint hardware
pr.body: An NB-2033-U (`298d:2033`) in a Fujitsu Lifebook is a working fingerprint reader, but `omarchy-hw-fingerprint` exits 1 on it, so the fingerprint setup never offers to enroll. The detector matches on a product string like `*fingerprint*` / `*biometric*` or a vendor ID from `fingerprint_vendors`. The reader announces itself as `NB-2033-U`, which trips neither: the product string carries no such word, and `298d` is not in the list. NEXT Biometrics builds fingerprint sensors only, so `298d` belongs in the vendor list alongside the other single-purpose vendors already there, rather than in the product-string branch. Verified on the reader this is from: ```console $ /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-hw-fingerprint; echo $? 1 $ git clone && ./bin/omarchy-hw-fingerprint; echo $? 0 ``` The added test case fails without the vendor-list change and passes with it.

pr.title: Fall back to device connection state and live status in network bar widget
pr.body: ### Summary Ensures the status bar network widget continues to display an active Wi-Fi state even when Quickshell has not populated or matched a `connectedWifiNetwork` object. ### Problem In `Panel.qml`, `kind` currently requires `connectedWifiNetwork` to evaluate to true in order to display the `wifi` icon. However, in cases where: 1. An 802.1X/Enterprise Wi-Fi profile omits `802-11-wireless.mode` (common with eduroam CAT tools and system profiles where NetworkManager defaults to infrastructure mode, but Quickshell rejects profiles without an explicit mode string), or 2. The scanner is stopped/closed and AP scan objects churn, `connectedWifiNetwork` returns `null`. This causes the topbar to show "Disconnected" (`󰤮`) even while `wifiDevice. connected` is true and `omarchy-network-status` is actively routing traffic and streaming bytes. ### Solution - Fall back to `(wifiDevice && wifiDevice.connected) || info.type === "wifi"` in `kind`. - Derive fallback `signalStrength` from live `info.signal_dbm` or device state when `connectedWifiNetwork` is null. - Added regression test in `test/shell.d/network-test.sh`.

pr.title: Preserve notification images from localhost file URLs
pr.body: Notifications using `file://localhost/tmp/avatar.png` keep referencing the sender's original file instead of copying it into the notification state directory. If the sender deletes that file, the persisted notification loses its image. `localImageFile()` removes `file://` but then rejects the remaining `localhost/...` because it does not start with `/`. Recognize an exact, case-insensitive `localhost` authority before decoding the path. This lets the existing persistence flow copy both `appIcon` and `image` values and restore them from the cache. Other host authorities remain rejected; themed icons and `image://` handling are unchanged. This follows the local-file semantics in [RFC 8089]( Regression coverage checks lowercase/uppercase localhost, percent-encoded spaces, single decoding, remote/lookalike hosts, both image roles, serialization/restoration, repeat persistence, and preservation of the live snapshot. Validation: - `bash test/shell.d/notifications-test.sh`: 152 assertions pass with Node 20.20.2 and Git Bash 5.2.26 on Windows, using a test-launcher-only conversion of `ROOT` to a Windows path. pr.title: Fix Display panel display toggle using rejected hyprctl keyword
pr.body: ## Problem The Display panel's per-display enable/disable toggle (the monitors row) silently does nothing on current Omarchy. `Panel.qml` builds the toggle command with the hyprlang-era CLI: ```js actionProc.command = ["hyprctl", "keyword", "monitor", name + (enabled ? ",disable" : ",preferred,auto,auto")] ``` Under the Lua config system, `hyprctl keyword` is rejected: ``` $ hyprctl keyword monitor eDP-1,disable keyword can't work with non-legacy parsers. pr.title: Restore the keyboard backlight after hibernation
pr.body: ## Problem After a long `suspend-then-hibernate` (or a plain hibernate), the laptop resumes with the keyboard backlight off, and it stays off until a brightness key is pressed. The system-sleep hook that `omarchy-hibernation-setup` installs (`default/systemd/system-sleep/keyboard-backlight`) runs `brightnessctl set 0` before hibernating. That's the ASUS S4 workaround. But it has no `post` branch, so nothing turns the light back on. It writes straight to the device and bypasses `omarchy-brightness-keyboard`, so `omarchy-system-wake` → `omarchy-brightness-keyboard restore` has nothing saved to restore either. Plain suspend is unaffected, because the hook only acts on the hibernate phase. Seen on a Dell (`dell::kbd_backlight`), so this applies to any laptop with hibernation set up, not just ASUS. ## Change - The hook now goes through the shared command: `omarchy-brightness-keyboard off` before hibernating and `omarchy-brightness-keyboard restore` after resume. It still acts only on the hibernate phase, and the duplicated device lookup is gone. - A migration refreshes the installed copy, since `omarchy-hibernation-setup` copies the hook rather than linking it. pr.title: Stop mistaking the T2 chip for an Apple GPU in Vulkan detection
pr.body: Fixes #13727 ## Summary - The Vulkan driver detection matched `(VGA|Display).*Apple` against `lspci`. `VGA` matches inside `Non-VGA`, so the T2 chip (`Non-VGA unclassified device: Apple Inc. T2 Bridge Controller`) made every T2 Mac install `vulkan-asahi`, the Apple Silicon GPU driver. - The match is now anchored on the lspci class name (`^\S+ (VGA compatible controller|Display controller): `), which keeps the existing VGA/Display semantics and just stops matching `Non-VGA`. This covers all three copies of the pattern: `install/hardware/vulkan.sh`, `migrations/1784401744.sh` and `bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`. - A new migration removes `vulkan-asahi` from x86_64 installs, where it can never drive a GPU. It only runs when `pacman -Rs --print` shows the removal is clean, so it never breaks a package that relies on it as its only Vulkan driver. Apple Silicon installs are left alone. This overlaps with the sysfs rewrites in #12076, #11259 and #12681, which would fix `vulkan.sh` for fresh installs. It's kept deliberately small so it can land independently or be folded into whichever of those merges first. The upgrade-script fix and the cleanup migration aren't covered by any of them. #

pr.title: Fix Codex limits timing out on buffered app-server replies
pr.body: ## Problem The agents panel shows **Codex limits unavailable** even when `codex login` is valid. `rpc_request()` in `bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex` calls `select()` on `proc.stdout` and then `readline()` on the text wrapper. The app-server sends notifications (`remoteControl/status/changed`, `account/updated`) around the same time as replies. When a notification and a reply end up in the same read, `readline()` pulls both into Python's buffer and returns only the first line. `select()` can't see lines that are already buffered, so the reply sits there until the deadline and the collector raises `TimeoutError`. ## Relationship to #13733 #13733 asks for `account/rateLimits/read` first and makes `account/read` a fallback, which avoids the most common failure. It keeps the buffered reader, though, so the same race can still cost the limits. With a notification in the same write as the rate-limits reply, `quattro` fails with `account/rateLimits/read`. This may also be why `account/read` looked like it never answered. With the reader below, a live probe here (codex-cli 0.157.1) got the `account/read` reply in about 0.46s. pr.title: Keep other systems' boot entries through a factory reset
pr.body: Fixes #13689. On a machine whose ESP is shared with other systems, a factory reset removed their Limine entries twice: once while staging (`omarchy-system-factory-reset`), and again on the first boot after it (`omarchy-provision-owner`). pr.title: Re-probe night light after each minute so the bar follows hyprsunset's schedule
pr.body: Fixes #8286. The night light service asks hyprsunset for its temperature once at startup and again after an Omarchy toggle, but hyprsunset also switches on its own: the stock `hyprsunset.conf` profiles at 07:00 and 20:00. Nothing tells the shell about those, so the indicator keeps the state it last saw. On my laptop the shell started in the afternoon, the 20:00 profile applied while the lid was shut, and the bar showed night light off all evening under a 4000K screen. In the morning it goes the other way, and clicking the indicator then toggles to the side the screen is already on. hyprsunset has no change events (its socket only answers requests), so the service has to ask. It now probes again a second past every wall-clock minute. hyprsunset lands scheduled switches exactly on the minute, so the bar follows within about a second. A switch due while suspended applies within a minute of wake, and the next probe catches it. pr.title: Stamp new migrations with wall-clock time
pr.body: ## Why `omarchy-dev-add-migration` named files after `git log -1 --format=%cd --date=unix`. Every branch cut from the same commit therefore received the same migration id. The runner records that id as done, so a later migration with the colliding name never runs. Reported in #13516 (observed collision on `1789095456` from the quattro merge of #11263). ## What Use wall-clock `date +%s` instead of HEAD's committer date. Claim the path with `noclobber` / O_EXCL create and bump the id until the create succeeds, so concurrent runs in one checkout cannot mint the same file. Does not rewrite existing migrations. Merge-time uniqueness against history is still a useful follow-up; this only stops the helper from minting the same id on sibling branches (and tightens same-tree races). ## Test ``` bash test/shell.d/dev-add-migration-test.sh bash test/shell.d/dev-add-migration-race-test.sh ``` Note: #13656 targets the same helper lines (with a test). Happy to coordinate / close if maintainers prefer that PR. Refs #13516

pr.title: Widen the network panel with a raised body-small font
pr.body: Fixes #13572. The network panel's stat grid puts two label and value pairs per row (Ping / Packet Loss, Receiving / Sending, Downloaded / Uploaded, IP Address / Gateway) in `Style.font.bodySmall`, inside a fixed `Style.space(380)`. Spacing scales with the base font size, but not with a `[font] body-small` override. So raising `body-small` on its own squeezes the value columns until the values paint over their labels ("Downloade20.04 GB", "Gatewa192.168.50.1"), and the "Cloudflare" DNS button overflows too. The panel now scales its design width by `body-small` over its default (`Style.fontPx(0.917)`, the same expression `Style.qml` uses for the token): - **Default fonts:** the factor is 1, so the layout is pixel-identical to today (378 px wide). - **Raised `body-small`:** the panel grows proportionally, still capped by `fittedContentWidth` to the space on screen. - **Stable width:** it depends only on the font settings, not on the text, so it doesn't jitter as the transfer rates change. ## Alternatives I tried - **Elide values (the issue's suggestion):** at the stock width, the IP and gateway are already tight, so eliding truncated them to `192.168.50…` for everyone on default fonts

So `defaultBarLoader` builds the stock `Bar` on every start, and destroys it as soon as the scan finds the replacement. Any `injectProps()` calls it had queued then run against the destroyed object: the `pluginBarApiFor is not a function` TypeErrors in the issue. ## Change - `PluginRegistry` gains `scannedOnce`, set when the first scan finishes. `scanning` can't be used for this, since it's already false before the first scan starts. - `defaultBarLoader` activates when the stock bar is the configured bar (unchanged, immediate), or once the first scan is done. pr.title: Support double-press actions in Hyprland bindings
pr.body: Adds optional double-press actions to `o.bind` and `o.rebind`, allowing two actions on one shortcut without custom timer logic. ```lua o.rebind("SUPER + K", "My shortcut", "single-command", { double_press = "double-command", timeout = 250, }) ``` The first press waits 250 ms by default. A second press within that window cancels the pending action and schedules `double_press` through a 1 ms one-shot timer. Dispatching outside the key event prevents global shortcuts from re-entering the binding on key release. Both actions accept the same commands, helpers, Lua functions, and dispatchers as ordinary bindings. Pending actions check that their binding is still enabled before running. The keybindings menu resolves timed shortcuts to their single action; arbitrary Lua callbacks require command metadata, as with ordinary bindings. Existing default shortcuts are unchanged. Menu metadata uses weak callback keys so it does not keep removed callbacks alive. ### Testing Added coverage for timing boundaries, cancellation, triple presses, binding lifecycle, supported action types, callback collection, release-event re-entry, cancellation of deferred double actions, and resolving timed shortcuts

pr.body: cc @AFOliveira @ryanrhughes `omarchy-sudo-keepalive` (sourced by `omarchy-pkg-install` / `omarchy-pkg-aur-install`) refreshed the cached sudo credential with `while true` and only `kill`ed the loop on `EXIT`. pr.title: Read the thumbnail index once in the direct image scan
pr.body: `shell/plugins/image-picker/list.sh` looks up each scanned image's thumbnail hash with its own `awk` scan of `~/.cache/omarchy/image-selector/index.tsv`, from the top of the file, exiting on the first matching row. `omarchy-menu-images` appends a row for every new `(path, size:mtime)` pair and nothing in the repo prunes them, so the index only grows. Scanning a directory of d images against e accumulated rows costs d awk spawns and d times e row comparisons, on every open of a direct picker, and the direct scan has no rows cache to skip any of it. The same lookup in `omarchy-menu-images` is being batched in #8884 and #12248. This gives the direct scan the same shape: one pass loads the index into an associative array before the scan loops, and each lookup becomes a hash read. pr.title: Move the parked overlay to the focused monitor before it is shown
pr.body: Fixes #13562. Since #13419, `OverlayWindow` parks its surface between opens and moved it to the focused monitor inside `onShownChanged`, the same step that shows it. pr.title: Compute image picker filter positions in one pass
pr.body: The filterable image picker gives every carousel slide a `relativeIndex` binding, and that binding calls `filteredPosition(index)`, which rescans every earlier entry with `itemMatches` to count the matches in front of it. QML bindings track every property a call reads, so one keystroke re-runs the binding for every delegate at once. Each of p slides rescans up to p earlier entries, re-running the name and label regexes at every step, and a selection move pays the same again through the selected position read in the same binding. That is quadratic work per keystroke on the compositor's UI thread. It is harmless at the theme picker's size today, around two dozen slides, but the picker is built to take a directory of any size, and a filterable picker over a large wallpaper library would turn each keystroke into millions of regex runs. `filteredPositions(images, filterText)` now builds every entry's position among the matches in one pass whenever the images or the filter change, and each delegate reads its position from that array in constant time. pr.title: Let apps opt out of the universal clipboard's Ctrl translation
pr.body: Refs #13515. Omarchy's universal clipboard bindings turn Super+A/C/V/X into Ctrl chords. That's right for most apps, but not for one that binds the Super chords itself: in an Emacs config with its own Super bindings, `Ctrl+C` is a command prefix and `Ctrl+V` pages down, so the translation fires the wrong command. The issue asks for a per-window pass-through, and this PR adds one. ## Change - `clipboard.lua` now checks tags through a generic `active_window_has_tag()` helper. When the focused window carries `native-super-clipboard`, the universal shortcut sends the Super chord itself through the same `send_key_state` path. - Super+A and Super+X also go through `universal_clipboard_shortcut`, so an opted-in app gets all four chords. They still send Ctrl+A/X everywhere else. - **No app is tagged by default.** Stock GNU Emacs and Doom bind `s-a/c/v/x` only on macOS, as a community review pointed out, so tagging Emacs by default would leave those chords unbound for most Linux Emacs users. Users opt in with one line in `~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua`, documented on the clipboard manual page: ```lua o.window("(emacs|Emacs)", { tag = "+native-super-clipboard" }) ``` ## Testing - `hyprland-def

pr.title: Route fcitx5 D-Bus activation through omarchy-fcitx5.service
pr.body: The fcitx5 package ships `/usr/share/dbus-1/services/org.fcitx.Fcitx5.service`. When any client asks for `org.fcitx.Fcitx5` while `omarchy-fcitx5.service` is between restarts, dbus-broker spawns a bare fcitx5 outside the unit. The unit's instance then finds the name taken, exits 0, and `Restart=always` loops it every ~2s for the rest of the session. This ships an activation file at `/usr/local/share/dbus-1/services/org.fcitx.Fcitx5.service` with `SystemdService=omarchy-fcitx5.service`. `/usr/local/share` precedes `/usr/share` in the session's `XDG_DATA_DIRS` (Omarchy already ships `wayland-sessions` there), so activation starts the unit instead of a second fcitx5. A migration reloads the bus config and hands a session that is already looping back to the unit; a healthy unit is left alone. Needs the matching omarchy-settings PKGBUILD change: omacom/omarchy-pkgs#704 ## Testing Fresh Omarchy 4.0.4 install, fcitx5 5.1.22, dbus-broker 37. pr.title: Offer the reboot after a channel switch
pr.body: Fixes #13416 `omarchy-channel-set` hands off to `omarchy update -y`. `-y` skips the "Ready to update?" question but also sets `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED`, and `confirm_reboot` in `omarchy-update-restart` then prints "Run omarchy-system-reboot when ready." instead of offering the reboot. A channel switch runs in a terminal someone is watching and usually replaces the kernel, so the reboot choice was lost exactly when it mattered. This adds `omarchy update --confirmed`, which skips only the update question for a caller that already asked it, and uses it in the channel switch. `-y` is unchanged for scripts and agents. An older packaged `omarchy-update` reached through a downgrade just ignores the flag and asks the question once more. ## Difference from #13444 #13444 makes the same change with a `--skip-confirm` flag. This one adds tests that pin the behavior down: `--confirmed` runs every step without the confirmation and without marking the update unattended (so the reboot offer runs), and the channel switch hands off with `--confirmed` on every channel. ## Test plan - `bash test/shell.d/update-sequence-test.sh`: new check that `--confirmed` skips `omarchy-update-confirm` and leaves

pr.title: Back off Bluetooth discovery retries while the adapter refuses them
pr.body: Fixes #13447 With the Bluetooth panel open, a `StartDiscovery` the adapter rejected was retried every second for as long as the panel stayed open. A busy or wedged controller got a request a second for minutes, and in #13447 lost its A2DP link until a power cycle. The retry delay now doubles after each unanswered attempt (1s, 2s, 4s … up to 30s) and retrying stops after eight attempts, about two minutes. Each time discovery starts or the panel reopens, retries begin at one second again, so an adapter that is still powering up is picked up as quickly as before. The schedule lives in `Model.js` so it can be tested directly. ## Difference from #13466 #13466 takes the same approach in `Panel.qml` (1s → 8s, stop after five attempts, about 15 seconds). This one keeps trying for about two minutes before giving up, so an adapter that needs longer to recover is still found while the panel is open, and it adds tests for the schedule and the stop. ## Test plan - `bash test/shell.d/bluetooth-test.sh`: new checks for the backoff schedule (1s doubling to a 30s ceiling), the retry limit, that the timer paces by attempts and resets when discovery is needed again, and that it stops asking at the li

pr.title: Finish fingerprint setup when a print is already enrolled
pr.body: Fixes #13433 `fprintd-enroll` refuses a finger that is already enrolled (`enroll-duplicate`), and PAM was only configured from the enroll-success branch. So re-running `omarchy setup security fingerprint` after an earlier run left a print behind always stopped at "Enrollment failed": the print existed but could never be used for sudo, polkit or the lock screen. Setup now checks `fprintd-list` first and, when a print exists, skips enrollment and goes straight to verify and PAM. If that existing print then fails verification, it says how to start over (`fprintd-delete $USER`, then rerun setup) instead of suggesting another enroll that would be skipped again. ## Difference from #13467 #13467 fixes the same issue, but detects an enrolled print with `grep -Eq 'has [0-9]+ fingerprints? enrolled'`. `fprintd-list` never prints that. pr.title: Hibernate laptops on critical battery once hibernation is set up
pr.body: Fixes #13256 UPower's `Auto` critical action resolves to logind's `Sleep()`, which is suspend-then-hibernate, and fires at 2%. A laptop can drain in the suspend before the hibernate runs and power off hard, even with hibernation set up. When `omarchy-hibernation-setup` runs on a machine with a battery, it now installs a UPower drop-in (`/etc/UPower/UPower.conf.d/70-omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf`) that hibernates directly at 5%, with critical at 8%. Rerunning setup adds it to machines set up before, and `omarchy-hibernation-remove` takes it out. Machines without a battery get nothing. If hibernate isn't available, UPower falls back to a clean power off. ## Test plan - `bash test/shell.d/hibernation-critical-battery-test.sh` (new): runs setup and remove against a scratch root (`/etc` and `/swap` redirected, sudo stubbed) and checks the drop-in is installed on a laptop, left alone when unchanged, not installed without a battery, and removed with hibernation. pr.title: omarchy-refresh-config shouldn't override symlinked file content
pr.body: When a file under `~/.config` is a symlink — a dotfile managed by GNU stow, say — `omarchy-refresh-config` writes the Omarchy default through the link. `cp -f` follows the destination, so the user's own file at the link target is overwritten, and the backup it saves is a copy of that file's content rather than the link. The user's `.bak` does hold their old content, but the dotfile they manage elsewhere has been clobbered without being told. This carries @J3rome's fix across to `quattro`: - The backup is taken with `cp -d`, so a symlinked config is backed up as the symlink. - A symlinked config is replaced with `cp --remove-destination`, so the link is swapped for a regular file holding the default and its target is left alone. - A regular config is still overwritten in place with `cp -f`, as on `quattro` today, so it keeps its mode and any hard links. Recreating every file would have turned a `0600` config into a `0644` one. - The comparison runs first and nothing is backed up or copied when the config already matches the default; `cmp` follows symlinks, so a link to identical content is left as a link. `test/shell.d/refresh-config-test.sh` now covers a stowed config (target untou

pr.title: Join a self-hosted Tailscale coordination server
pr.body: `sudo tailscale up --accept-routes` always joins Tailscale's hosted coordination server. On Headscale it prints a `login.tailscale.com` URL and waits, so the installer looks hung. The web app is also hardcoded to the hosted admin console. Nothing changes when the new variables are unset. - `OMARCHY_TAILSCALE_LOGIN_SERVER` must be an http(s) URL. It is passed as `--login-server`, and the hosted admin web app is skipped. - `OMARCHY_TAILSCALE_AUTH_KEY` is passed as `--auth-key` and is not printed. A value containing whitespace is rejected. - `OMARCHY_TAILSCALE_ADMIN_URL` installs a web app at that address when the coordination server has one. A bad URL or auth key exits before `omarchy-pkg-add` and before `tailscale up`. There is no prompt, so a scripted install does not block on stdin. The menu install still uses the hosted server unless those variables are in the environment. The same script is on `omarchy-mac`. This is the upstream copy. pr.title: Rotate the laptop display with the accelerometer on convertibles
pr.body: Convertibles and detachables report an orientation, but nothing acted on it, so the built-in panel stayed in landscape however the device was held. This adds `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-autorotate`, started from the default autostart, which follows the accelerometer through `iio-sensor-proxy` and sets the panel's transform to match. The daemon holds a `monitor-sensor` claim and reads orientations from its output, since `iio-sensor-proxy` only powers the sensor while a client holds a claim on its D-Bus connection. The claim is supervised: if `monitor-sensor` exits, the orientation would otherwise freeze at its last value, which looks exactly like a screen that has quietly stopped rotating. The transform is written together with the panel's live scale, because a monitor rule replaces the one that matched before it and a transform-only rule drops the scale. Rotation is re-applied on `configreloaded` rather than persisted, so it never fights `monitors.lua`. External monitors are never rotated. `omarchy-toggle-autorotate` is a rotation lock: the panel stays where it is, and turning rotation back on catches up with the device. pr.title: Activate zram swap after package updates
pr.body: `omarchy-settings` ships `/usr/lib/systemd/zram-generator.conf.d/90-omarchy.conf`, but nothing depends on `zram-generator`, so installs that never received the package run without zram swap (#7522). Adding the package is not enough by itself: once `swap.target` is already active, installing the generator produces `dev-zram0.swap` without starting it, so the machine stays without zram until the next boot. Migration `1787520405` installs `zram-generator` when it is missing, and starts `dev-zram0.swap` when it is not already active. If reloading systemd or starting the unit fails, it falls back to `reboot-required`, the same way `1784961000` does. An active swap device is left alone, so a second user on a repaired machine does nothing. A failed package install exits non-zero and leaves the migration pending for the next run. `test/shell.d/zram-activation-migration-test.sh` covers these paths against stubs, and the acceptance suite now asserts that `/dev/zram0` is active swap on a fresh install. pr.title: Wake from the screensaver on a lone modifier tap
pr.body: ## What A lone tap of Shift, Ctrl, Alt or Super (either side) now dismisses the screensaver, the way it does on macOS and Windows. Hyprland matches these binds when the key is released. ## Why `omarchy-screensaver` exits when a character reaches its terminal (`read -n1`) or focus leaves the window. A modifier key sends no character, so tapping Shift does nothing. The keys that do work are character keys, and the wake keystroke is easy to have land in whatever window takes focus next, so a Space or Enter meant to wake the screen ends up typed into an editor or chat box. Modifiers never produce a character, which makes them the wake keys that cannot leak. ## How `default/hypr/bindings/screensaver.lua` binds both sides of each modifier, non-consuming, to a Lua function that looks up windows of class `org.omarchy.screensaver` and closes each through the window close dispatcher, `hl.dsp.window.close({ window = window })`. pr.title: Fix menu JSONC inline comment tails emptying the whole menu
pr.body: Fixes #13493. Stacked on #13255: this branch builds on its head because the fix extends the same string-aware scanner. Whichever lands second is a small rebase over `stripJsonc`. The comment regex in `stripJsonc` is anchored to line starts (`^\s*\/\/`), so it only strips comments that occupy a whole line. An inline tail after the closing brace — `{"a": {...}} // note` — survives into `JSON.parse`, which rejects it, and the `catch` in `parseMenuJsonc` silently returns an empty item set: one stray comment empties the entire menu. **Fix.** Comment stripping is folded into the string-aware scanner: outside any string, `//` drops everything through the end of the line wherever the opener sits; slashes inside a string literal (`"A // B"`) are still copied verbatim. Verified live, before/after on the real files, narrated (67s): Repro: ```js parseMenuJsonc('{"a": {"label": "A"}} // note') // stock: [] — the whole menu is gone ``` **Checks** | Input | Stock | This PR | |---|---|---| | `{"a": {...}} // note` inline tail | `[]` — menu empties | 1 entry ✓ | | no comments | parses ✓ | parses ✓ | | full-line `//` comments | stripped ✓ | stripped ✓ | | `"A // B"` inside a string | preserved ✓ | p

pr.title: Fix menu JSONC top-level array rendering phantom rows

pr.title: Keep Foot's font size when changing the font
pr.body: Fixes #6957. ## What was wrong `omarchy-font-set` rewrote Foot's whole `font=` line with a fixed `size=9`: ```bash sed -i "s/^font=.*/font=$font_name:size=9/g" ~/.config/foot/foot.ini ``` So after `omarchy display text size 16` (Foot at 12pt), picking a new font put Foot back at 9pt while Alacritty, Kitty, and Ghostty stayed at 12. On a scale-1 screen that leaves the terminal text at 12px next to a 16px bar. ## Fix Replace only the family, the way the other three terminals already do: ```bash sed -i -E "s/^font=[^:,]*/font=$font_name/" ~/.config/foot/foot.ini ``` `font=Old Font:size=12` becomes `font=New Font:size=12`. pr.title: Fix: omarchy plugin clone can generate a colliding plugin id
pr.body: ## Problem `omarchy plugin clone <builtin>` derives the new clone's id from `$USER` as roughly `<username>.<plugin>`. When the username matches the namespace of a built-in plugin, the generated id collides with the built-in itself. Concrete case — the stock Omarchy VM's default username is literally `omarchy`, so: ``` omarchy plugin clone omarchy.weather ``` generates the clone id `omarchy.weather` — the **same id as the built-in weather plugin**. The clone can't be distinguished from what it was cloned from. This is not hypothetical: any user cloning an `omarchy.*` built-in on a stock install hits it. ## Fix After computing the candidate id, check it against every id in `omarchy-plugin-catalog` (built-in **or** already-cloned) and against any existing plugin directory, and suffix a counter until the id is free. The directory-existence guard is folded into the same check so a clone never clobbers an existing one. - Normal usernames are unaffected (`baron.weather`, etc.). - The collision case now yields `omarchy.weather2` instead of shadowing the built-in. ## Testing ``` # as user "omarchy": omarchy plugin clone omarchy.weather # -> clone id omarchy.weather2 (was: omarchy.weather) #

pr.title: Keep the shell supervisor attached after a locked Hyprland restart
pr.body: ## Problem A Hyprland crash while the screen is locked comes back from `start-hyprland` as `--safe-mode --locked`. Two things then leave the seat stranded: - `omarchy-launch-shell` keeps the crashed process's `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE`. `hyprctl monitors` follows that dead socket and fails, so `compositor_alive` exits the supervisor with no log and Quickshell is never started again. Safe mode does not run `hyprland.start`, so nothing else starts it. - `misc:allow_session_lock_restore` lives in `looknfeel.lua`, which safe mode does not load. A later lock request against the stranded session is a fatal Wayland error (`invalid object`) and Quickshell dies instead of drawing the unlock screen. ## Change `omarchy-launch-shell` now adopts whichever instance `hyprctl instances` can still talk to, including that instance's Wayland socket, before each Quickshell launch and before deciding the compositor is gone. The watchdog restart gets a few seconds to answer. When that instance is already locked, the supervisor enables `allow_session_lock_restore` before Quickshell connects. pr.title: Add recursion guard to omarchy-mise-install wrappers
pr.body: ## Summary When a tool is not installed or mise fails to provide the requested binary, `mise x <tool> -- <bin>` falls back to searching `PATH`. Because the wrapper itself is installed in `~/.local/bin`, mise re-executes the wrapper script. Without a recursion guard, this creates an unbounded fork loop (~1,000 forks/sec) that saturates the machine until it exhausts process limits. This emits a tool-specific environment guard variable (`_OMARCHY_MISE_GUARD_<COMMAND>`) at the top of the generated wrapper so recursive invocations fail fast with exit code 127 and a clear stderr message instead of hanging the machine. Fixes #13177 ## Testing - Updated `test/shell.d/mise-install-test.sh` with a test simulating `mise x` falling back to `PATH` when an executable is missing. - Verified that the wrapper catches the recursion, writes the error to stderr, and exits 127. - Ran `bash test/shell.d/mise-install-test.sh` (all 5 assertions passed).

pr.title: Document the hardware clock convention for dual boot
pr.body: ## Summary On a dual-boot machine, Windows keeps the hardware clock in local time while Linux reads it as UTC. After a Windows session Omarchy briefly comes up with a clock skewed by the UTC offset until NTP corrects it — and a snapshot taken in that window (e.g. the pre-update one from `omarchy update`) carries a future timestamp, so limine-snapper-sync adds no Limine menu entry for later snapshots until real time passes it (#13367). The upstream sync-side report is linked in the issue. This closes the issue's documentation option: the dual-boot manual said nothing about the clock, so it now explains the mismatch, the snapshot-menu symptom, and both conventions — making Windows read UTC (`RealTimeIsUniversal`, recommended) or making Linux read local time (`timedatectl set-local-rtc 1`) — with a `timedatectl` verification step. Fixes #13367 ## Testing Docs-only change; no test surface. Verified against the issue's reproduction description and `timedatectl`'s own output labels.

pr.title: Mark the menu apps provider loaded only once rows exist
pr.body: ## Summary The Apps section of the Quickshell menu showed "Nothing here yet" permanently on some installs even though every `.desktop` entry was valid and scannable (#13202). `startProviderForMenu` set `providersLoaded["apps"] = true` before `mergeAppRows()` ran, and `mergeAppRows()` bails silently when `root.appLibrary` (`shell.appLibrary`) is not wired up yet. A summon that loses that race merges zero rows but marks the provider done, so every later retry — each summon and each search, which skip loaded providers — silently does nothing. pr.title: Close panel overlays even when a plugin close() throws
pr.body: ## Summary `Ui/KeyboardPanel.qml` and `Ui/PopupCard.qml` delegate `close()` straight to the panel owner and only set `root.open = false` when there is no owner. An owner `close()` that throws leaves the overlay mapped with its full-screen input region intact (#13382): every click on the desktop lands on the dead surface, and every dismissal path (Esc, outside-click, `omarchy-shell <target> close`, `shell hide`) funnels back into the same throwing call — only a shell restart recovers. Both now wrap the delegation in `try`/`catch`: on a throw they log a warning naming the failure and force `root.open = false`, which unmaps the window and releases the input region. The happy path is byte-for-byte unchanged. Fixes #13382 ## Testing - No existing shell.d test covers these Ui components; QML change verified for structural correctness (`id: root`/`property bool open` present in both files, `console.warn` + JS `try/catch` are standard QML). - Suggested visual/behavioral check per `agents/skills/visual-verification.md`: a dev-linked shell with a plugin whose `close()` throws `throw new Error('x')` — Esc/outside-click must now dismiss the panel and the log must show the warning.

pr.title: List submap bindings under the chord that enters their mode in the keybindings menu
pr.body: A bind scoped to a submap only fires inside its mode, but `omarchy-menu-keybindings` lists it as an always-on global chord. On my config, `SUPER + P` enters a window mode whose binds render like this: ``` ESCAPE → Leave window mode H → Shrink width J → Grow height L → Grow width SHIFT + H → Swap left ``` The `ESC` fire, but `ESCAPE → Leave window mode` reads like a shortcut I can press right now, and none of these rows say what they belong to or where they come from. Meanwhile the chord that enters the mode lists rows above, unconnected: `SUPER + P → Window mode`. ### How a submap gets there, two ways - Plain Hyprland binds: `bind = SUPER, P, submap, window` enters the mode, and every bind scoped to it arrives through `hyprctl binds` with its `submap:` field filled. - Omarchy's Lua binds: `hl.dsp.submap("window")` as the `o.bind` action. These report dispatcher `__lua`, and the menu already recovers the dispatch from the Lua bind cache, which holds the evaluated argument — so the entry bind to a mode is in there, just never used. ### Fix - Carry each bind's `submap:` field through the emit stage. - Build a map from a submap name to the chord that enters it, sourced from both roads

pr.title: Keep a legacy Windows VM password with $$ working after the Quattro migration
pr.body: Upgrading a 3.x install to Quattro moves the Windows VM's compose from `~/.config/windows/docker-compose.yml` to the root-owned one, and `migrate_legacy_compose` carries the password across by reading the raw text between the quotes. That text is what Docker Compose parsed, and Compose turns `$$` into a single `$`, so a legacy password written as `a$$b` was set in the guest as `a$b`. Migration kept `a$$b`: it saved that as the RDP password and then escaped it again for the new compose. The guest's disk is preserved, so Windows keeps `a$b`, and every RDP login after the upgrade fails. This decodes `$$` to `$` as the password is read, so both the RDP credentials and the new compose hold the password the guest actually has. A legacy password with a lone `$` (`pa$`, `a$!b`) is unchanged, as before. One whose `$` was followed by a name (`pa$word`) was already cut short by Compose when the VM was installed, and the original cannot be reconstructed, so that case stays as it is. pr.title: Show live Dropbox sync status in the bar widget
pr.body: The Dropbox widget gave no sign that anything was transferring. While Dropbox was running, the panel's subtitle rotated through placeholder phrases ("Boxing bytes", "Shuffling folders", …), and the bar icon looked the same whether Dropbox was idle or in the middle of a 10 GB upload. `status.py` already returns Dropbox's real status text, but the panel never showed it. - **Bar:** while Dropbox is syncing, indexing, uploading, downloading or connecting, the icon pulses and shows a small accent-colored dot. When everything is up to date it goes back to a steady icon. - **Panel:** the hero reads "Syncing" during transfers and shows Dropbox's own status otherwise ("Up to date"). Below the hero, the full status lines appear, e.g. `Uploading "takeout-….tgz" (1,866 KB/sec, 52 mins)`. The hero meta is uppercased and elided, so the long lines go in the detail text instead of the hero. - **Polling:** during a transfer, the widget refreshes every 3 s while the panel is open, and every 10 s otherwise to keep the dot current. When idle it uses the configured `refreshIntervalSec`. The status parsing (`statusLines`, `isSyncing`) lives in `Model.js` and is covered in `test/shell.d/dropbox-test.sh`.

pr.title: Boot the DGX Spark without a UKI until Limine is fixed
pr.body: On the DGX Spark the screen stays black for about 20 seconds after an entry is picked in Limine. The Spark firmware clears memory as it is freed, and before starting a UKI, Limine returns all the memory it claimed at startup, about 124 GB. A timed Limine build spent 20.15 s in that step ([Limine#673]( Booting the kernel and initramfs directly skips it. On the Spark, a hardware drop-in sets `ENABLE_UKI=no`, named to sort after `omarchy-uki.conf`, and a migration applies it to existing installs and rebuilds the boot entries once. Other machines are unchanged. The drop-in should be removed once Limine is fixed. This builds on #13260, which adds `omarchy-hw-dgx-spark`; only the last commit is new here. The new shell test passes. On a Spark, running the migration from this branch switched the entry to `protocol: linux` and cut Limine's time, including the 5-second menu, from 26.3 s to 6.3 s. An Omarchy update to a new kernel, booting and restoring a snapshot, and removing the drop-in (back to a UKI) all worked. #6840's boot check reads only `omarchy-uki.conf`, so it would need to honour this override.

pr.title: Wait for the shell (for its notification service) before launching autostart apps
pr.body: ## Problem `o.launch_on_start` fires on `hyprland.start`, the same event that launches the Omarchy shell, and the shell needs a few seconds before it claims `org.freedesktop.Notifications`. Every autostarted app launches while the shell is still coming up. Chromium (so every web app) and Electron apps check for a notification service once at process start and keep the answer for their whole lifetime. When they win the race they draw their own bare popup windows for the rest of the session instead of sending toasts to the shell. The symptom is "notifications are broken after every boot until I restart the browser", which is hard to connect to startup order. Reproduced on Omarchy 4.0.4 / Hyprland 0.56.2: Chromium's scope started within the first second of `hyprland.start`, a few seconds before the shell. With the wait in place the browser starts after the shell reports ready and notifications render as toasts on every boot. ## Fix - New hidden command `omarchy-launch-autostart`: `gdbus wait --session --timeout 15 org.freedesktop.Notifications`, then `exec uwsm-app -- "$@"`. pr.title: Resolve the audio output sink through EasyEffects 8
pr.body: `omarchy-audio-output-sink` follows a DSP sink to the physical sink through the DSP's playback stream. EasyEffects 8 has no such stream: its output node links its ports straight to the sink's playback ports, so the search finds nothing and the volume keys, the bar's audio panel and the output switcher all act on `easyeffects_sink` itself. That sink's volume is inert (its monitor, which EasyEffects reads, does not follow it), so the OSD moves while the speakers do not. **Fix.** Follow the port links (`pw-link -l`) to the `alsa_output` sink instead. When EasyEffects is idle it drops those links, so fall back to the output device named in its settings (`~/.config/easyeffects/db/easyeffectsrc`), if that sink exists. Filter-chain tunings keep resolving through their stream as before. **Reproduce.** `easyeffects --service-mode`, make `easyeffects_sink` the default output, press the volume keys: the OSD changes, loudness does not. pr.title: Keep UVC webcams at a fixed frame rate
pr.body: ## Problem UVC webcams commonly power up with auto-exposure priority on. In anything short of bright light the camera then stretches the exposure past the frame interval, so a camera asked for 30 fps delivers 10 or 15 while `v4l2-ctl --get-parm` still reports 30. The screen-recording overlay, OBS, mpv and Firefox all get the slow stream, and nothing in the pipeline says why. The 1 is the vendor's power-on setting; nothing in the stack decides it. Two cameras from different vendors did this in ordinary room light. To check a camera, no app involved: ``` v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video0 --get-ctrl exposure_dynamic_framerate # 1 = affected v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video0 --set-fmt-video=width=640,height=360 --set-parm=30 \ && v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video0 --stream-mmap --stream-count=120 # delivered fps in your light ``` Measured that way: | Camera | Control on | Control off | |---|---|---| | Logitech C920 (`046d:08e5`), desktop | 14.99 fps | 29.9 fps | | Dell Inspiron 3501 integrated Microdia (`0c45:671e`) | 9.99 fps in YUYV and in MJPG | 29.9 fps | In a screen recording the overlay moved every sixth frame at 60 fps with the control on and every second frame with it off, so the effect reaches the saved vid

pr.title: Encode transcode clipboard file URIs
pr.body: ## Problem `omarchy transcode` builds its clipboard URI by concatenating `file://` with an unescaped output path. The encode succeeds, but URI consumers can resolve that text to a different file: `#` becomes a fragment, `?` becomes a query, and a literal `%20` in a filename becomes a space. I reproduced this with actual ImageMagick/FFmpeg conversions and GIO's `g_file_new_for_uri()` / `g_file_get_path()`, while substituting only clipboard delivery and notifications. For example, the generated `shot#1-low.jpg` was interpreted as `shot`, and `shot%20-low.png` as `shot -low.png`. ## Change Use Python's standard-library `Path.resolve().as_uri()` when building `text/uri-list`. This retains absolute/symlink resolution and percent-encodes the path. The Python invocation uses `-I` so it does not import a `pathlib.py` from the current directory. The only production change is in `copy_to_clipboard()`. Encoder arguments, output naming, menus, and clipboard MIME type are unchanged. No migration is needed. ## Verification Base: `e1614f2bdb94f7df11eda072644b31e1e118f1ba`. Quattro replaced hypridle with the Quickshell idle service. hypridle owned `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver`; nothing does now, so D-Bus `Inhibit()` from browsers and players is dropped and the screensaver fires over playing video. ## What this does `omarchy-idle-inhibit` owns `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` (the same name hypridle owned) and exports the object paths clients actually call: - **`/org/freedesktop/ScreenSaver`** — Chromium/Chrome `power_save_blocker_linux.cc` (video / display wake lock) - **`/ScreenSaver`** — VLC, Firefox/Zen `org.freedesktop.PowerManagement` is left unowned. Chromium uses that name for audio, downloads, and WebRTC; owning it would pin the screensaver and lock for background music. Chromium skips an unowned PowerManagement name, so video still inhibits via ScreenSaver. Inhibitors are ref-counted, reaped when the caller leaves the bus, and published as JSON under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy/idle-inhibit/state` (pid-signed so a crashed daemon cannot pin idle off). pr.title: Resync the clock when the wall clock is stepped
pr.body: Close a laptop lid and open it again, and the bar clock still reads the time the lid closed at (or the previous day if suspended overnight across midnight, such as showing Friday instead of Saturday). `date` in a terminal is correct the whole time. It does correct itself — but not for up to a full minute, and most of that minute passes behind the lock screen, so what you actually see is a stale clock on the bar you unlock into. Refs #13275 — a Try Omarchy VM whose bar clock is "often incorrect, running slow and does not update for many minutes at a time". A paused or migrated VM steps the guest's wall clock the same way a suspend does, so this is a plausible fix for that report, but the issue does not mention suspend or compare the bar against `date`, so it is not referenced as closing. Supersedes #10138 (rebased on current `quattro` with documentation merge conflict resolved). ## Cause `SystemClock` computes the delay to the top of the next minute from wall-clock time and arms a `QTimer` with that relative delay (`schedule()` in Quickshell). pr.title: Show plugin update diffs without git's pager
pr.body: Reopens #12335, which closed when I deleted my fork by accident. Same one-word change, rebased on current `quattro`. Tracking issue: #12332. `omarchy plugin update <id>` prints the diff with an unpiped `git diff`, so git starts its pager whenever output goes to a terminal. The `gum confirm "Update <id>?"` that follows waits behind the pager, invisible: Enter scrolls one line inside `less`, so the update looks stuck with nothing to suggest a keypress is expected. Quitting with `q` reveals the prompt. On the `delta` path the diff is piped, which makes git skip its pager, so the prompt is already visible there. `--no-pager` gives the other path the same behaviour. ## Why this is the default path, not an edge case `git-delta` is in neither `depends` nor `optdepends` of the `omarchy` package, while `git` is. pr.body: TVs and many OLED monitors don't support DDC/CI, so on those displays the brightness keys and the Display panel slider do nothing. Follows up on #8302. When the DDC probe fails on an external display, `omarchy-brightness-display` now dims with `hyprsunset` gamma instead: - **20% minimum.** 20% is already quite low, even in a dark room. At 1% you can easily lose track of the cursor and not find your way back to the slider, and then a restart is the only way out. - **Remembers a failed probe for 60s.** On my LG TV, every failed DDC probe takes about 4 seconds (`detect` finds an I2C bus, then `getvcp` times out). Without this, each key press and each panel refresh would stall. - **Starts hyprsunset if it isn't running**, the same way the nightlight toggle does. - **No change** for internal panels, Apple displays, or monitors where DDC works. pr.title: pkg: Add interactive prompt to run omarchy update when package install fails
pr.body: ### Motivation When trying to install a package using `omarchy pkg add`, the underlying `pacman -S` command often fails with 404 Not Found errors if their local package databases are out of date. ### Changes This updates `bin/omarchy-pkg-add` to catch installation failures. Instead of doing a risky partial upgrade (`pacman -Sy`) or forcing a heavy automatic system upgrade on every install, this PR: 1. Detects if the terminal is interactive (`-t 0`). 2. If interactive, prompts the user to safely run a full `omarchy update` and then retries the installation. 3. If non-interactive, falls back to printing a helpful error message instructing the user to run `omarchy update`.

pr.title: Enable Sunshine by its real unit name
pr.body: ## Problem `omarchy install service sunshine` fails on a fresh install with: ``` Failed to enable unit: Unit sunshine.service does not exist ``` The current `sunshine` package (2026.516.143833) ships its user unit as `app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service`. The unit declares `Alias=sunshine.service`, but systemd only creates alias symlinks when the unit is enabled, so `systemctl --user enable --now sunshine` can't resolve the name on a machine where it has never been enabled. Because the installer runs under `set -e`, it exits there and never opens the ufw ports, installs the Sunshine Admin webapp or sets up autostart. ## Fix Refer to the unit by its real name in both the install and remove scripts. ## Testing Reproduced on Omarchy 4.0.4 (Intel NUC6i7KYK). Running `systemctl --user enable --now app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service` enables and starts the unit. Note that once the unit is enabled, re-running the current installer still fails, now with `Failed to enable unit: Refusing to operate on linked unit file sunshine.service`, because systemd won't enable a unit through its alias symlink. pr.title: Fix BCM4350 Bluetooth coexistence on MacBookPro14,1
pr.body: Fixes #13297. On MacBookPro14,1, BCM4350's default hybrid coexistence policy interrupts A2DP audio while 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi is connected. Switching to parallel mode restored steady tones and music, including a concurrent Wi-Fi download; restoring hybrid mode reproduced the failure. The issue and [hardware measurements]( document the comparison. Add one NetworkManager dispatcher scoped to MacBookPro14,1, BCM4350 rev 5 (`14e4:43a3`), and firmware `7.35.180.133` / `01-c45b39d6`. It changes default mode 5 to mode 4 on 2.4 GHz and restores only its owned override when disconnected or on another band. Ownership records the interface's `ifindex`, so a stale marker cannot authorize restoration after re-registration. Different firmware and nondefault policies are preserved. Repeated events with mode 4 active send no additional firmware write; irrelevant events exit before Python. A boot-only command would miss later firmware reloads, while leaving mode 4 enabled on every band broadens the tested policy. The existing `omarchy-settings` recipe ships the executable directly from `etc/`, so package updates maintain or retire it and new/existing installs pick it up at their next network activation. N

pr.title: Install OpenClaw as a self-updating copy under ~/.openclaw
pr.body: OpenClaw could not update itself on any machine that installed it through Omarchy. The `openclaw` package put it in `/usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw`, owned by root and by pacman, and upstream's updater refuses that install: `openclaw update` stops with `global-install-foreign-destination` or `EACCES`, and the Control UI's _Update Gateway_ fails with `EACCES: permission denied, mkdtemp '/usr/lib/node_modules/.openclaw.update-stage-…'`, which is why the manual told people not to press it. Choosing OpenClaw under _Setup > Default Agent_ and installing it under _Install > AI_ both led there. Both paths now set up the OpenClaw that upstream's own `install-cli.sh` makes: a private Node and the package in `~/.openclaw`, owned by the user, which `openclaw update` and the Control UI replace in place before restarting the gateway on the new version. pr.title: Fix battery status reading a phantom BAT device on dual-bay ThinkPads
pr.body: ## Summary - `omarchy-battery-status` always took the first `upower -e` device listed, unconditionally. On a ThinkPad T480 this is `BAT0`, a phantom device for the unpopulated second battery bay: `present: yes` but `energy-full: 0 Wh`, no model/manufacturer, `technology: Unknown`. The real, physically installed battery is `BAT1`. The status bar/notifications therefore always showed `0% / not charging` even while the real battery was actively charging fine on AC. - Fixed by preferring the first candidate whose `energy-full` is a real, nonzero number, instead of blindly taking whatever `upower -e` lists first. This doesn't change behavior on a genuinely dual-real-battery machine — this script has never aggregated two real batteries, only ever reported a single device's data. - Two other spots had the same underlying bug independently: the `cycle_count` and `charge_control_*_threshold` sysfs fallbacks re-globbed `BAT*` and took the first match via `head -1`, so they could read the phantom device's values even after the primary fix. pr.body: A brightness key press currently spends about sixteen processes: | | | |---|---| | monitor name | `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-focused` (bash + `hyprctl` + `jq`) | | is it an Apple display | `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-focused-apple` (bash + `hyprctl` + `jq`) | | which device | `omarchy-hw-display` (bash) | | read | `brightnessctl` + `awk` | | write | `brightnessctl` | | read again, for the OSD | `brightnessctl` + `awk` | | OSD | `omarchy-osd` (bash + `jq`) + `omarchy-shell` (bash + `timeout` + `qs`) | `default/hypr/bindings/media.lua` marks those bindings `repeating = true`, so it happens several times a second while the key is held down. pr.title: fix(keybindings): keep the Lua bind scan alive past qconsole.lua
pr.body: ## Problem Bindings declared in a user's `~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua` lose their dispatcher and argument, so the keybindings menu can render them but never dispatch them. Because Hyprland's Lua config reports every bind as `dispatcher=__lua` with an opaque argument, `omarchy-menu-keybindings` reconstructs the real dispatcher by re-running the config in Lua against a stub (`build_lua_bind_cache`). That scan dies partway through: ``` $ DEBUG=1 omarchy menu keybindings --print [DEBUG] lua bind scan failed: /usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/qconsole.lua:123: attempt to compare number with table ``` `qconsole.lua:97` evaluates `mon.scale > 0`, and the stub answers `hl.get_active_monitor()` with a table that has no `__lt` and no arithmetic metamethods. The load is wrapped in a bare `pcall` (`:234`) that only reports when `DEBUG=1`, so nothing surfaces in normal use.
