pr.title: Draft: bound the hotspot to a participant limit
pr.body: ## Summary Draft follow-up to #7435. Adds an optional participant limit to the hotspot, built on the safety fixes now on `hotspot-panel` (`548bde94`). NetworkManager already owns a shared connection's DHCP pool, so the limit is a `ipv4.shared-dhcp-range` that hands out exactly N leases — a device past the last one still associates but never gets an address. `status` reports the count the profile carries, and `apply` takes an optional limit that is set, changed, or cleared deliberately. - Omitting the limit leaves the profile's range alone, which is what `start` must do, so starting the hotspot can never quietly clear a limit the user set. - A changed range only reaches a running dnsmasq on a restart, so a live AP is bounced instead of reporting a limit the current clients are not subject to. - A non-`/24` hotspot subnet is refused rather than reinterpreted. - The panel shows the limit as a pill next to the band selector, always passes it explicitly, and marks a full hotspot in the status line, so the next client failing to get an address is not a surprise. - A malformed status reads as unlimited, so a bad poll cannot invent a cap. ## Also fixed here The band-selector delegate never

pr.title: Explain that the empty monitor rule applies to every display
pr.body: An empty `output` in `hl.monitor` is the fallback for every monitor that has no rule of its own. The shipped rule uses `mode = "preferred"`, which is what keeps each display at its native mode. Replacing `preferred` with a fixed mode — typically to pin the laptop panel — applies that mode to external monitors as well, so they run below their native resolution. Naming the output and leaving the fallback at `preferred` restores it. Confirmed on a laptop plus an external display: the external output switched from the internal panel's mode to the first mode in its own list. The note lives where that rule is edited: the config comment, the monitors chapter of the manual, and the Hyprland skill.

pr.title: Retry bt-agent after bluetooth.service instead of skipping
pr.body: ## Problem `bt-agent.service` used `ExecCondition=systemctl is-active bluetooth.service`. When that condition fails, systemd **skips** the unit. A skip is terminal for that activation — `Restart=on-failure` does not try again — so a race with bluez at login (or after `systemctl restart bluetooth`) leaves the session with **no pairing agent**. The radio still scans; pairing never completes. Reported in #13247 with journal evidence (`Skipped due to 'exec-condition'` until bluetoothd is already up). ## Change - Wait for `bluetooth.service` **inside `ExecStart`**, then `exec bt-agent`, so a late bluez is no longer a terminal skip and the Type=simple start job does not hold `graphical-session.target`. - Add `After=graphical-session.target` (same pattern as migrate-notify) so the unit cannot pin the session target open. - Do **not** add user-manager `After=`/`Wants=` on system `bluetooth.service` (those deps are inert in the user manager). - Keep `ConditionPathIsDirectory=/sys/class/bluetooth` so machines with no Bluetooth class still skip cleanly. - Update `systemd-test.sh` with directive-anchored assertions for the wait + ordering. ## Test - `ROOT=... bash test/shell.d/systemd-test.sh`

pr.title: Force DPMS enable on system wake when status is stale
pr.body: ## What `omarchy-brightness-display on` skips the DPMS enable when every enabled monitor already reports `dpmsStatus=true`. That avoids an extra modeset flash on the lock screen, but on NVIDIA s2idle resume Hyprland can report that status while the panel is still dark, so the skip leaves the laptop black until a hard reboot. `--force` bypasses the guard. `omarchy-system-wake` uses it (lock-screen input, auth, cancelled idle — not a dedicated resume hook). Plain `on` still trusts the status. Refs #13251. ## Limits / follow-up Hyprland `setDPMS(true)` early-returns when `m_dpmsStatus` is already on, so a lone forced enable may not re-light a panel that is dark while status is stale. If hardware still needs recovery, next step is compare enable-only vs disable→enable on the affected laptop and hook a real resume signal if an off/on cycle is required. ## Test - `test/shell.d/brightness-display-test.sh`: plain `on` skips when status is lit; plain `on` dispatches when status is dark; `--force on` still dispatches when status is lit (via `run_brightness --no-osd`). - `test/shell.d/monitor-recovery-test.sh`: wake calls `--force on`.

pr.title: Fix menu JSONC trailing-comma stripping corrupting string values
pr.body: Fixes #13250. `stripJsonc` removes trailing commas with a string-blind regex (`/,(\s*[}\]])/g`), so a label containing comma + whitespace + `]` or `}` (e.g. `"x, ]y"`) is silently rewritten to `"x ]y"`. The result stays valid JSON, so parsing succeeds and the corruption is invisible — the user just sees a label that isn't what they wrote. **Fix.** Replace the regex with a small string-aware scanner: a comma inside a string literal is copied verbatim (handling `\"` escapes); a comma outside any string is dropped only when the next non-whitespace character is `}` or `]`. Comment stripping is untouched — #6525 reworks it separately, and the two changes compose (whichever lands second is a one-function rebase). Verified live, before/after on the real files, narrated (50s): **Checks (run against this branch's file and the stock quattro file, same script):** | # | Case | Stock | This PR | |---|------|-------|---------| | 1 | Label `"x, ]y"` | `"x ]y"` — corrupted | `"x, ]y"` ✓ preserved | | 2 | `{"c": {"label": "y"},}` trailing comma | parses ✓ | parses ✓ | | 3 | Trailing comma inside `aliases` array | parses ✓ | parses ✓ | | 4 | Escaped-quote label `a\", ]b` | corrupted | preserved ✓ |

pr.title: Group audio outputs and label same-named AirPlay speakers
pr.body: With PipeWire's AirPlay discovery loaded (`pipewire-zeroconf` + `libpipewire-module-raop-discover`), every AirPlay receiver on the network becomes an output. On a home network that is easily a dozen or more rows in the audio panel, mixed in with the monitor, the headphones and the onboard card, and in whatever order mDNS happened to answer. This groups the output list: - **DIRECT**: ALSA and Bluetooth outputs, in their existing order - **AIRPLAY**: RAOP sinks, sorted by name - **OTHER**: anything else, such as a speaker tuning or EasyEffects Headings are only drawn when more than one group is present, so a machine without AirPlay discovery looks exactly as it does today. They are labels, not cursor stops: the list is sorted before it reaches the Repeater, so `selectedIndex` still means "row N as drawn" and keyboard navigation is unchanged. It also tells apart AirPlay speakers that share a name. A house commonly has a "Kitchen" HomePod mini and a "Kitchen" amplifier. pr.title: Invalidate image row cache when a file is edited in place
pr.body: Fixes #11806. The image selector cache keyed its fast signature on directory mtime alone, so editing an image in place (which never touches the directory) left a stale thumbnail on a cache hit forever. The fast signature now includes each file's size and mtime. Verified via a full cache round-trip: an in-place edit invalidates the row cache even when the directory mtime is held byte-identical, and an unchanged tree still hits the cache.

pr.title: Stop mise-install from clobbering a user's own wrapper
pr.body: Fixes #7101. omarchy-mise-install removed ~/.local/bin/<command> unconditionally before writing its shim. For a user's own wrapper at the same path — pinning a version, or pointing the tool at a custom API base URL — that silently destroyed their setup on every update/migration. It now refuses to touch anything that is not a mise wrapper: - a symlink is always dropped (it previously wrote through it into the real binary, see #6618); - a regular file is overwritten only when it matches the current shim template or one of the older generated forms the migrations also recognize; - anything else prints a warning and exits nonzero, leaving the file alone.

pr.title: Bound speedtest transfers so hung endpoints cannot strand workers
pr.body: Fixes #10768 and #6989, #8515, #10186. omarchy-network-speedtest could hang forever: a worker blocked inside a hung curl attempt (no timeout), a dead endpoint did not kill the worker, and the whole run had no self-imposed cap, so orphaned workers survived the speedtest panel being SIGKILLed. Changes: - each transfer is wrapped in `timeout -k 1 8`, with curl `--connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15` as a backstop; - a failed attempt continues the round-robin instead of returning; - workers and the main loop both stop at ~8s, and remaining workers are cleaned up before the final wait. Verified with hung and fast-failing stubbed endpoints: runs end in ~9s and zero worker processes linger 9s after the caller is killed with SIGKILL.

pr.title: Document Lua bind dispatch and new plugin install steps in agent skill
pr.body: The agent skill under \`default/agents/skills/omarchy/\` was missing two things an agent needs to act correctly: - **hyprland.md**: it didn't say that \`hyprctl -j binds\` reports an \`o.bind(...)\` binding as dispatcher \`__lua\` with an opaque numeric handle in \`arg\`, not \`exec\` plus the command. This matters for a tool that installs its own keybindings and needs to find them again later (e.g. on reinstall): it has to match on \`description\`, not on dispatcher or command. - **plugins.md**: it covered cloning a built-in plugin, but not the steps for installing a plugin that's neither built-in nor published in git (write the folder into \`~/.config/omarchy/plugins/<id>/\`, validate, rescan, then enable), nor \`omarchy plugin add\` for a plugin published in git. This matters for a tool that installs its own plugin. Both verified on Omarchy 4.0.4-1: all 240 binds report \`__lua\`, and the plugin command syntax was checked against \`bin/omarchy-plugin-validate\`, \`bin/omarchy-plugin-enable\`, and \`bin/omarchy-plugin-add\`. pr.title: Reset keyboard layout before suspend lock
pr.body: ## Problem If the machine suspends while on a non-Latin keyboard layout, the lock screen after resume stays on that layout, so the password is rejected (typed in Cyrillic instead of Latin). XKB layout survives suspend, so the lock screen inherits whatever layout was active. Verified against shipped packages: `omarchy-system-sleep-lock` is byte-identical across 4.0.2/4.0.3/4.0.4 and never contained a reset; the bug shows only on the suspend path, manual lock always worked. ## Fix Mirror the `omarchy-system-lock` reset step in `omarchy-system-sleep-lock`, right after requesting the lock.

pr.title: Fix silently broken display toggle under the Lua config parser
pr.body: ## The bug The Display panel's enable/disable toggle does nothing, on any system using the Lua config parser, and reports no error. `toggleDisplay()` in `shell/plugins/panels/monitor/Panel.qml` runs: ``` hyprctl keyword monitor <name>,disable ``` Hyprland's Lua parser rejects `keyword` outright, and `hyprctl` still exits 0: ``` $ hyprctl keyword general:gaps_in 5 keyword can't work with non-legacy parsers. Use eval. $ echo $? 0 ``` The zero exit is what makes this invisible — nothing surfaces in the panel, and nothing is logged. ## The fix Prefer `hyprctl eval` with `hl.monitor`, keeping `keyword` as the legacy-parser fallback. This is the same order `omarchy-screensaver` already uses. Unlike `keyword`, `eval` exits non-zero on failure (7 on a Lua error), so the fallback is actually reachable rather than dead code. Two details worth calling out for review: - **`disabled = false` is required to re-enable.** The direct translation of `,preferred,auto,auto` is accepted, returns `ok`, and leaves the output off. pr.body: ## Problem The bar's workspace indicator sometimes freezes and stops following workspace switches. Hyprland itself is fine (`hyprctl activeworkspace` is correct); only the shell is stale, and it stays that way until `omarchy restart shell`. When it happens, the shell log has exactly one line: ``` WARN: Hyprland event socket error: QLocalSocket::PeerClosedError ``` Hyprland closes the event socket (`.socket2.sock`) of a client that stops reading while events pile up. Quickshell 0.3.1 logs the error but never reconnects, so every `Hyprland.*` binding and `onRawEvent` handler in the shell goes quiet for the rest of its life. pr.body: ## Problem After the Windows VM has booted once, the guest leaves the shared folder `~/Windows` setgid (`2777`). From then on every `omarchy-windows-vm launch` fails with only the "Failed to start Windows VM" toast. `prepare_caller_mounts` hardens both sources with `chmod 0700` and then requires the mode to be exactly `700`. pr.title: Expose shell controls to assistive technology
pr.body: The shared `shell/Ui` kit controls now expose Qt `Accessible` roles, names, states and actions: buttons, toggles, switches, sliders, text fields, dropdowns and their popup rows, `ConfirmDialog`, `CursorSurface` rows and `KeyboardPanel`. Each accessibility action calls the signal the control already emits for a click, toggle or slider step, so there is no second code path. First-party icon-only controls get names through a new `accessibleName` property: bar buttons, switches, sliders, media transport buttons, workspaces, and the list rows in the Network, Bluetooth, Audio, Display, Dropbox and Tailscale panels. `accessibleName` is used rather than `tooltipText`, so no tooltip appears. Refs #12009. Today screen readers and AT-SPI tools see nothing in the bar, panels or dialogs, because the kit builds its controls from `Rectangle`/`Item` with no accessible role. pr.title: Let omarchy-hyprland-focus-app focus an exact window by address
pr.body: `omarchy-hyprland-focus-app` matches by application identity, which can't tell one window of an app from another. With nine kitty windows open, a caller that knows *which* terminal it means (a notification raised by a specific window, a plugin, a script) still lands on whichever one the search reaches first. This lets the caller say exactly which window it wants: ``` omarchy-hyprland-focus-app address:0x561019ece480 ``` - Only a window that is currently open gets focused. Hyprland ignores a dispatch at a stale address without saying so, which looks the same as a broken click, so a stale address exits 1 without dispatching. - It uses the `hl.dsp.focus` dispatcher and falls back to `focuswindow`, the same approach the rest of the script takes. - Any argument that isn't an `address:0x…` goes through the existing identity search unchanged, so current callers (`omarchy-launch-browser`, the notifications `focusApp`) behave exactly as before. ## Testing - `test/shell.d/hyprland-focus-app-test.sh`: two new cases (focusing by address dispatches only that window; a stale address is refused and nothing is dispatched). pr.title: Keep the bluetooth widget on the bar when the radio is blocked
pr.body: ## Problem On hardware where the Bluetooth rfkill switch is a **platform** switch, turning Bluetooth off removes the Bluetooth widget from the bar — including the control that turns it back on. The radio cannot be re-enabled from the GUI at all; recovery requires dropping to a terminal. `omarchy-bluetooth-power off` turns the radio off with `rfkill block bluetooth`, which is deliberate and correct — it is the half of the state that survives a reboot. But on a platform switch, blocking does not merely clear BlueZ's `Powered`: it **cuts power to the radio**. The controller leaves the USB bus, `hci0` disappears, BlueZ drops the adapter, and `Bluetooth.defaultAdapter` becomes `null`. `shell/plugins/panels/bluetooth/Panel.qml` gated the whole widget on that object: ```qml visible: adapter !== null ``` so the widget disappeared with the adapter, and `Bar.qml` collapsed the slot to zero width (`implicitWidth: activeItem && activeItem.visible ? ... : 0`). The panel already has the states this needs — a `󰂲` off glyph and a "Turned Off" label, both keyed on `!adapter.enabled`. On this hardware those branches are simply **unreachable**, because the adapter object is gone rather than disabled.

pr.body: ## What `openCaptivePortal()` handed the sign-in page to the default browser. It now opens a small layer-shell view that grows out beside the network panel, which stays open; the view closes with it. One line of behaviour changes in the panel; the rest is the view, a toggle, and tests. ## Why A browser window is a workspace member: it tiles, rearranges the layout when it opens and again when it closes, and meets the hotel's gateway carrying the user's real cookie jar, extensions and DNS settings. pr.body: ## Use the KeyboardPanel focus pattern on the full-screen overlays The overlays take keyboard focus exclusively: ```qml WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive ``` Hyprland routes every pointer and touch event to a surface with exclusive focus before hit-testing anything above it. So a surface drawn on top of an overlay cannot be touched. The event goes to the overlay underneath, which treats it as a click outside and dismisses itself. Omarchy already knows this. `Ui/KeyboardPanel.qml` says so: > Exclusive would also grant map-time focus, but it makes Hyprland route *every* pointer event to the exclusive surface no matter which output the cursor is over, which leaves clicks on any other monitor unable to reach the dismissal surfaces below. And it already has the fix: ```qml WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: open ? (focusPrimed ? WlrKeyboardFocus.OnDemand : WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive) : WlrKeyboardFocus.None ``` Prime with Exclusive so focus is acquired when the surface maps, settle on OnDemand 75ms later, which releases compositor-wide hit-testing. pr.title: Force software video decode in Chromium on NVIDIA GPUs with GSP firmware
pr.body: Fixes #13188. Video renders black in every Chromium-family browser on NVIDIA cards with GSP firmware. Audio plays, the player UI draws, the picture never arrives. It is not DRM: a local H.264 file in a bare `<video>` tag does it too. That driver targets Firefox; Chromium only uses it with an explicit opt-in (`VaapiOnNvidiaGPUs`). Chromium still reads the same variable, and when it ends up decoding through the NVIDIA driver (on my machine, a desktop with the i7-12700K's UHD 770 enabled next to an RTX 3080), it fails to import the frame: ``` eglCreateImage failed with 0x00003009 (EGL_BAD_MATCH) native_pixmap_egl_binding.cc:76 Unable to initialize binding from pixmap ozone_image_backing.cc:320 failed to create GL representation ``` I measured 442 to 568 of those in 8 seconds of playback, with no picture. pr.title: Mirror Hyprland triangular corners in shell surfaces
pr.body: Mirror Hyprland triangular corners in shell surfaces The shell already mirrors Hyprland's `decoration:rounding` as `Style.cornerRadius`, but it ignores `decoration:rounding_power`. Themes that use `rounding_power = 1.0` (Hyprland's triangular corner) get 45° cut window corners, while every shell surface still draws round corners. This makes `BorderSurface` follow the window corner shape: - `Style` also reads `decoration:rounding_power`, the same way it reads `decoration:rounding`, and sets `cornerChamfer` when the value is 1.0 or less. - `BorderGeometry` gains a `chamfer` flag. Corner arcs become straight cuts, and the inner edge is offset so borders keep an even width along the diagonal. - When `cornerChamfer` is set, `BorderSurface` clips itself to the cut outline (MultiEffect mask), squares its native fill underneath, and draws its border along the cut through `BorderOverlay`. - The cut follows Hyprland's effective window rounding (`rounding * rounding_power / 2`, as in `CWindow::rounding`) and is capped at 30% of a surface's shorter side, so short surfaces (menu rows, OSD, notifications) get a small cut instead of turning into hexagons. - Selection and hover highlights that wer

pr.title: Retry delay inhibit after logind OperationInProgress on resume
pr.body: ## Why `omarchy-sleep-lock.service` is `Restart=always`. After suspend/resume, logind still treats the previous delay inhibit as in progress, so `systemd-inhibit --mode=delay` fails with: ``` Failed to inhibit: The operation inhibition has been requested for is already running ``` (logind `OperationInProgress` / sd-bus `EINPROGRESS`). The unit then logs FAILURE every wake, churns restarts, and does not hold a delay inhibit for the *next* suspend. Closes #13160. ## Change Probe with a throwaway `systemd-inhibit ... true`, retrying only that "already running" error (up to ~6s), then `exec` the real inhibitor so `systemd-inhibit` remains the unit main PID and monitor stderr stays on the journal. Unrelated inhibit failures still fail the unit immediately. ## Tests `test/shell.d/sleep-monitor-test.sh` covers: - retry until the third probe succeeds, then final `exec` (4 calls) - unrelated inhibit errors fail after one call (call count asserted) Base: quattro.

pr.title: feat(notifications): cap critical popups at max duration instead of forever
pr.body: ## What A critical notification popup waits for the user: `durationFor()` returns `0` for `NotificationUrgency.Critical`, so it stays on screen until it is clicked, dismissed or replaced. That is what the first-party senders are for. Taildrop announcements (`manual/35-networking.md` promises the toast waits), pending migrations, a crash to diagnose, the sleep-lock warning and the first-run setup hooks all send critical with no `expire_timeout`, because they mean "wait for me". So the rule is now: **critical waits unless the sender states a timeout.** A positive `expire_timeout` is honoured for critical too, clamped like every other urgency between the normal floor and the 30s ceiling the rest already had. ```js if (urgency === criticalUrgency && requested === 0) return 0 var floor = urgency === lowUrgency ? LOW_POPUP_DURATION : NORMAL_POPUP_DURATION return Math.min(MAX_POPUP_DURATION, Math.max(floor, requested)) ``` The policy moved to `NotificationLogic.js` so it can be tested, which nothing covered before. pr.title: Strip stray special mode bits when hardening Windows VM directories
pr.body: If `~/Windows` picks up a setgid bit (mode 2700), launching the Windows VM dies with a generic "Failed to start Windows VM" and nothing in the logs. The culprit is GNU chmod: on directories it preserves setuid/setgid across a four-digit numeric mode, so root's `chmod 0700` leaves the directory at 2700, and the strict 700 check that follows returns 1 without saying a word. So use the five-digit `chmod 00700`, which actually clears the special bits, and have both the chmod failure and the mode mismatch say what went wrong on stderr, like every other validation in this script already does. Comes with a boundary test that puts stray setgid/setuid bits on the pinned sources and expects hardening to land on exactly 0700. It fails on the old script and passes on this one. Fixes #13146

pr.title: Keep the Windows VM running through a guest restart
pr.body: Restarting Windows from inside the VM kills it: `launch` runs `priv down` as soon as `xfreerdp3` exits, and a guest restart ends the RDP session. The same path tears the VM down when RDP is tried before the guest listens (#5202), including mid-install. `launch` now checks why the session ended with an RDP-level probe: it sends an X.224 Connection Request to 127.0.0.1:3389 and expects a TPKT reply. A plain TCP check can't do this because docker-proxy holds the port open for the container's lifetime. - Window closed locally (rc 0/11, guest up) → stop, as before (`--keep-alive` still keeps it running) - Server-initiated disconnect (rc 1): Windows keeps answering RDP for several seconds while restarting, so wait for it to drop, then wait for it to return and reconnect - Container gone → Windows shut down; exit without another `priv down` - Guest not listening yet → wait up to 10 min instead of tearing down (#5202) - Immediate repeated failures → give up after 3 tries Tested on Omarchy 4.0.4 with dockurr/windows (Win 11) and FreeRDP 3.31.1, using the same logic in a local launcher: guest restart reconnects, guest shutdown exits cleanly. pr.title: Wait for a slow-exiting shell before restarting it
pr.body: ## Problem `omarchy restart shell` can report success and leave no shell running (no bar). The kill loop runs `timeout 5 quickshell kill …`. When the shell is busy enough to take longer than 5 s to exit, `timeout` ends the command, the loop reads that as "no instances left", and the replacement is launched while the old shell is still alive. The new `quickshell -n` exits at once as a duplicate ("An instance of this configuration is already running."), which `omarchy-launch-shell` treats as a deliberate stop. The readiness ping can then be answered by the still-dying old shell, so restart exits 0 just before that shell goes away. I hit this during a plugin stress test; the journal showed the new instance refusing as a duplicate 5 s before the old one logged "Exiting due to IPC request". ## Reproduce ```sh pid=$(quickshell list -p "$OMARCHY_PATH/shell" --any-display -j | jq -r '.[0].pid') kill -STOP "$pid"; ( sleep 7; kill -CONT "$pid" ) & omarchy restart shell; echo "exit=$?" # exit=0 sleep 4; quickshell list -p "$OMARCHY_PATH/shell" --any-display # no running instances, no bar ``` ## Fix After the kill loop, wait until `quickshell list` reports no instance for the config. pr.body: ### Summary Fixes a class of lock-screen blank/wake loops on AMD HDMI systems: displays that drop HDMI hotplug-detect (HPD) when blanked re-light a locked screen over and over. Related: #11330, #8580, #10778, #8863. ### Problem When a DPMS-off output enters power save, many HDMI monitors de-assert HPD and then re-assert it as an input-source "autoscan" ~15s later. Linux has no HDMI HPD filter, so the kernel sees a disconnect→reconnect with an identical EDID (~0.75s apart) and raises a hotplug event: the output is removed and re-added with DPMS back on. Locked, that blank→wake→blank cycle repeats indefinitely (`drm: HDMI-A-x is not connected, clearing stale crtc`), measured at thousands of cycles per night on real installs. ### Root cause Userspace re-blank debounces ([#8896]( [#10130]( treat the symptom — the removal happens in amdgpu before userspace ever sees it. amdgpu's Display Manager now ships the right tool: an HDMI HPD filter (upstream *"drm/amd/display: Add an HPD filter for HDMI"*, a driver parameter disabled by default). pr.title: Keep the reveal mask rendering so background transitions animate
pr.body: Fixes #13125 ### Problem The background reveal never animates. Theme and wallpaper changes cut to the new image in a single step instead of drawing the centre-out reveal. The `NumberAnimation` is not at fault — it runs for its full 420 ms. The new wallpaper appears at ~550 ms (≈130 ms image load + 420 ms animation), all at once, at the moment the animation *finishes*. That points at the mask. `revealMask` is declared `visible: false` while being used as a live `MultiEffect { maskEnabled: true; maskSource: revealMask }`. A hidden item's layer texture is not re-rendered as `revealProgress` animates, so the mask stays frozen at progress 0. The incoming wallpaper is fully masked out for the whole animation and only becomes visible when `revealProgress >= 1` satisfies the other term of `incomingLayer.visible`. ### Fix `opacity: 0` instead of `visible: false`. The item stays in the render graph, so its layer texture updates every frame, while remaining invisible. pr.title: Only leave the alternate screen after SSH when it is still on
pr.body: Fixes #13057 ## Problem `_ssh_disarm` always sends `\e[?1049l` when an SSH session ends. Besides leaving the alternate screen, 1049l restores the cursor saved when the alternate screen was entered. A session that stayed on the primary screen (a plain remote shell) never saved one, so the cursor jumps to a stale position, often (1,1), and "Connection lost. Reconnecting..." and the next prompt print over the scrollback. Swapping in `\e[?1047l`, as the issue suggests, fixes that case but breaks the opposite one: when a remote tmux or editor dies while on the alternate screen, the cursor would be left at the alternate screen's coordinates on the primary screen instead of being restored to where the session started. ## Fix Ask the terminal whether the alternate screen is on with a DECRQM query (`\e[?1049$p`), and skip 1049l when it answers reset (2) or permanently reset (4). pr.title: Lock instead of suspending on the IdeaPad Slim 3 15AMN8
pr.body: ## Summary On the IdeaPad Slim 3 15AMN8 (Lenovo `82XQ`), `s2idle` is the only sleep state and the Micron NVMe firmware rejects all I/O with `Access Denied (sct 0x2 / sc 0x86) DNR` ~0.5 s after resume — btrfs remounts root read-only, and the machine needs a hard power cycle. The failure presents as a black screen or a lock screen that never accepts a password (PAM can't read the disk), so it gets debugged as a compositor bug. Per the reporter's suggested fallback: `HandleLidSwitch=lock` is strictly better than `ignore` — the session locks and the panel powers down (what a user expects from closing a laptop) while the filesystem stays alive. Hibernate was considered but the reporter's own attempt cold-booted on tight swap, so `lock` is the safe default. - New `install/hardware/fix-ideapad-suspend.sh` writes `/etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/50-ideapad-suspend.conf` only when DMI identifies `LENOVO`/`82XQ`, registered in `install/hardware/all.sh` - Migration applies the same drop-in on existing installs and reloads logind (not restart — restarting logind tears down the session) - Both paths gated on `OMARCHY_DMI_PATH`/`OMARCHY_LOGIND_CONF_DIR` for testing Fixes #12887 #### Test plan - [x] N

pr.title: Stop broadcasting hostname and permanent MAC on every network
pr.body: ## Summary Setup asks for a hostname and NetworkManager then sends it to every network the machine joins — DHCP option 12 on IPv4, the FQDN option on DHCPv6 — alongside the permanent hardware MAC, with no IPv6 privacy addresses. On shared networks that puts a name people often set to their own into every router's client list, tied to a fixed MAC that follows the machine around. - New `etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/omarchy-privacy.conf`: `dhcp-send-hostname` off for IPv4/IPv6, `wifi`/`ethernet.cloned-mac-address = stable` (one MAC per network — reservations and captive portals keep working), `ipv6.ip6-privacy = 2` - A migration retrofits `dhcp-send-hostname`/`ip6-privacy` onto saved wireless and wired profiles; it deliberately does **not** change MACs on existing connections, which would silently break MAC-filtered networks — saved profiles keep their address, new connections get the stable default - VPN/tunnel profiles are untouched Fixes #13054 #### Test plan - [x] New `test/shell.d/network-privacy-test.sh`: asserts the drop-in keys, and runs the migration against a stub `nmcli` to verify wifi/ethernet profiles get updated, VPNs are skipped, and no `cloned-mac` change is made Generate

pr.title: Read codex app-server replies unbuffered in the usage collector
pr.body: ## Summary - `rpc_request()` waited with `select()` on the pipe fd, then read through `proc.stdout.readline()` — a buffered text stream - When the app-server chunked a notification (`remoteControl/status/changed`, `account/updated`) into the same read as a reply, `readline()` pulled the whole chunk into Python's buffer and returned only the first line; the reply was already buffered so the fd never became readable again, `select()` kept timing out, and `account/read` intermittently raised `TimeoutError` (~1 in 4 runs in the issue's repro) - New `RpcLineReader` reads the fd raw via `os.read` and splits lines itself; the buffer persists across `rpc_request()` calls since a reply can arrive together with the previous one Also makes the scanner test's `mapfile`/`stat -c`/`touch -d` usage portable so the suite runs off GNU userland. pr.title: Keep the launch OSD timeout from being restarted indefinitely
pr.body: ## Summary Refs #12922. pr.title: Restart bluetoothd and reload btusb when the adapter is wedged
pr.body: Fixes #13078. Fixes #12519. ## Problem `omarchy-restart-bluetooth` summarises itself as *"Unblock and restart the bluetooth service"*, but the whole script was: ```bash rfkill unblock bluetooth rfkill list bluetooth ``` It never restarted anything. That is the correct and complete fix for a radio the user switched off, and it is a no-op for the two ways an adapter actually goes missing: - **bluetoothd desynced from D-Bus adapter state** (#13078, Intel `hci0` after a controller bounce). `systemctl restart bluetooth` recovers it instantly. The shell panel cannot do it either — `adapter` is `null`, so `toggleBluetooth()` returns early — so **Update → Hardware → Bluetooth** was the user's only route, and it printed `Unblocking bluetooth...` and exited. - **Firmware handshake timed out** (#12519, AX200 `8087:0029`): `Bluetooth: hci0: Reading Intel version command failed (-110)`. The controller stays in `HCI_SETUP` and is hidden from bluetoothd. Restarting the daemon cannot clear it; reloading `btusb` re-runs the firmware upload and the controller is back in ~1.4s. ## What changed ```text rfkill unblock unprivileged, unchanged sudo systemctl restart bluetooth.service unconditional; exit

pr.title: Prevent lid closure from interrupting shutdown
pr.body: ## Problem Choosing **Shut Down** and closing the lid can suspend the laptop instead of shutting it down. Reopening the lid resumes the session. See [#4273]( ## Fix Add `sleep:idle:handle-lid-switch` inhibition through shutdown preparation, the two-second delay, and the power-off request. The lid-specific lock is needed because ordinary sleep inhibitors do not normally block lid-triggered suspend. Start the user service immediately and move the delay inside it. Run preparation in the background and add a 30-second runtime limit to initiate cleanup if the worker stalls. Show a critical notification if inhibitor acquisition or the power-off request fails, while preserving the failure status. ## Testing - Eight focused tests pass, including blocked window closing and failure notifications. Real-systemd checks verify inhibitor lifetime and cleanup. - The original patch passed physical shutdown tests with the lid open and closed on a Dell XPS 13 DX13260 (Omarchy 4.0.4-1, September 19).

pr.title: Add Flutter dev environment
pr.body: Adds Flutter to the development environments you can install from the Omarchy menu (Install > Development > Flutter), or with `omarchy install dev-env flutter`. **How it works** Flutter is managed by `mise`, just like Go, Zig or .NET. mise ships prebuilt Flutter SDK releases, so the install is quick and you get per-project versions for free: ``` mise use flutter@3.44 # pin Flutter for this folder only mise use --global flutter@latest mise up # update Flutter ``` The installer also adds `clang cmake ninja pkgconf gtk3`, which is the toolchain `flutter doctor` asks for to build Linux desktop apps. It also turns off Flutter's analytics. **What's not included** The Android SDK and Android Studio are left out on purpose. They take several GB and not every Flutter developer targets Android. After installing, `flutter doctor` tells you what else you need for the platforms you care about. **Removal** `omarchy-remove-dev-env flutter` (and the Remove menu entry) uninstalls every mise-managed Flutter version and drops the global pin. The Linux toolchain packages stay, because other tools may need them too.

pr.title: Allow TRIM through dm-crypt on encrypted installs
pr.body: ## What this fixes An Omarchy full-disk-encrypted install never lets TRIM reach the SSD. dm-crypt drops every discard unless its mapping was opened with `allow-discards`, so on every encrypted host tested the root reports `discard_granularity 0`, `cryptsetup luksDump` shows `Flags: (no flags)`, `fstrim` answers "the discard operation is not supported", and `fstrim.timer` is disabled. btrfs turns `discard=async` on by itself since 6.2, but only for devices that advertise discard support, and a LUKS mapping without the option does not — 400+ GiB of freed blocks were still treated as live data by the controller. pr.title: fix: report panel plugin load failures instead of throwing
pr.body: ## What happens A panel, overlay or menu plugin that fails to load produces **no actionable message at all**, and is never hidden. `shell/shell.qml`, panel loader `onStatusChanged`: ```js var detail = errorString && errorString() ? errorString() : "" ``` `Loader` has no `errorString()` member, so `errorString` is an unresolved name. In JavaScript a bare unresolved identifier throws rather than evaluating as falsy, so this line raises ``` ReferenceError: errorString is not defined ``` which aborts the whole handler — before `console.warn(...)` and before `shell.hide(panelEntry.pluginId)`. The comment above the line assumes `Loader.errorString()` exists and works even when `sourceComponent` is null; that is not part of Qt Quick's `Loader` API. ## The fix Probe the name defensively with `typeof` and keep the existing `sourceComponent` fallback. The intended diagnostic is emitted again and `hide()` runs. ## How I ran into it Debugging a third-party `menu` plugin on omarchy 4.0.4. Every load failure showed up only as this `ReferenceError`, with the actual QML error never printed — it hid the real cause for hours. pr.title: Have the omarchy skill check existing and marketplace plugins before building
pr.body: ## Summary When asked for a new shell feature (a bar widget, overlay, lock screen and so on), agents using the end-user `omarchy` skill tend to go straight to writing a new plugin or config. They skip over first-party plugins Omarchy already ships, some of which are installed but disabled, and the 4,000+ plugins in the community marketplace. This adds a "Check What Exists Before Building" section to `plugins.md`, plus a matching step in the SKILL.md decision framework. Before building, the agent: 1. **Checks what's already on the system**: `omarchy plugin list` (including disabled first-party plugins such as `omarchy.tailscale`, `omarchy.microphone` and `omarchy.active-window`), existing keybindings, and `omarchy commands`. It offers `enable` or `clone` where one of those fits. 2. **Searches the marketplace**: it queries ` with `jq`, matching whole words and ranking verified plugins first, then by stars. pr.title: Honour explicit expireTimeout for critical notifications (#12911)
pr.body: Closes #12911. Per the FreeDesktop notification specification, an explicit non-zero `expireTimeout` should be honoured regardless of urgency. Previously, `durationFor()` unconditionally returned 0 for Critical notifications, ignoring finite timeouts requested by senders (such as low-battery warnings) and causing toasts to persist indefinitely across reboots.

pr.title: Menu: coerce string select deltas; let summons open on a named row with primed checkmarks
pr.body: ## Summary Two menu improvements driven by summonable state — the shell IPC delivers every argument as a JS string, and menu-mode summons could start on the wrong row with stale checkmarks. 1. **`select()` coerces string deltas.** `omarchy.menu select "1"` used to concatenate (`selectedIndex + "1"`), so the cursor jumped by more than a row — or froze on repeated taps. 2. **`open()` accepts `checked` / `initialIndex` / `initialId`.** A menu-mode summon can now appear already sitting on the right row with the right rows checkmarked on the first paint, instead of row 0 with markers arriving late from the async guard batch. pr.body: ## Problem Playing a video podcast fullscreen in Spotify does not stop the screensaver. It launches mid-playback and covers the video. ## Root cause Spotify runs under XWayland: ``` $ hyprctl clients -j | jq '.[] | select(.class=="Spotify") | {class, xwayland}' { "class": "Spotify", "xwayland": true } ``` XWayland clients cannot bind `zwp_idle_inhibit_manager_v1`. Nothing therefore reports playback to the compositor. `shell/plugins/services/idle/Service.qml` sets `IdleMonitor { respectInhibitors: true }`, which is correct — there is simply no inhibitor to respect, so the screensaver fires on the normal timeout. ## Fix Add the same compositor-side window rule already used for GeForce NOW, Moonlight, RetroArch, and Steam — apps that likewise do not inhibit idle themselves. pr.title: Disambiguate keyboard layout labels for dual-script languages
pr.body: ### Problem In XKB (`xkeyboard-config`), dual-script languages share the same ISO 639-1 `brief` code across their scripts: - `Serbian` (Cyrillic) and `Serbian (Latin)` both carry `brief: 'sr'` - `Belarusian` (Cyrillic) and `Belarusian (Latin)` both carry `brief: 'by'` - `Kazakh` (Cyrillic) and `Kazakh (Latin)` both carry `brief: 'kk'` - `Uzbek` (Cyrillic) and `Uzbek (Latin)` both carry `brief: 'uz'` - `Azerbaijani` (Latin) and `Azerbaijani (Cyrillic)` both carry `brief: 'az'` Because `shortLabel()` only looks up the brief and truncates it to uppercase, both variants evaluate to the exact same two-letter bar label (e.g. `SR` and `SR`), making it impossible to know which script is active. ### Solution When a two-letter brief covers multiple scripts, append the script initial (`L` for Latin, `C` for Cyrillic) within the widget's existing 3-character width ceiling: - `Serbian` → `SR` - `Serbian (Latin)` → `SRL` - `Belarusian (Latin)` → `BYL` - `Kazakh (Latin)` → `KKL` - `Azerbaijani (Cyrillic)` → `AZC` The delimiter check `/(^|[^\w-])(Latin|Cyrillic)(?=[,)])/i` ensures compound terms like `Spanish (Latin American)` and `French (alt., Latin-9 only)` are not treated as script annotations

pr.title: Make the notification text font themeable via [notifications] font-family
pr.body: Notification summary and body text hard-code `Liberation Sans`, so they are the only shell surface that ignores both the theme and `omarchy font set`. Users who want them to match the bar currently have to clone the whole notifications plugin to change two lines, and the clone then stops receiving upstream fixes. This adds an optional `font-family` token to `[notifications]` in `shell.toml`: ```toml [notifications] font-family = "monospace" # follows `omarchy font set` ``` - Default stays `Liberation Sans`, so nothing changes for anyone who doesn't set it. - Works from a theme (`shell.toml` / `shell.notifications.toml`) or machine-wide in `~/.config/omarchy/shell.toml`, which survives theme switches. - Rebinds live: editing the user `shell.toml` updates notifications already on screen, no shell restart. Changes: - `Color.notifications.fontFamily` reads the token with `Liberation Sans` as fallback. - `NotificationCard.qml` binds summary and body to it. - Commented token in `default/themed/shell.toml.tpl`, a short section in `docs/theming.md`, and assertions in `test/shell.d/notifications-test.sh` pinning the binding and the default. pr.title: feat: add symfony-cli local server hint to laravel installation
pr.body: ### What does this PR do? This PR enhances the Laravel development environment installation by adding a helpful hint for developers to use the Symfony CLI tool for local domains and SSL. ### Why is this needed? Since PHP on Omarchy is now decoupled from system services and managed via `mise` (#12141), Laravel developers lost the "Herd/Valet-like" experience for `.test` domains. We initially considered bundling `symfony-cli` with Laravel, but that would break the Omarchy menu state and create uninstallation conflicts. Instead, this PR adds a smart terminal hint after Laravel installation, educating developers to explicitly install the **Symfony Environment** from the Omarchy menu if they want advanced local serving capabilities. This maintains perfect separation of environments (Opt-in philosophy) while guiding developers to the best tools available. ### How to use it? 1. Install the Laravel environment: ```bash omarchy-install-dev-env laravel ``` 2. The terminal will now guide the user with a helpful tip on how to get local SSL and domains using Symfony CLI. 3. pr.title: Add a camera bar widget that shows when a webcam is in use
pr.body: ## Summary Adds `omarchy.camera`, a bar widget that stays visible while a webcam is plugged in and switches to a record mark while an app has the camera open. It is off by default, same as the microphone widget. Enable it with: ```bash omarchy plugin enable omarchy.camera ``` That places it in the right section. `--before omarchy.microphone` only works once the microphone widget is already on the bar. The icon is a camera while the device is idle. It becomes a record mark, using the bar's active color, while a PipeWire link leaves the webcam's v4l2 or libcamera source, or a process has that node's `/dev/videoN` open. When `pw-dump` returns data, other video nodes (metadata, codecs, a leftover v4l2loopback) do not count as a webcam. A v4l2 loopback source counts only while its `v4l2-relayd` instance is running, so an unplugged Cam Link does not leave a camera on the bar, and a running relay still counts when PipeWire never created a node. A loopback with no matching active relay does not count, including an OBS virtual camera and a relay whose name or `CARD_LABEL` the probe does not match. pr.title: Guard battery sysfs rate against bogus EC readings
pr.body: On some machines the EC reports a bogus but numeric current. My MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI+ (BAT1 BIF0_9) reports current_now=-65A for a ~7.5W discharge, so the panel showed Discharging -1124W while UPower correctly reported 7.5W. The sysfs override only guarded readability, so any numeric value clobbered the good UPower rate. This: - only trusts sysfs reads that succeed and are numeric (allows negative current_now, which is the normal discharging sign), - rejects insane magnitudes (>150W) or values wildly above UPower's rate (>3x when UPower is solid), keeping the UPower value instead, - displays the rate as magnitude (state already says charging/discharging, so no more -1124W), - compares idle against magnitude so a large negative rate can't fake charge-idle, - omits cycle_count 0 when UPower reports charge-cycles N/A so the panel shows — instead of a misleading 0. Complements #12649/#12755 (those cover failed/empty reads); this covers bogus-but-numeric reads. Verified with the extended battery-status-test.sh scenarios (bogus -65A, non-numeric, sane negative discharge) plus live hardware: bogus -1113W discharge now shows 7.5W, and a sane 29.1W charge still uses the live sysfs value.

pr.title: fix(hypr): resolve universal clipboard letters from primary layout
pr.body: Summary Fixes #12570. Universal "SUPER+A/C/V/X" shortcuts currently inject logical letters through Hyprland's "send_key_state". When a non-Latin XKB group such as Russian is active, Hyprland may fail to resolve the Latin keysym and report: send_key_state: key not found Using fixed QWERTY keycodes avoids that lookup, but introduces a different regression: physical key positions do not preserve logical "A/C/V/X" across layouts such as Dvorak and French AZERTY. This revision resolves each logical clipboard letter against the configured primary XKB layout, then injects the resulting "code:N" keycode. That gives us both invariants: - a non-Latin secondary group cannot make "C/V/X/A" unresolvable; - a non-QWERTY primary layout still receives the intended logical shortcut. pr.title: fix(plugins): suspend local watch during plugin update (#12859)
pr.body: Summary Fixes #12859. "omarchy plugin update" mutates a third-party plugin checkout while "PluginRegistry" recursively watches the same tree with "inotifywait". A fast-forward can therefore emit a burst of filesystem events while QML files are only partially updated. The shell may begin "reloadPlugins()" during that burst and recreate components from an inconsistent tree. This revision makes the update mutation an explicitly owned critical section: 1. serialize concurrent updater processes; 2. fetch and obtain confirmation while the watcher remains active; 3. suspend the watcher immediately before filesystem mutation; 4. fail before mutation if a reachable shell cannot suspend it; 5. merge and validate the approved updates; 6. request one explicit rescan while observation is still suspended; 7. restore the watcher. Ordinary local editing still uses a trailing reload debounce, now "500 ms". Why the first revision was incomplete The earlier version correctly stopped the watcher during one updater process, but two ownership gaps remained. pr.title: Add signal fallback to omarchy-restart-shell for IPC-wedged shells
pr.body: Fixes #12641. `omarchy restart shell` could not recover a shell whose IPC socket was wedged. `quickshell kill` talks to the instance over `ipc.sock`; if the shell's event loop is stuck (e.g. after a WirePlumber restart leaves Quickshell spinning on a dead PipeWire socket), the kill never lands and the command immediately reported failure while the old process kept running and leaking. Changes: - After the existing IPC kill loop, collect any `quickshell` processes still running this config from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` - Escalate from `SIGTERM` to `SIGKILL` for survivors - Clean up stale Quickshell runtime directories: dead `by-pid` entries and dangling `by-shell` symlinks. This matters because a spinning shell can fill `/run/user/$UID`, and once `instance.lock` cannot be written, `qs list`/`qs ipc` cannot match the fresh instance even after the old process is gone. Tested: - `bash -n bin/omarchy-restart-shell` - `test/shell.d/restart-shell-recovery-test.sh` validates the IPC kill loop, signal fallback, and cleanup logic Generated with [Devin](

pr.title: Fix Codex usage timeouts on batched replies
pr.body: Codex 0.156 can send notifications and an RPC reply in the same stdout chunk. `readline()` buffers the reply, but the next `select()` only checks the pipe. The collector then times out on `account/read` and the panel shows an "account/read" error despite having received the answer. Read raw bytes into a shared buffer and consume complete lines before waiting on the pipe. Partial replies still respect the request timeout. Validation: - Added regression coverage for batched notifications and replies, split replies, stalled partial replies, and EOF. The batched case fails on the original collector. - Collector, usage-update, and agents-panel tests pass. - Live Codex 0.156: the installed collector failed 5 of 6 runs; the patched collector passed all 6 in 0.80–1.09 seconds. - `./test/all`: CLI suite passes. Seven shell test files fail, all reproduced on clean upstream: `config`, `kernel-headers-migration`, `omarchy-kernel-migration`, `runtime-smoke`, `screenshot-sanity`, `snapper`, and `unowned-system-paths`. Three other files report skipped checks.

pr.title: Keep speakersafetyd retrying after 96 kHz panics and toast if amps stay locked
pr.body: Fixes #12976. A screen recording that opens the Asahi speaker path at 96 kHz panics `speakersafetyd` on bad ivsense. Stock `StartLimitBurst=10` / 60s then leaves the unit in `start-limit-hit`. macaudio clamps the amps (`Speaker Volume Unlock=0`) while PipeWire still reports 100% unmuted, so YouTube/X go silent with no UI cue. This does not fix the 96 kHz trigger (see #10970 / #11092 for the *file* sample rate). It stops the desktop from staying muted after the capture client is gone, and it toasts if the lock lasts ~20s. - Drop-in disables the start limit and waits 5s between restarts. Copied only when `speakersafetyd.service` is installed (install + migration), so x86 images do not grow a unit directory they will never load. - User watcher (inert without `/usr/bin/speakersafetyd` and a Wayland display) toasts once while `Speaker Volume Unlock` stays at 0. It never writes mixer controls. - Migration also `reset-failed` + starts the daemon when it is already dead on an existing install. Related: #10970, #10858.

pr.title: Dismiss screensaver on pointer activity after launch settle
pr.body: ## What Pointer/touchpad motion while the screensaver is up now dismisses it and cancels the pending idle/lock cycle. Arm a second `IdleMonitor` only while an `org.omarchy.screensaver` window is present. It ignores the self-inflicted launch activity until it has settled for 1s, then `pkill`s the screensaver script on the next seat input. The existing `closewindow` path cancels the idle cycle and stops the lock timer. Also stop clearing tracked screensaver windows at idle-cycle start so a menu-launched screensaver remains dismissable. ## Why `omarchy-screensaver` only exits on keyboard stdin or focus loss. The main idle monitor reports `active` from the launch focus blip and then stays active, so further pointer motion never reaches `handleActiveSignal`. Touchpad users could not wake the screensaver, and the lock timer could still fire while they were moving the pointer. ## Tests ``` bash test/shell.d/idle-test.sh ``` Passes: dismiss-state pins in `IdleModel.js`, QML wiring for `dismissMonitor` / script `pkill`, and Stay Awake toggle checks. Fixes #12650

pr.title: Honor critical notification expireTimeout when sender requests one
pr.body: ## What `durationFor()` mapped every Critical notification to lifetime `0`, discarding the sender's `expireTimeout`. That made critical toasts with an explicit timeout (e.g. battery-low via `omarchy-notification-send -u critical -t 30000`) immortal on screen and resurrect on every reboot via `restorePopups()`. ## Why FreeDesktop treats `expireTimeout == 0` as never-expire. A **non-zero** timeout should still be honoured for critical urgency. Sticky critical (timeout 0/absent) stays intentional. ## Change In `shell/plugins/notifications/Service.qml` `durationFor()`: - Critical + `expireTimeout > 0` → finite lifetime from `requestedDuration`, clamped to `maxPopupDuration` - Critical + `expireTimeout <= 0` → still `0` (sticky until dismiss) Restore already calls `durationFor(entry.urgency, entry.expireTimeout)` and archives via `popupExpired` when the lifetime has elapsed; snapshots already persist `expireTimeout`. No restore-path change required once duration is correct. ## Tests Extended `test/shell.d/notifications-test.sh`: - Critical with positive timeout → finite duration (and clamp to max) - Critical with 0/missing → stays 0 - Low/Normal floors unchanged - Finite-lifetime critic

pr.title: fix(lock): give session lock 1500ms to stabilize outputs
pr.body: ## What Bump `sessionLockStabilizeTimer` in `shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml` from **500ms** to **1500ms** before `requestSessionLock()` creates per-screen lock surfaces. ## Why On idle lock with multi-monitor fractional-scale layouts (e.g. DP-2 3840x2160 @ 1.5 whose logical width positions DP-3), 500ms is too short for all outputs to settle geometry. Lock surfaces can be created against invalid/zero-sized screens; the second monitor then never unlocks and can leave Hyprland/outputs in a bad state. Manual lock does not hit the same race. Reporter verified that **1500ms** reliably fixes the idle path. Smallest tip-apply only — not widening into a full per-screen geometry wait. ## Tests - No adjacent automated test pins this QML timer interval (lock plugin has no unit coverage for `sessionLockStabilizeTimer`). - Interval pinned by inspection of `Service.qml` + reporter’s verified repro/fix on idle dual-monitor lock (`Fixes` path in #12949). - Diff is the single interval change; other lock timers left untouched. Fixes #12949

pr.title: Keep the update transcript out of world-writable /tmp
pr.body: `omarchy-update` re-execs itself through `script(1)` into a hardcoded path, as the first thing it does, and `omarchy-update-analyze-logs` reads the same path back: ```bash exec env OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOGGED=1 script -qefc "$script_command" "/tmp/omarchy-update.log" ``` `/tmp` is world-writable and nothing checks who owns that file. `script` opens it with `O_CREAT`, which `fs.protected_regular=1` refuses when the file belongs to someone else. So whoever owns the file decides who may run `omarchy update`. This is not the same issue as #11630. That one exits 0 with no log created at all. This one exits 1 with `script: cannot open /tmp/omarchy-update.log: Permission denied`, and needs the file to already exist owned by another user. ## Two ways it goes wrong **Another local user blocks everyone's updates.** Verified on 4.0.4 in a VM: ```console mallory$ echo x > /tmp/omarchy-update.log; chmod 666 /tmp/omarchy-update.log dev$ omarchy-update script: cannot open /tmp/omarchy-update.log: Permission denied $ echo $? 1 ``` It aborts before the confirmation prompt and before any work. pr.title: Keep Bluetooth USB controllers awake when TLP manages USB power
pr.body: Refs #12095 (complements #10140) ## What Ships `/etc/tlp.d/omarchy-bluetooth-usb.conf` — a TLP drop-in that excludes the Intel Bluetooth combo cards from TLP's USB autosuspend — and registers the path in the upgrade `--overwrite` list. ## Why Two independent layers keep Bluetooth USB controllers suspended on Omarchy machines: 1. The no-op `modprobe.d` option documented in #12095 and addressed for the kernel-parameter layer by #10140 (usbcore is built in). 2. **TLP**, when a user has installed it (it is not an Omarchy package). TLP applies `power/control=auto` and `autosuspend_delay_ms=2000` per USB device through its udev hook, which runs as a `RUN+=` program — i.e. after rule processing — so `power/control` writes from ordinary udev rules lose on add events, and no kernel parameter helps because the delay is written explicitly. With layer 2 active, the controller is runtime-suspended when a bonded BLE peripheral tries to reconnect; the advertisements are dropped and the peripheral only comes back after it is removed and paired again. pr.title: Don't let the Codex usage collector install Codex
pr.body: The Agents widget runs `omarchy-agent-usage-codex` on each refresh. That command found `codex` on `PATH`, which is the lazy launcher at `~/.local/bin/codex`, and the launcher's first step is `mise use -g`. A machine with no Codex install therefore started a download. The collector kills the launcher when the app-server handshake times out, systemd adopts `mise`, and the install continues. This happens with no default agent set. The probe now uses `mise which codex`, which only prints a binary that is already installed. A symlink at the launcher path is still probed, since that is the user's own binary. The launcher file itself and mise shims are not executed. If Codex is not installed, the usage record says so.

pr.title: Load high contrast VS Code themes as hc-black/hc-light
pr.body: `omarchy-theme-set-vscode` builds the local extension's `uiTheme` from the theme's `vscode-theme.json` `type`, but only distinguishes `light` from everything else. A theme that declares `"type": "hc"` is therefore installed as `vs-dark`, so VS Code never enters high contrast mode and ignores high-contrast-only colors such as `editor.selectionForeground` (inverted selection text), `contrastBorder` and `contrastActiveBorder`. This maps `hc` / `hc-black` to `hc-black` and `hc-light` to `hc-light`; `light` and everything else behave as before. Motivation: [Darkroom Night Vision]( is a red-only theme where every syntax color is red, so the only way to make selected editor text readable is black-on-red, which VS Code only renders in high contrast mode. Testing: added a `test/cli` case asserting a `"type": "hc"` theme gets `uiTheme: hc-black`. I checked the scripts with `bash -n` and the mapping by hand but couldn't run `test/cli` locally (no `jq` on that machine). pr.title: Add a reveal toggle to masked TextFields, wired up for the Wi-Fi passphrase
pr.body: Typing a Wi-Fi passphrase into the network panel is blind. There is no way to check what you typed before hitting connect, and a wrong character only surfaces as "Wrong password" after the connect attempt has already failed. This adds an opt-in reveal control to `Ui/TextField`. A field with `password: true` can set `revealable: true` and gets an eye button inside its right padding that flips `echoMode`. The button is only drawn when `password` is set, so a plain field never grows an inert button, and `revealed` resets whenever the field is hidden, so a prompt reopened later always starts masked. The Wi-Fi passphrase field in the network panel opts in. The dev gallery's password demo does too, so the new variant shows up in the kit preview. The button is deliberately mouse-only: the network panel blocks its key catcher while the prompt is open so the TextField owns the keys, and making the button tabbable would sit between the field and Enter-to-connect. Verified in the running shell. `network-password`, `network`, `qml-text-format`, `border-geometry`, `button-border-stability` and `pointer-move-gate` all pass.

pr.title: fix(menu): contain the keybindings Lua bind scan
pr.body: ## Summary `SUPER + K` could OOM-kill the session and take Hyprland down (issue #12852). Root cause: the keybindings menu's Lua bind scan dofiles the user's config under a fake `hl` environment, and two growth paths there were unbounded: - Dispatcher expressions serialize their own arguments back into the expression, so a nest of `hl.dsp.*(...)` calls **doubles in size every level** — ~35 levels is ~16GB, matching the reported 18GB. - `lua_literal()` recursed through tables with no cycle detection, so a cyclic config argument recursed without bound. pr.title: Serialize concurrent migration runs
pr.body: Two concurrent `omarchy-migrate` processes can both see a missing completion marker and execute the same migration. The top-level update lock does not cover a direct migration run alongside an update or another direct run. Hold a per-user lock in the migration state directory across migration execution and completion-marker writes. A waiting runner rechecks the markers after obtaining the lock. The lock is separate from the update lock, `--pending` remains nonblocking, and migration children close the lock descriptor so background services cannot keep it held after the runner finishes. Validation: - The new concurrency regression fails on upstream `quattro` at `947e2fc0` because both runners execute the first migration. - `bash test/shell.d/migrate-lock-test.sh` passes: direct/direct and direct/update contention, marker publication, failed-migration retry, independent state directories, a surviving background child, and runner-only HUP/INT/TERM signals. - Existing `migrate-wrapper-test.sh`, `migrate-scope-test.sh`, and `migrate-notify-test.sh` pass. - `./test/cli`, `bash test/shell.d/bin-style-test.sh`, Bash syntax checks, and `git diff --check` pass. pr.title: Preserve active themes when staging or publication fails
pr.body: If copying or rendering a theme fails, `omarchy-theme-set` currently continues, deletes the working theme, and reports success. Reproducing with a renderer that exits 42 on current `quattro` leaves the newly selected theme without its generated terminal configuration; the previous `foot.ini` is gone. Check staging, palette conversion, and rendering before changing active files. The renderer now propagates required read/write failures and cleans its scratch files. Move the completed staging directory to a unique sibling before the atomic exchange, and roll it back if publishing `theme.name` fails. If rollback also fails, report and retain that unique recovery directory so later failed or successful activations cannot delete the previous working files. Initial activation uses a rename with equivalent rollback. Application hooks still run only after publication. This complements #11223: it handles failed commands and publication, while that PR defines the missing-palette policy. Existing manual themes without `colors.toml` retain their current behavior. pr.title: Propagate AUR update failures
pr.body: When `yay -Sua` fails or is interrupted, `omarchy-update-aur-pkgs` currently runs its trailing `echo` and returns success. The parent update then continues through its remaining steps instead of reporting the failed AUR transaction. Enable `set -e` in the helper so it preserves the failing exit status. No foreign packages and an unavailable AUR remain successful skips. Regression tests cover the helper and the real helper inside a stubbed full update, including stopping later steps and releasing the update inhibitor. Validation: - Reproduced both failures on upstream `quattro` at `947e2fc0`: the helper and parent update incorrectly succeed when the `yay` stub fails. - `bash test/shell.d/update-aur-test.sh` and `bash test/shell.d/update-sequence-test.sh` pass, including exit statuses 1, 42, and 130. - `./test/cli`, `bash test/shell.d/bin-style-test.sh`, Bash syntax checks, and `git diff --check` pass. Package and session operations are stubbed in these tests; no real package transaction was run.

pr.title: Remove dead CommonJS module.exports guards from shell JS modules
pr.body: ## What Removes a trailing `if (typeof module !== "undefined") { module.exports = {...} }` block from 26 `.js` files under `shell/plugins/` and `shell/services/`. `module` is never defined in quickshell's QML JS-module import context (`import "X.js" as X`), so this block is dead CommonJS/UMD boilerplate — it never runs, and nothing reads `module.exports`; every one of these functions is already reachable as a top-level declaration via the QML import. ## Why See #12677 (and my comment there). Evaluating `typeof module` at module scope, inside a QML JS module context created fresh during `Repeater` delegate incubation, appears to trigger a real Qt 6.11.2 QML-engine crash (`Runtime::TypeofName` → `QObjectWrapper::getQmlProperty` → SIGSEGV). I hit this independently via `plugins/services/idle/IdleModel.js`, with a full symbolized backtrace matching #12677's. The identical dead block exists in 25 other files, which is a plausible shared trigger for a number of other open "Repeater SIGSEGV" issues in this repo (different subsystems, same call-chain shape) — several already got narrow per-subsystem mitigations (debounce/snapshot before feeding a `Repeater`) that treat the symptom rather t

pr.title: Keep a closed lid awake from the power panel
pr.body: Closing the lid suspends the laptop. That is right for a laptop in a bag, and wrong for a laptop carrying a build, an agent, or an SSH session that should survive the walk from the office to the kitchen table. This adds a *Lid close* choice to the Power panel: **Suspend** (the default) or **Stay Awake**. ## How it works - The idle service owns a second stay-awake flag, `~/.local/state/omarchy/indicators/lid-stay-awake`, persisted next to the existing one and picked up through the same directory watcher. - While the flag is set the service holds a logind `handle-lid-switch` inhibitor. logind honours that inhibitor type regardless of `LidSwitchIgnoreInhibited`, so nothing in `logind.conf` is touched and no privileges are needed. pr.title: Discover shell plugins through XDG data directories
pr.body: A dev-linked Omarchy shell only discovers plugins in its checkout and the user plugin directory, so packages installed under `/usr/share/omarchy/shell/plugins` are missed without a user symlink. Make the shell and CLI resolve external plugin IDs from `$HOME/.config/omarchy/plugins`, then `$OMARCHY_PATH/shell/plugins`, then `omarchy/shell/plugins` under each `$XDG_DATA_DIRS` directory in order. The first valid manifest wins; unset or empty `$XDG_DATA_DIRS` uses `/usr/local/share:/usr/share` in both the CLI and shell. Keep `omarchy.*` reserved for built-ins from the active Omarchy tree. Trust `omacom.*` plugins from the active tree or XDG data directories; a user-directory copy still wins by precedence and remains untrusted. Discovery origin determines trust rather than manifest claims or pathname prefixes. Trusted plugins receive the existing first-party host APIs and declared capabilities, and trusted non-bar plugins are enabled by default unless explicitly disabled. pr.title: Stop treating an initramfs hook banner as a failed rebuild
pr.body: `omarchy-update-analyze-logs` treats pacman's `Updating linux initcpios...` line as proof that mkinitcpio rebuilt an image. That line is the hook banner. It is printed when the hook starts, before mkinitcpio decides whether the triggered hook is actually in the preset. A `pcsclite` upgrade triggers `sd-encrypt-opensc`. A preset that only uses `encrypt` makes mkinitcpio exit without building anything, so `Initcpio image generation successful` never appears. The update then prints: ``` Error: Initramfs generation may have failed. Review logs before restart. ``` Nothing failed, and the boot image was left alone. The same false alarm happens for any `pcsclite`, `cryptsetup`, `systemd`, or `lvm2` upgrade that does not belong in the preset. The warning is the one signal that should catch a real initramfs failure, so a repeated false alarm trains people to ignore it. The checker now warns only when mkinitcpio reports an error, or a preset build starts and does not succeed. A hook banner by itself stays quiet. A preset that mkinitcpio skips (`Skipping image`, after it has already printed `Building image from preset`) is not counted as a failed build. `test/shell.d/update-analyze-logs-test.

pr.title: Drop a2dp_source from Bluetooth auto-connect to prevent WirePlumber crash
pr.body: ## Problem When a phone (advertising Audio Source / A2DP source profile) comes into Bluetooth range and connects, BlueZ refuses the source transport with `org.bluez.Error.NotAuthorized`. The stock Omarchy WirePlumber config auto-connects both `a2dp_sink` **and** `a2dp_source` for every Bluetooth card: ``` bluez5.auto-connect = [ a2dp_sink a2dp_source ] ``` WirePlumber's `scripts/monitors/bluez/create-node.lua` (line 42) does not guard the return of `LocalNode()` against nil. When the source transport acquisition fails, the node is nil, and line 43 dereferences it — crashing WirePlumber. After the crash, every PulseAudio sink input lands on sink `4294967295` (uint32 -1), silently detaching from all audio output for all streams. Restarting WirePlumber fixes audio, but on Omarchy that recovery then triggers quickshell issue #1052, causing the shell to spin on the dead PipeWire socket growing RSS by ~47 MB/s. So one phone entering Bluetooth range can cascade: **audio broken → shell RAM spiral → /run/user/1000 fills → Super+Space fails**. pr.title: Scope the LocalSend firewall rule to private networks
pr.body: `install/config/firewall.sh` opens 53317/tcp+udp with no source restriction, so every install carries an `ALLOW IN ... Anywhere` rule on both IPv4 and IPv6: ```console $ sudo ufw status verbose Default: deny (incoming), allow (outgoing), disabled (routed) To Action From 53317/udp ALLOW IN Anywhere 53317/tcp ALLOW IN Anywhere 53317/udp (v6) ALLOW IN Anywhere (v6) 53317/tcp (v6) ALLOW IN Anywhere (v6) ``` LocalSend is installed but has no unit and no autostart entry, so on a fresh 4.0.4 system the port is open and nothing is listening on it. pr.title: Add lazy thumbnails and gate layer effects to nearby slides in background switcher
pr.body: Fixes #12792 ### Problem When opening the background switcher (`omarchy-theme-bg-switcher`) with large wallpaper directories (hundreds of images), the switcher timed out with: ``` omarchy-shell is not responding Image selector failed to accept request ``` This was caused by two compounding bottlenecks: 1. `bin/omarchy-theme-bg-switcher` invoked `omarchy-menu-images` without `--lazy-thumbnails` (unlike `omarchy-theme-switcher`), causing synchronous generation of all thumbnails before opening the picker. 2. In `shell/plugins/image-picker/ImagePicker.qml`, `layer.enabled: true` was hardcoded on both the mask shape and effect items in the delegate. As a result, opening a directory with hundreds of images created offscreen texture FBOs for every delegate at startup rather than only for the visible/nearby slides, blocking the main thread during initial presentation. ### Solution - Added `--lazy-thumbnails` to `bin/omarchy-theme-bg-switcher`. - In `shell/plugins/image-picker/ImagePicker.qml`, bound `layer.enabled: item.nearby` and gated border `Shape` visibility on `item.nearby`, ensuring offscreen rendering resources are allocated only for slides in the active viewport window. - Verified

pr.body: Omarchy can open the lock screen by looking at you, and approve `sudo` and polkit requests with a nod, using the infrared camera that Windows Hello laptops carry. Three commits, each standing on its own: 1. **lock: face authentication opens the lock screen.** A third PAM stack, `omarchy-lock-face`, beside the password and fingerprint ones. The face module answers it and `pam_deny` closes it, so looking at the machine is the act and no prompt is involved. The panel probes for a face while blank and wakes only for an attentive one; a face indicator and media controls on the lock view. 2. **security: setup, another look, removal, hardware probe, manual.** `omarchy setup security face` installs `omarchy-faceauth`, fetches and verifies the models, enrols, verifies, and only then wires the lock screen, `sudo` and polkit. Add Look enrols glasses or a hat into the same identity. Removal restores the original PAM files. Menu entries appear only when an IR camera is detected. pr.title: Refuse to run the tailscale and sshd setup commands as root
pr.body: ## Summary - `omarchy-install-service-tailscale` and `omarchy-setup-security-sshd` both escalate via `sudo` internally and act on the desktop user's session, so running them under `sudo` misapplies them to root: sshd writes its authorized key to `/root` and disables password logins system-wide, leaving the desktop user locked out; tailscale sets the Taildrop operator to root, breaking it for the desktop user. - Add the same `EUID == 0` guard already used by thirteen other commands (e.g. `omarchy-install-ai-hermes`, `omarchy-dev-link`) so both scripts refuse to run as root before doing anything. ## Test plan - [x] `./test/shell.d/root-guard-test.sh` — new test asserting both commands exit 1 with the expected message and touch nothing (via `fakeroot` + stubbed PATH) when run as root - [x] `./test/cli` — full pass - [x] `./test/shell` — full pass 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](

pr.title: Keep panel focus during panel switches
pr.body: **Problem:** switching panels with SUPER+CTRL+1-9 briefly gives focus back to the window below, which causes a flickering sensation when moving between panels (e.g. a text box or search bar briefly shown as focused). See attached video. **Cause:** the old panel drops focus before the new panel has appeared. **Fix:** the old panel keeps its surface and focus for an unnoticeable 75 ms (same as `focusPrimeTimer`). See attached video. * Closing a panel _without switching_ still releases focus immediately. **Validation:** switching panels over Chromium no longer flickers (see videos). `./test/all` passes apart from five unrelated files that need `omarchy-pkgs` or `omasnap`, neither of which is on my machine. **Alternative solution:** have the new panel close the old one only once it's on screen. It'd be more precise, but also more complex.

pr.title: Use popup text color for network panel popup content
pr.body: Fixes #12732 ### Problem In `shell/plugins/panels/network/Panel.qml`, elements rendered inside the popup card (hero labels, header buttons, band selection, DNS pills, network rows, passphrase prompt, and info labels) used `root.bar.foreground` instead of `Color.popups.text`. On themes where the bar and popup backgrounds contrast (e.g., Familiar theme with a dark bar / light popup), this caused low contrast or white-on-white text inside the popup. Furthermore, `hoverFill` and `selectedFill` derived from `bar.foreground`. ### Solution - Added `readonly property color popupForeground: Color.popups.text` and `readonly property color urgent: bar ? bar.urgent : Color.urgent`. - Derived `hoverFill` and `selectedFill` from `popupForeground` and `Color.accent`. - Replaced references to `root.bar.foreground` with `root.popupForeground` across the popup card elements, keeping bar widget components intact. - Verified in isolated OMAVM: `./test/shell.d/network-test.sh` passed 102/102, `./test/cli` passed 100%, and visually confirmed live network panel rendering via screenshot.

pr.title: Pre-filter Codex session lines before JSON parsing
pr.body: ### Summary In `bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex`, `scan_native_codex_sessions()` called `json.loads(raw)` on every single line across all `.jsonl` files in `~/.codex/sessions` and `~/.codex/archived_sessions`, even though only lines containing `"turn_context"` (to track model) and `"token_count"` (for token usage) are relevant. In active session files, the overwhelming majority of lines are assistant responses, diffs, tool calls, and user messages, causing unnecessary CPU overhead parsing irrelevant JSON. This PR adds a fast substring pre-filter: ```python if '"token_count"' not in raw and '"turn_context"' not in raw: continue ``` matching the pattern already used by `omarchy-agent-usage-claude` for transcript scanning. Fixes #12702 ### Testing - Ran `test/shell.d/agent-usage-codex-scanner-test.sh` inside OMAVM (QEMU isolated VM), verifying that non-JSON lines and unrelated JSON payloads are skipped while `turn_context` model switching and `token_count` usages are recorded accurately. - Ran `./test/cli` inside OMAVM with 100% pass rate. - Executed `bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex` inside OMAVM and verified valid output schema.

pr.title: Explicitly set text/plain UTF-8 MIME type in omarchy-clipboard-paste-text
pr.body: ## Problem When copying text from clipboard history or directly via `omarchy-clipboard-paste-text`, the helper pipes content to bare `wl-copy` without specifying a MIME type. For certain valid UTF-8 strings (such as Cyrillic text preceded by whitespace, e.g. ` Тест\n`), `libmagic`'s automatic MIME inference misidentifies the payload as binary (`application/x-dtsz`), causing `wl-paste --type text` and GUI text-paste operations to fail or exit with status 1. ## Root cause and fix The history lookup in `omarchy-clipboard-paste-text` already verifies `.[$index].type == "text"`. By explicitly setting `--type "text/plain;charset=utf-8"` on `wl-copy` for both the history and direct text-copy paths, the clipboard content is guaranteed to be advertised as valid UTF-8 text and remains pasteable across all applications. Fixes #12662. ## Verification Tested in a disposable OMAVM guest (Omarchy 4.0.3-1, Hyprland 0.56.2, Quickshell 0.3.1) from the clean `fresh` snapshot: - Added assertions to `test/shell.d/clipboard-test.sh` ensuring `--type "text/plain;charset=utf-8"` is passed to `wl-copy` for both history and direct text paths. pr.body: ## Problem During `omarchy update` (or when running migrations like `migrations/1789581661.sh`), migrations call `omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins` right before `omarchy-bar put ...`. Because migrations execute under `set -euo pipefail`, this aborts on the very first timeout and terminates the entire system update with pending migrations stranded. ## Root cause and fix Treat `*"is not responding"*` as a retriable condition alongside `*"not ready"*` in `ask_to_put`, recording `SHELL_ANSWERED=1` so `omarchy-bar` waits out the busy shell during reload/rebuild rather than failing on the first timeout.
