pr.title: Follow an opened link to the browser window, never an open web app
pr.body: ## Problem With a Chromium web app open (`omarchy-launch-webapp`, e.g. Slack), opening a link through `omarchy-launch-browser` intermittently yanks focus to the **web app** workspace and opens the link in a **second browser window** there, instead of adding a tab to the existing browser window. Two causes, both in `bin/omarchy-launch-browser`: 1. The follow-focus pattern is `^<browser>.*$`, and `omarchy-hyprland-focus-app` takes `first(...)` of `hyprctl clients`. Chromium web apps share the browser's class prefix and only differ by the app id Chromium derives from their URL, so `^brave.*$` also matches `brave-chat.example.com__-Default`. Client order varies between calls, which is why it only misfires *sometimes*: ``` $ hyprctl clients -j | jq -r 'first(.[]|select(.class|test("^brave.*$";"i"))).class' brave-chat.example.com__-Default # the web app, not the browser ``` 2. The follow runs *before* Chromium resolves its target window, and an app window cannot hold tabs. Once the web app is focused, Chromium stops reusing the tabbed window and creates a new browser window, which Hyprland places on the web app's workspace. pr.title: Keep the desktop responsive during AUR source builds
pr.body: ## Summary `omarchy-update` runs AUR source builds (via yay/makepkg) at default process priority with unbounded build parallelism. A heavy source build — e.g. `libsignal-client`'s cargo + cmake stack — can therefore compete head-to-head with foreground apps for the CPU while it compiles: observed on a 4-thread machine, load average reached ~10, PSI cpu `some` sat at ~56%, and interactive apps (editor, terminal, compositor) were effectively frozen until the build finished. This change treats updates as background work: the AUR build step runs at lowered CPU and I/O priority — costless when the machine is otherwise idle — and offers build tools a default job count of half the machine's cores, so a source build stops elbowing interactive apps for the whole machine. The count is delivered through each tool's usual variable (Make, CMake, Cargo) as a default; tools that ignore those variables are not capped, so this is polite backgrounding rather than a hard guarantee. ## Changes - `bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs` - `yay` now runs under `nice -n 15 ionice -c 2 -n 7` (inherited by makepkg, rustc, cc, cmake and ninja) - `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`, `MAKEFLAGS` and `CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL` default

pr.title: Restart media marquee once width bindings settle
pr.body: Fixes #7054. The media bar widget's marquee could freeze with only the first few characters of the title showing, and stay frozen for the lifetime of that track or the shell. `NumberAnimation on x` latches `from`/`to` when it starts. Because `running` was bound to `needsScroll`, the animation could start in the same evaluation pass as the width bindings, while `scrollClip.width` was still `0`, and lock in a `0 → 0` animation. Later track or width changes never reach an animation that is already running. A long → short change also left `x` wherever the animation stopped. This drives the animation imperatively instead: - `restartScroll()` stops the animation, resets `x = 0`, and, if the title needs to scroll, sets `from`/`to`/`duration` from the settled widths and starts it again. - It runs through `Qt.callLater` on text changes, `implicitWidth` changes, scroll-state changes (popup, vertical bar), and on creation. Bursts of changes collapse into one restart after the bindings have settled. ### Verification On 4.0.4-1 / quickshell 0.3.1-1, I tested a clone of the widget in the running shell with `maxLabelWidth` temporarily set to 80 so the current title needed to scroll, then restarte

pr.title: Add Bluetooth file receiving to the Bluetooth panel
pr.body: **What**: the Bluetooth panel gains an **Accept files** switch, and `omarchy-bluetooth-files <on|off|toggle|is-on>` moves the user unit behind it. With it on, a file shared from a paired phone (Android's share sheet → *Bluetooth*) lands in your downloads directory. **Why Object Push**: it is the one file transfer every phone already speaks, so it needs no app on the phone, no Wi-Fi, no mDNS and no vendor protocol. Quick Share is not an option on Linux today (rquickshare can advertise over mDNS, but current Android drops off Wi-Fi while the share sheet is open and looks for BLE receivers), and LocalSend requires installing its app on the phone. **How it works** - `omarchy-bluetooth-files` only moves the unit: `on` is `enable --now`, so the receiver also comes back at the next login; `off` is `disable --now`; `is-on` is the exit code a caller reads instead of parsing systemd output. - `omarchy-bluetooth-files.service` runs `omarchy-bluetooth-files-agent`, an Object Push agent for obexd (bluez-obex). pr.title: Refuse direct boot on Surface firmware
pr.body: `omarchy setup direct boot` already refuses two firmware vendors as unsafe for custom EFI entries. This adds Microsoft/Surface to that list. ```bash *microsoft*) echo "Error: Surface firmware manages its own boot order and may drop custom EFI entries" >&2 exit 1 ;; ``` ## Why Surface firmware manages its own boot order and is known to drop or reorder third-party EFI entries, so the entry the command creates may simply not be honoured. What makes it worse than an entry that does not work is the combination: - **Direct boot bypasses Limine**, which also removes the snapper snapshot menu — the normal recovery path. The command's own prompt notes this ("so snapshot booting must be done via bios"), but on hardware where the created entry may be ignored, that leaves no in-band way back. - **The UKI is unsigned**, so the entry cannot be used with Secure Boot either. On a Surface Go this resulted in an unbootable system and a reinstall. `/sys/class/dmi/id/bios_vendor` reads `Microsoft Corporation` on these devices, so the existing `case` handles it with no new machinery. ## Note The feature's benefit is available on this hardware without the risk: Limine's own `timeout: 0` gives a menu-les

pr.title: Rebuild the IdleMonitor instead of retuning it
pr.body: ## The problem The screen never blanks and never locks. No error is logged anywhere — the idle service looks healthy, the timers just never fire. `omarchy-shell idle status` shows the tell: `"monitorAlive": false` with `"monitorTimeout": 0`, while `screensaver`/`lock` hold their configured values. ## Cause Quickshell's `IdleMonitor` stops delivering notifications permanently once `timeout` is reassigned on a live instance, and toggling `enabled` does not bring it back. `shell.qml` starts `shellConfig` at the built-in defaults and swaps in `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json` once it loads, so the timeout *does* change under a live monitor on every startup where the user has configured `idle`. Editing `idle` values in `shell.json` hits the same path through hot-reload. ## Fix Rebuild the monitor instead of retuning it: the `IdleMonitor` now lives in a `Loader` that is destroyed and recreated when the desired timeout changes. `monitorPlan` in `IdleModel.js` decides the target timeout and whether a replacement is needed, keeping the decision testable and out of QML. ## Tests - New `monitorPlan` cases in `test/shell.d/idle-test.sh` cover building the monitor when idling is enabled, leaving a

pr.title: Add --branch to omarchy plugin add
pr.body: `omarchy plugin add` clones whatever the repository's default branch is, and there is no way to ask for another. Installing a plugin's development branch means skipping the command and cloning into `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/<id>` by hand, which also skips validation and the duplicate-id check. This adds `--branch`: ``` omarchy plugin add --branch dev ``` ## Option-shaped branch names The branch name is handed to `git clone`, so one beginning with `-` would be read as a flag rather than a ref. `omarchy-git-url-check` already closes that hole for the URL, and the same check now runs on the branch before anything is cloned. ## The second commit `omarchy-plugin-update` fetches `origin HEAD`, which is the remote's default branch whatever the checkout is on. A plugin installed with `--branch` would fast-forward onto a different branch, or, where the default branch is an ancestor of the installed one, report success having changed nothing. The second case is the one I hit while testing: the update printed nothing unusual and left the plugin exactly where it was. pr.title: Fix infinite iteration in keybinding scanner API stubs
pr.body: The keybinding menu can spin indefinitely when a user's Lua config iterates an API query such as `ipairs(hl.get_loaded_plugins())`. The scanner's no-op object's `__index` returns itself for every numeric index, so the iterator never sees `nil`. Repeated menu launches can leave multiple Lua processes consuming one CPU core each. Return `nil` for numeric lookups while preserving chained attribute access and calls. This lets query results act as empty lists during the offline scan. The regression test loads a plugin through the stub, iterates the plugin query, then checks that subsequent Lua bindings are still resolved. A five-second timeout bounds the test if the bug returns. Validation: - The new regression times out on the original code and passes with the fix. - `bash test/shell.d/keybindings-menu-test.sh` passes. - The corrected embedded scanner finishes against the affected machine's actual config. - Bash syntax checks and `git diff --check` pass. - `./test/all` completed: CLI passed; 236 of 245 shell test files passed. pr.title: Preserve configured cursors for screenshots on transformed displays
pr.body: When taking a screenshot on a transformed display, `omarchy-capture-screenshot` forces `cursor:no_hardware_cursors = 0` throughout region selection, even when software cursors are configured. This overrides a working cursor configuration during the part of capture that requires accurate pointing. This proposes an automatic, scoped fallback: when any active output is transformed and cursor mode is software (`1`) or automatic (`2`), preserve the cursor configuration and select on the live desktop. The region helper accepts `--no-freeze` while retaining its two-line `--keep-freeze` protocol. Untransformed setups and explicitly configured hardware cursors keep the existing behavior. Tradeoff: content can move during selection, and a software cursor may appear in the capture. The manual documents both. ### Evidence and limits The originating report was an interactive selection offset on a portrait external display, next to a fractionally scaled laptop display. pr.body: ## The problem `BluetoothDevice.batteryAvailable` is BlueZ's `org.bluez.Battery1`, and BlueZ publishes that interface only for peripherals reporting battery over GATT. UPower republishes it with `nativePath` set to `hid-<address>-battery-71`. pr.title: fix(hypr): bind the lid switch by its Apple Silicon device name too
pr.body: `default/hypr/bindings/utilities.lua` binds the lid to the device name `Lid Switch`. Apple Silicon reports its lid as `Apple SMC power/lid events`, so neither bind matches and `omarchy-system-lid-close` never runs on that hardware. Hyprland matches a switch bind by exact string comparison and has no wildcard form. Checked against the v0.56.2 tag: - `CInputManager::newSwitch` passes the raw device name to `onSwitchOnEvent` / `onSwitchOffEvent`. - `onSwitchOnEvent` builds `keyName = "switch:on:" + switchName` verbatim, with no normalization. - `handleKeybinds` compares with `if (key.keyName != k->key) continue;`, a plain `std::string` inequality. No prefix, substring, or case folding. - There is no "any switch" form. `switch:on:` with an empty name is just another literal, and the `catchAll` branch is gated on `key.keyName.empty()`, which never holds for a switch event. - Aquamarine does expose `AQ_SWITCH_TYPE_LID`, but Hyprland's fire listener reads only `event.enable`, so capability matching is not available either. pr.title: Parse keys whose type is spelled out in the keybindings menu
pr.body: A `code:` bind on an F-key or keypad key shows its raw keycode in the `SUPER K` menu — `code:67` instead of `F1` — on every layout, US included. `xkbcli compile-keymap` writes most keys on one line (`key <AE11> { [ minus, underscore ] };`), the only form `parse_keycodes()` matched. Keys with an explicit type put their symbols on a following `symbols[1]= [ … ]` line and never resolved. The US fallback table masked it for the codes Omarchy binds by default. Repro: `xkbcli compile-keymap | grep -A2 'key <FK01>'` shows the long form (21 keys use it on the stock US keymap); bind anything to `code:67` and open the menu. The fix remembers which key block is open and reads the symbols when they arrive. Keys that resolved before resolve identically. The test stubs `xkbcli` with `semicolon` on `code:20` in the long form, so the fallback table can't pass it by accident: fails before, passes after. Cache version bumped. `test/shell.d/keybindings-menu-test.sh` passes. #10468 builds on this. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](

pr.title: Add toggle to keep occupied workspaces numbered consecutively
pr.body: ## What An opt-in toggle (Trigger → Toggle → Consecutive Workspaces, or `omarchy-hyprland-workspace-compact-toggle`) that keeps occupied workspaces numbered 1, 2, 3 … with no gaps. When a workspace empties, the workspaces above it slide down over the hole with their windows, so the order is preserved. Without it, closing the last window on workspace 2 while 3 and 4 are in use leaves the bar reading 1, 3, 4. - The workspace you are on counts as open even when empty. If it is numbered past the next free slot (Super + 7 with only 1-2 in use) you land on the next free number instead. - Special workspaces (scratchpad) are ignored. - Off by default. It follows the existing toggle pattern: `omarchy-hyprland-toggle workspace-compact` copies `default/hypr/toggles/workspace-compact.lua` into `~/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/`. ## Changes - `default/hypr/toggles/workspace-compact.lua`: the compaction logic, run 120 ms after workspace/window events so close and move events settle first - `bin/omarchy-hyprland-workspace-compact-toggle`: toggle command with notification - `default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc`: menu entry next to Workspace Layout - `docs/file-layout.md`: lists the new toggle -

pr.title: omarchy-hibernation-available: return failure when the kernel will refuse to hibernate (#7730)
pr.body: ## Why `omarchy-hibernation-available` returns success even when the kernel has hibernation disabled, so the Hibernate menu entry appears and then silently does nothing when selected (#7730). The old check accepted any machine where `/sys/power/image_size` exists, non-zram swap is larger than the image, and `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/omarchy_resume.conf` exists — all three can pass while the kernel still refuses to hibernate (lockdown, `nohibernate`, secretmem, an active CXL device, or simply no `disk` sleep state). ## What changed `bin/omarchy-hibernation-available` now: - requires `/sys/power/state` to be readable and to list the `disk` sleep state — the kernel only presents `disk` while it will actually accept a hibernation request; - requires `/sys/power/image_size` to be readable and numeric; - reads these files and `/proc/swaps`/the resume config through env-overridable paths (`OMARCHY_SYS_POWER_PATH`, `OMARCHY_SWAPS_PATH`, `OMARCHY_RESUME_CONF_PATH`) so the logic is testable. - Adds `test/shell.d/hibernation-available-test.sh` covering: available vs no-`disk`, a longer state name containing `disk`, unreadable state, `disk`-only kernels, unreadable image size, zram-only swap, sw

pr.title: omarchy-font-set: fire terminal-restart notifications and stop leaking PIDs (#12596)
pr.body: ## Why `omarchy font set "<family>"` never shows the "you must restart your terminal" reminder. Instead it prints stray output: the PIDs of every running `foot`/`ghostty` instance, followed by a usage error from `omarchy-notification-send`. Two bugs in `bin/omarchy-font-set`: 1. `pgrep -x ghostty` / `pgrep -x foot` are used as conditions without redirecting stdout, so the PIDs leak into the user's terminal. 2. `omarchy-notification-send -g "You must restart Foot to see font change"` passes the message as a glyph (`-g` takes a value), leaving the headline and body empty — the helper prints usage and exits 1, and no notification fires. ## What changed - Silence `pgrep` output with `>/dev/null 2>&1` (same pattern already used in `omarchy-display-text-size`). - Call `omarchy-notification-send` with a real headline and body for both Ghostty and Foot restart reminders. - Track the change with a regression test that simulates `pgrep`/`busctl`/`notify-send`, asserts no PIDs reach stdout, that both D-Bus notifications fire with the right summary/body, and that `notify-send` is never invoked directly. ## Verification - `test/shell.d/font-set-notify-test.sh` — passes (5 assertions). - `./test

pr.title: Follow symlink starting points in omarchy-menu-file
pr.body: ## Summary `omarchy-menu-file` ran `find` without following symlink **starting points**, so paths like `~/Videos` / `~/Pictures` on extra disks produced zero files. Transcode never opened the picker because `omarchy-menu-select` got empty stdin. Uses `find -H` so only command-line starting points are followed (not nested symlinks inside the tree). Also bounds listing / menu payload so a huge library cannot blow `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`: - newest 500 files, and - ~80KB total **path bytes** via `LC_ALL=C awk` (byte length under UTF-8 `LANG`, first cut for ordinary valid UTF-8 names), and - `omarchy-menu-select` rejects oversized **encoded** options JSON (`MAX_MENU_OPTIONS_JSON_BYTES=120000`, measured in C-locale bytes) before the Perl/shell IPC hop. Closes #12665. ## Test plan - `test/shell.d/menu-file-symlink-test.sh` stubs `omarchy-menu-select` and asserts a symlink starting point still yields `$link/...` paths (`find` `%p`). - `test/shell.d/menu-select-options-byte-budget-test.sh` checks oversized invalid-UTF-8 options fail closed under `C.UTF-8` with `options payload too large`. - `./test/shell` for those files (no GitHub Actions on this repo). Did not ping maintainers.

pr.title: Accept keypad digits on the lock screen while NumLock is desynced
pr.body: ## Problem Typing a digit on the numeric keypad does nothing in the lock screen's password field. The same digit on the number row types fine. Anyone whose password has digits typed on the keypad has to toggle NumLock off and on at every lock (#8552). ## Cause Qt never reads the compositor's NumLock state at startup (QTBUG-32687). Even with NumLock on, the keypad reaches the field as Home, Up, PageUp and the rest with `Qt.KeypadModifier` set and no text, and `TextInput` treats them as cursor movement. ## Fix Map those keys back to their digits in the field's key handler when `KeypadModifier` is set. Digits that already carry text, the top row and plain cursor keys are untouched, and nothing is inserted while the field is read-only during authentication. pr.title: shell: clamp notification toast width to viewport; battery warning auto-expires
pr.body: ## What Two changes so notification toasts scale correctly on small logical viewports and never become undismissable pin walls: 1. **Toast width clamps to the viewport** (`shell/plugins/notifications/components/NotificationCard.qml`) - `implicitWidth: Math.min(Style.space(380), Math.round(Screen.width * 0.8))` - Keeps the 380px desktop target when there is room; on small logical screens the card now always fits with margins. 2. **Low-battery warning no longer stacks forever** (`bin/omarchy-battery-low`) - `-u critical` → `-u normal`, `-t 30000` → `-t 12000`. ## Why Found on a CM5 mini-Linux box (720x720 panel, scale 1.6 → 450 logical px). The fixed `Style.space(380)` card is 507 logical px wide there (×fontScale 16/12) — literally wider than the screen. Worse: the battery warning is sent as **critical** urgency, and (a) critical toasts get `durationFor() → 0` (no auto-expiry), (b) each threshold flap sends a **new** notification id (no `replaces_id`), and (c) popups are mirrored to disk and restored on shell start. pr.title: Keep PwNode objects out of the audio panel's Repeater models
pr.body: ## Why The audio panel feeds its three `Repeater`s with snapshots of live `PwNode` objects. Quickshell deletes a node the moment PipeWire drops it, and Qt dereferences that row without a null check in `VDMListDelegateDataType::createMissingProperties` (`qqmldmlistaccessordata_p.h:222`, unchanged in Qt 6.11.2) while it builds the delegate. Any teardown that empties the graph with the panel open segfaults the shell: a USB DAC unplugged, a Bluetooth profile switch, `omarchy-restart-audio`, a WirePlumber restart, or a laptop suspend (issue #6952). ## What changed Rows now carry the node's `id` and `name` as primitives instead of the `PwNode` itself, and each delegate resolves its own node through `nodeFor()`, so labels, glyphs and stream volumes stay live. The `name` rides along because PipeWire reuses object ids, and `PwNode.name` is CONSTANT for as long as the node exists — it pins a row to the node it came from. This is the projection the bluetooth panel already uses against the same crash class. - `Model.js` replaces `listSnapshot` with `nodeRow`/`rowSnapshot`. pr.title: Show parallel video downloads with option to cancel
pr.body: Video downloads already run in parallel, but they all update the same progress popup. Users can’t identify individual downloads or cancel them. When downloading multiple videos in parallel, the differing progress percentages override each other, making the progress bar constantly "jump around". This replaces the shared progress bar with a compact popup listing every active download, its title, progress, and a cancel button. Longer lists scroll, while the existing browser button, keyboard shortcut, and completion notifications remain unchanged. Things considered: - Cancellation stops the selected download and its subprocesses during preparation, downloading, or processing, without affecting other downloads. - Private per-download state supports shell restart recovery. Process identity checks and stale-state cleanup prevent cancelling unrelated processes. - Progress updates preserve existing rows so they don’t interrupt button presses or reset scrolling. - The `OMARCHY_PATH` override was removed intentionally, because Chromium's native-host-launcher does preserve the parent environment --- **Screenshots** Before:

pr.title: Install triage-o-mator: tool to manage Issues and PRs (no binary, just plain data)
pr.body: Tooling to work through a GitHub issue / PR backlog too large for one person to read cold: a terminal UI, `triage-o-mator`, on top of a set of small scripts that do the actual work. This does not install the binary. Please read its repo's [README]( It adds the ledger of all pending items, along with categorization for them, groupings to work in this collaboratively, and even final reports. The backlog gets a first pass of categorization done in batches, by you or by an AI Agent, and whoever's triaging gets a fast, git-tracked way to check and correct that first pass before anyone acts on it. It does not modify the live repo. It reads issues and PRs via `gh` and writes categorization decisions to a local ledger. Turning a reviewed decision into an actual label / comment / close on GitHub is a deliberate future step, not something this does automatically. I mostly open this PR here (Ironic?) for testing purposes and as an invitation for adoption of the tool, hoping it brings value to the team (which you should call **Hawks**, btw). To summarize, this is how the whole tool would look as first "installed" into the target repository.

pr.title: Keep UPower rate when sysfs power read fails with ENODEV
pr.body: Single-battery HP/ACPI machines expose a `power_now` that passes `[[ -r ]]` but whose `read()` fails with `ENODEV`, so the script gets `""` and `awk` coerces it to `0W`, discarding UPower's correct `energy-rate` (~16-30W). Only trust numeric sysfs reads, otherwise keep UPower's `energy-rate`. Same guard for the `current_now`/`voltage_now` fallback, which had the identical coerce-to-0 hole. Split out from #6845 per @bjarneo's request — that PR grew to cover 3 failure modes and was closed as a dup of #10392, which only handles multi-battery percentage and keeps this bug. This is the minimal fix for #6895 with regression tests for both empty-read cases. Fixes #6895. Extracted from #6845 (`3c40745`). Verified: existing `battery-status-test.sh` + 2 new ENODEV cases pass.

pr.body: Omarchy installs MIPI camera support automatically for laptops with the Intel IPU7 controller (`install/hardware/intel/ipu7-camera.sh`) and does nothing for IPU6. pr.title: Wake displays before restoring keyboard and clamshell state
pr.body: ## What `omarchy-system-wake` ran three steps sequentially on every wake (idle activity and post-unlock): 1. `omarchy-brightness-display on` — lights the panels (user-visible) 2. `omarchy-brightness-keyboard restore` 3. `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell` — can take seconds on docked setups when it triggers `hyprctl reload` Only step 1 is on the critical path. Steps 2 and 3 now run in the background, so the session is responsive as soon as the displays are lit. Ordering is preserved: DPMS enable still runs first. ## Side-effect fix Both QML callers (`idle/Service.qml` `cancelIdleCycle`, `lock/Service.qml` `runWake`) skip a wake while a previous one is still `running`. A slow clamshell (with reload) used to hold the process open, so a second wake event during that window was dropped entirely — including its DPMS enable. With the script returning fast, every wake lights the display. ## Numbers (this machine: single eDP-1, no kbd backlight) 5 runs each, `omarchy-system-wake` wall time: | | run1 | run2 | run3 | run4 | run5 | median | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Before (sequential) | 171ms | 153ms | 151ms | 151ms | 151ms | ~151ms | | After (display foreground, rest background) | 38

pr.title: Stop counting Hyprland virtual outputs as external monitors
pr.body: Fixes #8027. ## What goes wrong Dock the laptop, turn the laptop screen off (SUPER + CTRL + Delete, or Hardware -> Laptop Display), then unplug the external monitor. The laptop is left with no screen at all until the next login. ## Why When the last enabled monitor goes away, Hyprland creates a placeholder output named FALLBACK (FallbackStateKeeper, src/state/FallbackState.cpp, since 0.56.0). Nothing is behind it, but it reports `disabled: false` and its name is not eDP/LVDS/DSI, so `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-external-active` answered "an external monitor is active". Six callers use that answer to decide whether turning the laptop screen back on is safe, and all six back off: `off()` and `recover()` in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal`, `recover()` in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal-mirror`, `enable_internal()` and the dock check in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell`, and the poll in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-watch`. Only the next login recovers it, because `omarchy-recover-internal-monitor.service` asks `omarchy-hw-external-monitors` instead, which reads the kernel. ## The fix Ask the kernel too: a real display has a DRM connector, a placeholder has none. pr.title: Inhibit idle and screensaver when browsers or video web apps are fullscreen
pr.body: ## Problem Web browsers (Firefox, Chromium-based browsers, and video web apps like Zoom and YouTube) do not reliably inhibit idle under Wayland during fullscreen video calls (e.g., Google Meet, Zoom, Teams), presentations, or media playback. With Omarchy's default `idle.screensaver` timeout (150s), participating in a fullscreen video call triggers the Omarchy screensaver (and later DPMS/lock) mid-call because the user is listening and watching without continuous keyboard or mouse input. Related context: #12579 (which addressed idle inhibition for VLC). ## Fix Add window rules in `default/hypr/apps/browser.lua` setting `idle_inhibit = "fullscreen"` for: - `firefox-based-browser` - `chromium-based-browser` - Video web apps (`youtube.com` / `zoom.us`) While a browser or video web app is in fullscreen mode, Hyprland will inhibit idle so the screensaver and screen lock do not take over. Once the user exits fullscreen, standard idle timing resumes. ## Verification - Validated with `hyprctl reload` and `hyprctl configerrors` (clean, 0 errors). - Confirmed against active Firefox video call window with tag matching. - Ran `./test/cli` (all tests pass cleanly).

pr.title: Keep the idle monitor subscribed while stay-awake is on
pr.body: Fixes #12302. Turning stay-awake off (`omarchy toggle idle allow-idle`) did not re-arm screensaver or lock if the shell had started with stay-awake already on. `omarchy-shell idle status` then reported `enabled:true` while the compositor never sent another idle event. `IdleMonitor.enabled` was bound to `idleEnabled`. That property is false until the stay-awake state file is read, and stays false for the whole session when the file is present. Quickshell's `IdleMonitor` only creates the `ext-idle-notify-v1` notification from `enabled`; a monitor that begins disabled does not re-subscribe when `enabled` later becomes true. Stay-awake still cancels idle cycles and `handleIdleChanged` still ignores events while stay-awake is on. The compositor subscription now stays up so disabling stay-awake can re-arm without restarting the shell.

pr.title: font-set: actually show the terminal restart notification
pr.body: Fixes #12596. `omarchy font set "<family>"` never showed the "you must restart your terminal" notification. It printed stray output instead: the PIDs of every running `foot` window, followed by a usage error from `omarchy-notification-send`. ``` $ omarchy font set "Maple Mono NF CN" 587447 3922164 4002998 Usage: omarchy-notification-send [--app-name <app-name>] [-g <glyph>] ... <headline> [description] [--exec <program> [args...]] ``` Two bugs in the same block: - `-g` takes a value, so the message string was consumed as the glyph and no headline was left. `omarchy-notification-send` then printed its usage and exited 1, making both notification branches dead code. - `pgrep -x ghostty` / `pgrep -x foot` were used as conditions without redirecting stdout, so the PIDs of the running terminals were printed into the user's terminal. The patch restores the font glyph (U+E659) that the pre-standardization `notify-send` call carried, so the toast looks the way it did before 4e2da848. ### Testing - New `test/shell.d/font-set-restart-notification-test.sh` drives the real `bin/omarchy-font-set` with `pgrep` and the D-Bus transport stubbed and the **real** `omarchy-notification-send` on `PATH`

pr.title: Preserve existing Snapper retention policy
pr.body: ## Summary Preserve an existing Snapper root retention policy instead of replacing it with Omarchy's default template. `install/config/snapper.sh` currently creates a root config when one is missing, but then unconditionally installs `default/snapper/root` over `/etc/snapper/configs/root`. During `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`, that can silently replace user-defined retention values such as `NUMBER_LIMIT`, `NUMBER_LIMIT_IMPORTANT`, and `NUMBER_MIN_AGE`. A later Snapper cleanup can then make existing snapshots eligible for deletion under a policy the user never selected, including the pre-upgrade recovery snapshot. pr.title: Accept numpad digits in the menu and image-picker filters
pr.body: Digits typed on a numeric keypad never reach the filter in the Omarchy menu or the image picker. Both handlers gate their printable-character branch on an exact modifier match: ```qml && (event.modifiers === Qt.NoModifier || event.modifiers === Qt.ShiftModifier) ``` Qt sets `Qt.KeypadModifier` on every key originating from the keypad, so `KP_7` arrives as `Qt.Key_7` with `event.text === "7"` and `event.modifiers === Qt.KeypadModifier`. The equality test fails and the keystroke is dropped with no feedback. The number row works because it carries no modifier at all. Match on the modifiers that mean "this is a shortcut" instead. Ctrl, Alt and Meta combinations stay out of the filter; Shift and the keypad get through. Traced from `Keys.onPressed` in the running menu, on a laptop with an embedded numpad and NumLock correctly locked at the compositor: ``` key=0x37 mods=0x20000000 text=[7] the current branch evaluates to false key=0x38 mods=0x20000000 text=[8] the current branch evaluates to false ``` `0x20000000` is `Qt.KeypadModifier`; `0x37` and `0x38` are `Qt.Key_7` and `Qt.Key_8`. pr.body: ## What `stop_screenrecording()` used to SIGINT `gpu-screen-recorder` and then SIGKILL after a flat 5s. Invalid values fall back to 30: non-digits, empty, and digit strings outside 1..5 length; accepted values are forced base-10 and clamped to 1..600. ## Why Reproduce without needing a slow machine: start a recording, `pkill -STOP` the recorder, then `--stop-recording`. Five seconds later the force-kill toast fires and the file is cut. Raising the grace period is the smallest change that matches the reported trailer-write failure mode. Mitigates #12469 (longer post-SIGINT grace). pr.title: Restore ThinkPad keyboard backlight after sleep and boot
pr.body: On ThinkPads the keyboard-light key stays in firmware. It never hits the XF86Kbd bindings, so the level you set there was never saved. Unlock and boot then put 0 back. This watches `tpacpi::kbd_backlight/brightness_hw_changed`, stores that level, and writes it back at login and after resume. Unlock uses the same store, and only for this LED. Other keyboards still use `brightnessctl -r`. Hardware events are ignored while the machine is suspending and for a short settle after resume, so a resume glitch cannot overwrite the saved level with 0. A different level from the firmware key still wins. Needs the settings package so the user unit is installed: The idle-timeout work is separate and is not part of this change. Merge this before the pkgs PR.

pr.title: Enable Num Lock by default on the SDDM login screen
pr.body: The SDDM greeter runs its own minimal Hyprland configuration, which does not enable Num Lock. This leaves keypad users having to enable it when entering their login password, even though Omarchy enables it in the desktop session. Set `input.numlock_by_default = true` in the greeter configuration, using the same comment as the user keyboard configuration template, so Num Lock starts enabled at login as well. Validation: - `luac -p default/sddm/hyprland.lua` passes. - `git diff --check` passes. - Actual login-screen behavior has not been tested; this PR is a draft pending review and runtime validation. Compatibility consideration: #11369 reports that forcing Num Lock on can turn letter keys into keypad input on older Apple keyboards without a physical numpad. This change could extend that existing desktop issue to password entry at login and needs review before merging.

pr.title: Skip Elsewhen migration on unpackaged Omarchy installs
pr.body: ## Summary Migration `1789581661` always runs `omarchy-pkg-add elsewhen`. On WSL/dev checkouts there is no `omarchy` pacman package (`/usr/share/omarchy` is a symlink into the checkout). Because `elsewhen` Depends: `omarchy`, pacman resolves the packaged desktop and conflicts with that symlink, aborting `omarchy update`. The migration marker is never written, so every later update fails the same way. Guard: if `pacman -Q omarchy` fails, skip the migration cleanly (`exit 0`). Fixes #12531 ## Test plan - [x] Harness: unpackaged install mocks — stock migration fails on pkg-add; patched skips with exit 0 (`prs/12531-elsewhen-wsl-migration/smoke-test.sh`) - [ ] WSL install: `omarchy update` after this migration no longer wedges on elsewhen

pr.body: ## Summary Follow-up to #12203. pr.title: Position picture-in-picture from its final size, like webcam overlay
pr.body: ## What Stock `default/hypr/apps/pip.lua` floats Chromium/Firefox PiP, forces `size = { 600, 338 }`, then parks it with: ```lua move = { "(monitor_w-window_w-40)", "(monitor_h*0.04)" } ``` Hyprland evaluates `window_w` / `window_h` from the **client's original size**, then applies `size`. Chromium PiP often opens around 200px wide, so on a 1440-wide panel that becomes: - x = 1440 − 200 − 40 = **1200** - resize to 600px - right edge at **1800** → **360px hanging off the right** (about half the overlay) This is a kit-wide rule, but it is much more obvious on a lower-res older MacBook Air (this was reproduced on a 2015 Air, eDP-1 1440×900 @ 1x). On a 2560 or 4K display the same ~360px overflow is a small corner nibble that is easy to miss. `default/hypr/apps/webcam-overlay.lua` already avoids this: it inlines the same size math in both `size` and `move` instead of using `window_w`. This PR copies that pattern for PiP and the Meet overlay. ```lua move = { "(monitor_w-600-40)", "(monitor_h*0.04)" } ``` Verified on the same 1440×900 Air with a 200×112 GTK window titled `Picture-in-Picture`: | | x | size | right edge | vs 1440 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Before | 1200 | 600×338 |

pr.title: Add an optional macOS transition welcome wizard
pr.body: People moving from macOS need a clear path to iCloud Drive, Photos, email, local files, and Omarchy’s keyboard-first desktop. This adds an optional seven-step welcome wizard under **Setup → Welcome**, also available through `omarchy setup welcome`. The wizard creates removable iCloud web-app shortcuts, opens existing desktop tools, explains file and mail migration, and saves a local checklist that can be resumed or exported. Apple sign-in stays on Apple’s website. Drive and Photos provide web access; native mounting and background synchronization are outside this version. The implementation uses Python’s standard library and local HTML/CSS/JavaScript, with no runtime build step or remote assets. Its loopback API uses a per-session token, validates Host and write Origin, and dispatches only fixed desktop actions. There is no automatic first-boot launch, package installation, keyboard remapping, credential collection, or change to Apple security settings. A manual page and backend regression tests are included. ### Validation - 14 upstream backend tests and JavaScript syntax checks pass through `./test/shell.d/welcome-test.sh`. - Upstream CLI routing and command metadata tests pass.

pr.title: Prompt about unauthorized Thunderbolt devices
pr.body: ## What When a Thunderbolt device connects unauthorized (BIOS security level `user`/`secure`), its USB ports stay silently dead — power delivery and displays keep working, so the failure is invisible. Proposal discussion: #12508. ## Why explicit-only #934's blanket auto-authorize was rejected over the DMA exposure. pr.title: Keep the keyboard backlight level across lock and suspend
pr.body: ## What's wrong The keyboard backlight goes off and never comes back. Turning it on by hand doesn't help — the next wake turns it off again. ## How it's meant to work Locking blanks the backlight: 1. Remember the current level (`brightnessctl -s`) 2. Set it to 0 Waking puts it back: 3. Restore the remembered level (`brightnessctl -r`) That is correct, as long as step 1 only ever runs while the light is actually on. ## Why it breaks Step 1 remembers **whatever it finds** — including 0. So a blank that runs while the light is already off remembers 0. After that, "restore the remembered level" means "set it to 0". Every time. Nothing ever writes a good value back, so it never heals on its own. So the whole bug reduces to one question: **can a blank ever run while the light is already off?** ## Yes — and only one path does it A blank is normally preceded by a wake, and a wake restores the light. So the light is on when the blank runs. Fine. Four places schedule a blank: | | what it is | wake before it? | |---|---|---| | `:146` | you lock the screen | yes — you were just using the laptop | | `:181` | you touch the lock screen | yes — `runWake()` ran first | | `:551` | a password attempt

pr.title: fix: write Hermes bootstrap marker after headless install
pr.body: Fixes #12206 `omarchy install ai hermes` sets up the runtime with the packaged hermes-desktop `install.sh --skip-setup`. That path never writes `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/.hermes-bootstrap-complete`. Omarchy's own readiness check (`omarchy-install-hermes-cli --check`) requires that file, so `omarchy-theme-set-hermes --activate` and the one-shot migration `1788619462.sh` keep saying Hermes isn't ready even when the install works. Windows `install.ps1` already stamps the same marker; this closes the gap on the Omarchy headless path. - Stamp `.hermes-bootstrap-complete` after a usable headless runtime is in place (same schema as `install.ps1` / `writeBootstrapMarker()`, without `desktopVersion`). - Shared helper `omarchy-stamp-hermes-bootstrap` used by the installer. - Migration `1789746834.sh` backfills the marker on already-usable installs that are only missing the file (does not re-run `install.sh`). Tests: `hermes-desktop-install-test.sh`, `hermes-bootstrap-migration-test.sh` (plus related hermes cli/theme/migration tests). Stubbed `--skip-setup` leaves no marker; Omarchy stamps a valid one; `--check` passes; migration is a no-op without desktop/usable runtime and is idempotent.

pr.title: List each plugged-in jack of a multi-port sink as its own audio output
pr.body: Analog cards usually drive the rear Line Out and the front Headphones as ports of a single sink. The audio panel lists sinks, so both jacks showed up as one entry ("ALCS1200A Analog" here), and switching between them meant opening pavucontrol. The panel now lists each plugged-in port of a multi-port sink as an output of its own: - Picking a port sets the default sink and switches it to that port, so Line Out and Headphones can be chosen directly. WirePlumber already keeps a volume per port, so the slider follows the jack. - An unplugged jack drops out of the list, the same way unavailable sinks already do. - Sinks with a single port (HDMI, Bluetooth, USB) are listed exactly as before, and so is a sink with nothing plugged in. pr.title: Drop destroyed PipeWire nodes from the audio panel fallback cache
pr.body: Fixes #12330. `audioSinks` falls back to `cachedAudioSinks` when `rawAudioSinks` is empty. That fallback fires exactly when PipeWire has dropped every node — wireplumber restarting or dying — so the cache hands the Repeaters `PwNode`s that are already being destroyed. Nothing keeps them alive: the `PwObjectTracker`s track `candidateSinks`/`candidateSources`, not the cache. The Repeater regenerates delegates over freed objects and the shell takes a SIGSEGV in `libQt6QmlModels`. The 75 ms `audioModelRefreshTimer` is not the bug. It only defers the stale array long enough for the objects to be gone by the time delegates are built. Filter the fallback against the live node list. `indexOf` compares identity, so a dropped entry is never dereferenced to decide whether it survived. ## Testing Machine: Lenovo LOQ 15IRX9, i7-14700HX, i915 + RTX 4060, kernel `7.2.5-3-omarchy`, Omarchy 4.0.4, quickshell 0.3.1-1, qt6-declarative 6.11.2-1, pipewire 1:1.6.8-1, wireplumber 0.5.17-1. pr.title: network: keep passphrase prompt focused through scan reorders
pr.body: Fixes #11363 ## Problem The inline Wi-Fi passphrase prompt loses focus while typing because `syncWifiNetworks()` unconditionally rebuilds `wifiNetworks` on every scan tick. Reassigning the array reorders the model, and the `ListView` recycles the row holding the open `TextField`, dropping focus and losing whatever had been typed. The existing keyboard freeze (`PanelKeyCatcher.blocked: root.passwordSsid !== ""`) already protects keyboard navigation while a prompt is open, but nothing froze the underlying data path. ## Fix Mirror that same freeze on the data path, in `syncWifiNetworks()`: skip rebuilding `wifiNetworks` while a passphrase prompt is open and no connect attempt has started yet (`passwordSsid !== "" && actionKind === ""`). Once the user submits the password and `actionKind` becomes `"connect"`, syncing resumes so `checkActionCompletion()` can still detect success/failure. When the prompt closes (submitted or cancelled), `onPasswordSsidChanged` triggers one `syncWifiNetworks()` call to catch up on anything deferred while it was open. ## Testing - Added a regression test to `test/shell.d/network-test.sh` asserting `syncWifiNetworks()` defers the update while a prompt is op

pr.title: Fix recording indicator stuck 'active' after a force-killed stop
pr.body: ## Summary `stop_screenrecording()` called `toggle_screenrecording_indicator` while `gpu-screen-recorder` could still be alive — after the 5s SIGINT grace loop but before the `pkill -9` fallback. On a force-kill the refresh therefore read `recording=true` right before the process died, and nothing refreshed again, leaving the bar indicator stuck 'active'. Once stuck, every later click ran `--stop-recording`, which hit `elif [[ $STOP_RECORDING == "true" ]]; then exit 1` — a silent exit with no refresh, so the button stayed dead until something else happened to call `omarchy.indicators refresh`. This is the script-side half of #9205: the QML watchdog fixed in #9296 covers `statusProc` never completing; this covers the probe completing at the wrong moment. Complementary, not overlapping. Changes: - Refresh the indicator **after** the kill/finalize decision is final in `stop_screenrecording()` - Refresh before `exit 1` on a redundant `--stop-recording`, so a desynced click self-heals #### Test plan - [x] New regression coverage in `test/shell.d/screenrecording-test.sh`: asserts the `pkill -9` precedes `omarchy.indicators refresh` on the force-kill path, the error notification still pos

pr.title: Drop redundant height bindings that loop in panel delegates
pr.body: Fixes the QML binding loops reported in #11099. ## Root cause Four items inside a `Column` bind their own `height` back to their `implicitHeight` in order to collapse when hidden: ```qml height: visible ? implicitHeight : 0 ``` `Column` already excludes children with `visible: false` from layout, so the binding adds nothing the layout does not already do — the intent stated in the comment ("Collapses to zero height when empty so rows without status keep a tight one-line look") is fully satisfied by `visible` alone. What the binding does add is a cycle. For the status `Text` in the network panel, `elide: Text.ElideRight` makes `implicitHeight` depend on layout, and binding `height` back to it closes the loop. For the section headers and the separator the chain runs through the delegate: ``` Item.height -> delegateColumn.implicitHeight -> child heights -> child.height -> child.implicitHeight ``` QML breaks such cycles by keeping whichever intermediate value it reached, so it usually renders correctly — but the resolved height is order-dependent. pr.title: Scale Battle.net to the focused monitor
pr.body: Battle.net comes up tiny on any scaled monitor. On a 4K display at scale 2 the whole client draws at half size. Reported in #10669. ## Why it happens Omarchy sets `xwayland:force_zero_scaling`, so XWayland windows are left unscaled and each X11 app sizes its own UI (GTK gets `GDK_SCALE` for this). Wine draws at 96 DPI unless the prefix's `LogPixels` says otherwise, and nothing sets it for the Battle.net prefix. Setting `LogPixels` by hand often appears not to work, which is what #10669 ran into. Wine fixes the DPI for the life of a prefix session. Battle.net is a Qt shell around CEF: CEF re-reads the system DPI on each client start, but Qt takes the monitor DPI the session began with, and Qt decides the UI size. Blizzard's `Agent.exe` keeps the session alive long after the client window closes, so "restarting Battle.net" reuses the old session. Battle.net's own log shows it: `[HighDpiManager] Detected screen ... devicePixelRatio=1` on every start until the whole session is restarted, then `devicePixelRatio=2`. ## The change New hidden helper `omarchy-games-battlenet-scale`: - Wanted DPI is the focused monitor's scale (via `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling`) times 96. pr.title: Install rtkit so PipeWire gets realtime priority
pr.body: Fixes #9390 ## Summary Omarchy ships the full PipeWire stack but not `rtkit`. PipeWire requests realtime scheduling from RealtimeKit over D-Bus at startup; with the service absent, every `mod.rt` request fails (`RTKit error: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown`) and all data-loop threads run at `SCHED_OTHER` nice 0. The fallback paths are also absent on a stock install: no `LimitRTPRIO` in the shipped user units, no `realtime-privileges` group, empty `limits.d`. The result is audio xruns/crackling under sustained CPU/GPU load — invisible at idle, which is what makes it so hard to trace. ## Changes - **`install/omarchy-other.packages`**: add `rtkit` next to the pipewire family — covers fresh installs - **`migrations/1789747667.sh`**: repair existing installs — install `rtkit` via `omarchy-pkg-add` and restart the running audio units so PipeWire's priority request succeeds without a reboot. pr.title: feat(sleep): opt-in suspend battery floor for laptops without hibernation
pr.body: ## Summary Suspend alone has no floor: lid-shut in a bag drains until the battery is flat (and on boards with battery-backed RTCs, the clock stops too). New opt-in `omarchy battery-floor setup` for machines where hibernation won't work. - New `default/systemd/system-sleep/battery-floor` hook. A lid-shut, undocked suspend arms a 20min RTC self-wake (`rtcwake -m no -s 1200`, matching the lid-close suspend-then-hibernate delay). An early wake keeps the countdown where it was and re-arms the time left, so a machine that stirs on a timer shorter than the grace period still reaches the floor instead of postponing it forever. At expiry the decision is deferred to a transient `systemd-run` unit ordered `After=suspend.target`: logind refuses a new action while the original suspend job is in progress, and this hook runs inside that job. The unit powers off on battery, suspends again on AC, and stands down with the lid open or docked (clamshell, same rule as `omarchy-system-lid-close`). Hibernate resumes are untouched; inert without a battery; all lid/AC detection goes through the existing `omarchy-hw-*`/`omarchy-power-present` helpers, no hardcoded device names. - New `omarchy battery-floor

pr.title: lock: stop fingerprint scans while the display is blanked
pr.body: ## What and why While a display is blanked, the lock screen keeps the fingerprint reader running scan cycles against an empty pad. On fingerprint readers that thermally self-disable (Broadcom CV3 / `0a5c:5843`, Goodix `27c6:533c`, Elan `04f3:0c4b`, all `libfprint-tod`), that cycles the driver into `Device disabled to prevent overheating` refusals: 31,534 `PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL` / code 9 returns in under four hours on a CV3, in a 205 s-refusing / 122 s-available cycle. Each refusal re-arms the 250 ms retry timer, so the reader stays in the storm. This PR stops new scans while the display is blanked and re-arms on wake. With it, a CV3 logged **0 refusals across a 15-minute lock** and read on the first touch after wake ([measurement thread](/omacom/omarchy/pull/12201#issuecomment-5721534266)). ## Changes (gating, purely additive vs stock) - `runBlank()`: stop `fingerprintRetryTimer` so a blanked display is not re-arming scan cycles - `startFingerprint()`: return early while `displaysBlank` (single call site; every trigger goes through it) - `runWake()`: re-arm a scan **only when the display was actually blank** (`wasBlank`), so fingerprints do not restart on every pointer move or key p

pr.title: Replace eval with quote-aware word split in omarchy-launch-or-focus
pr.body: ## Summary The launch path in `omarchy-launch-or-focus` passed the caller-supplied launch command through `eval exec setsid `, so any shell metacharacter in the string was executed, not just word-split. The PR adds a quote-state validator (`launch_command_is_safe`) that walks the string character by character, tracking quote state and word boundaries, and rejects a launch command containing unquoted separators (`; | & ( ) < >`), comment starters, backticks, or a $ that starts anything but a variable name. A validated string can then only word-split, expand variables, and glob when parsed, so dangerous or malformed strings are refused with an error before anything runs: ```bash launch_command_is_safe "" || { echo "Refusing to launch: ..." >&2 exit 1 } eval "set -- " exec setsid "$@" ``` Quoting and $HOME/~ expansion semantics match the previous eval exactly; only strings that could run a second command are now refused. ## Tests `test/shell.d/launch-or-focus-test.sh` (new) mocks `hyprctl`/`setsid` and covers every real caller format: - `uwsm-app -- foot`, `omarchy-launch-tui zsh -c 'fastfetch; read -k 1'` (menu/TUI wrapper) - quoted paths with spaces, Lua `shell_quote` escaping (`'it

pr.title: fix(imv): open AVIF, HEIF, and JXL files
pr.body: Omarchy copies its own imv.desktop into ~/.local/share/applications, where it shadows the entry shipped by the imv package. Ours names six image types; the packaged one also names AVIF, HEIF, and JXL. Since the user-level copy wins the XDG lookup, imv drops out of the candidate list for every type it does not name, and those files open in whatever else is installed. On my machine an AVIF landed in qView; without qView the next candidates are GIMP and the browser. imv decodes all three today through the libheif and libjxl it already links against, so this is purely a declaration gap. This adds the types to the shadowing entry and makes imv their default, matching the other image types. image/heic gets its own line even though shared-mime-info aliases it to image/heif: on Hyprland, xdg-open takes its generic path and classifies files with file --mime-type, which says image/heic for phone photos and heif-enc output, and xdg-mime query default matches that name literally without resolving aliases. pr.title: Add a hardware-matched Blackwell/audio compatibility profile
pr.body: ## Scope Draft a narrowly matched installation/update compatibility profile for the tested B650I / RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell / Arctis Nova Pro Wireless combination. This proposes a reusable workaround bundle rather than asking each affected user to reconstruct local settings. It is **not a confirmed root-cause fix for NVIDIA stalls**, and the automatic rollout is not ready for release yet. ### Changes - Add `omarchy setup blackwell-audio status|on|off|auto` and invoke `auto` from per-user installation and an existing-user migration. - Match board/BIOS/CPU, GPU PCI ID, headset USB ID, the specific tested package versions, and the running kernel. An old kernel package left installed is not sufficient. Do not depend on bus addresses or DRM card ordering. Unmatched hardware/software is a no-op. - Retain the tested 48 kHz / 1024-frame audio scheduling margin, output-only headset IRQ scheduling/ALSA buffering, and native-Wayland/ANGLE-GL Chromium video-decode fallback. pr.body: `prioritize_entries` ends with `sort -k1,1n -k2,2` (`bin/omarchy-menu-keybindings:504`), and that sort decides the order of every row in the keybindings cheatsheet. pr.title: Let the menu selector return an option's index
pr.body: `omarchy-menu-select` answers with the text of the row the menu displayed. Clicking the shell update affordance opens a floating terminal whose first interaction is a yes/no prompt. `gum confirm` never enables mouse reporting, so the Yes/No boxes look like buttons but ignore clicks. `omarchy-confirm` is an inline fzf yes/no widget. pr.title: Toggle a touchpad's mouse-emulation sibling with it
pr.body: Fixes #12339. `omarchy-hw-touchpad` returns the first `touchpad|trackpad` node, and the toggle applied `hl.device` to that name only. I2C precision touchpads also expose a kernel mouse-emulation node (`msft0001:00-093a:0255-mouse` next to `...-touchpad`). Leaving it enabled after a toggle produces the 1-finger-dead / 2-finger-move / 3-finger-scroll state. The toggle now looks up a `-mouse` sibling that shares the same base name, applies enable/disable to both, and persists both names so `disabled-input-device.lua` re-applies them on reload. Unrelated mice are left alone. `on` re-enables the names `off` saved, then whatever the current device list still shows, so a later `hyprctl devices` failure does not leave the saved sibling disabled. The sibling is chosen by name. On some touchpad-plus-pointing-stick controllers the stick's events share that `-mouse` node, and udev's pointing-stick tag does not separate them for I2C `*Mouse` nodes. Turning the touchpad off can turn that stick off until the touchpad is turned back on. pr.title: Declare which command output is parsed, and gate it
pr.body: Some Omarchy commands print text for a person to read. Others print a value another program parses. The two look identical in the source, and nothing in the tree says which is which — so the first person to mark strings for translation has to guess, and a wrong guess fails silently. Here is the live example, no hypothetical: ```bash $ omarchy-dns Custom ``` `default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc` decides which DNS provider shows as selected by comparing against that word. Hand `Custom` to a translator and they will translate it — it is an ordinary English adjective with nothing marking it as load-bearing. After that the DNS menu shows no provider selected, on a machine whose DNS is working fine. No test fails, no command exits non-zero, nothing appears in a log. The only symptom is a radio button that is never on. This PR adds no i18n. It records the boundary so that the i18n work arriving in #8765, #10776, #10949 and #10955 has something to check itself against. #12345 is the design proposal this pairs with; it stands or falls separately, and this PR is useful either way. ## What it adds `test/shell.d/i18n-parse-boundary.txt` — 16 commands, each with a kind and the vocabulary it emit

pr.title: Make the menu search line a real text input
pr.body: The menu's search line cannot be typed into with a CJK input method. Composing Chinese, Japanese or Korean through fcitx5 either drops the text or leaves the raw Latin keysyms behind: typing the bopomofo for 你好 fills the filter with `su3cl3`, so the menu cannot be searched in those languages. pr.title: Clear setgid when hardening Windows VM directories
pr.body: Fixes #9334 ## Problem `omarchy windows vm launch` exits 1 with no output whenever `~/Windows` (or `~/.windows`) is setgid. From the app menu nothing happens after the polkit prompt. `prepare_caller_mounts` runs `chmod 0700` on both sources and then requires the mode to be exactly `700`. A numeric `chmod` keeps setuid/setgid on directories, so `2700` stays `2700` and the check fails: ``` $ mkdir d && chmod 2700 d && chmod 0700 d && stat -c %a d 2700 ``` This is not an exotic setup: `dockurr/windows` sets the bit itself. `/run/samba.sh` in the container runs `chmod 2777` on `/shared` when it is empty, which is the state of `~/Windows` on a fresh install. The next launch that has to recreate the bind anchors (any reboot) then fails. ## Changes - Harden with `chmod u=rwx,go=,a-s` at both sites (`prepare_caller_mounts` and `prepare_user_mount_sources`), which also drops a sticky bit. pr.title: apple: rebind brcmfmac across suspend
pr.body: ## Problem On Macs whose Wi-Fi is driven by `brcmfmac` (BCM4350 and relatives), a long suspend wedges the Broadcom firmware. After wake the kernel logs `brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd: Timeout on response for query command` for every request, NetworkManager sees `do-change-link: failure 5 (Input/output error)`, and the interface never recovers — only a reboot brings Wi-Fi back. Short suspends (seconds) resume fine; the failure shows up after hours asleep. Observed on a MacBook10,1 (BCM4350, `14e4:43a3`): suspended 16:53, resumed 19:55, firmware dead from the first msgbuf command after wake. ## Fix A `systemd/system-sleep` hook unbinds the Wi-Fi PCI device from `brcmfmac` before sleep and rebinds it after wake, forcing a clean firmware reload. NetworkManager then sees a fresh interface and reconnects on its own (~seconds after wake). Devices unbound at `pre` are recorded under `/run` and only those are rebound at `post`; a `post` with no matching `pre` is a no-op. ## Gating Mirrors `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`: T2 Macs via the T2 PCI ID, older Macs via the `brcmfmac` PCI IDs from `brcm_hw_ids.h`. pr.title: Fix silent speakers on 12-inch MacBook (CS4208)
pr.body: ## Problem On the 12-inch MacBook (MacBook9,1 / MacBook10,1) the internal speakers are completely silent out of the box. Headphones work; every mixer looks fine; PipeWire shows an active sink — and nothing comes out. `manual/44-mac-support.md` currently lists "Sound is not functioning" as a known Mac limitation. Additionally, once speakers do work, **audio dies after every suspend/resume** and only a reboot brings it back. ## Root cause The Cirrus Logic CS4208 codec's speaker amplifier is never powered by the in-tree driver: the HDA controller reports a **generic PCI subsystem ID** (`8086:7270`), so `snd_hda_codec_cs420x` matches no Apple fixup and probes with `speaker_outs=0` (only the headphone jack `0x10` is wired through the analog DAC). Mainline has no working speaker config for this codec. Four independent things are required for sound to actually come out — and stay out: 1. **The out-of-tree driver** — [leifliddy/macbook12-audio-driver]( replays the codec init (reverse-engineered from macOS) that powers the amp. 2. **The EFI startup chime un-muted** in NVRAM. pr.title: Ask the multiplexer where the focused pane is
pr.body: Fixes #12282. `omarchy-cmd-terminal-cwd` resolves the directory behind *File manager (cwd)*. Outside the kitty path it takes the terminal's last direct child, reads `/proc/<pid>/cwd`, and discards it unless that child's exe is in `/etc/shells`. Both multiplexers Omarchy ships defeat that, each in its own way: - `omarchy-launch-terminal-tmux` (`SUPER + ALT + RETURN`) runs `bash -c "tmux attach || tmux new -s Work"`, so the last direct child is `bash` — listed in `/etc/shells`, so its launch directory is returned confidently and wrongly, while the pane's shell lives under a server that is reparented to `systemd --user` and is not in the window's process tree at all. - `omarchy-launch-terminal-herdr` (`SUPER + CTRL + RETURN`) runs `herdr` directly, so the last direct child is the client itself: its cwd is readable, and the `/etc/shells` check is what throws it away. In the tmux case no amount of child-walking reaches the pane. pr.title: Show the Claude usage-credit allowance in the agents panel
pr.body: Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint returns a `spend` object beside the rate limit windows. It is the monetary credit allowance Claude Code's own `/usage` screen draws, and it fills up the way a window does: a percentage of a cap, refilled with the billing month. The Claude collector already has that payload in hand when it reads the windows and dropped the object, so an account spending against its credits could sit at 100% of them with nothing in the panel to say so. This reads it as one more window. The collector carries the amounts and the panel formats them, the way the prepaid balance section already splits that work. `spend` carries no reset stamp of its own; credits refill monthly, so the window resets on the first of the coming month, dated in the offset that day carries rather than today's. ## Three ways it is not a rate limit window - **The bar icon's alarm passes over it.** Running credits down returns the account to its rate limit windows rather than stopping the next prompt, and a month-long window at 100% would hold the bar in alarm for weeks over money already spe

pr.body: After waking from suspend, the bar clock keeps showing the time from before the lid was closed, for up to a minute. `SystemClock` schedules its next tick with a `QTimer`, which runs on the monotonic clock and doesn't advance during suspend. pr.title: Trust battery device state over UPower.onBattery
pr.body: Fixes #12005. The power widget derived charging and discharging from the daemon-wide `UPower.onBattery` flag and ignored `displayDevice.state`. That is wrong when the battery is discharging on AC — a Dell charge limit draining toward its threshold, or Asahi's stale tps6598x `online=1` after unplug — so the bar kept the charging icon, "Charging" / "Time to full", and the charging hero phrases while the battery was draining. Device state now wins for the icon, the mode label, and the panel's charging and discharging bindings: - `Discharging` shows the on-battery icon, "On battery" / "Time left", and the on-battery hero, even when `UPower.onBattery` is still false. - `Charging` shows the charging icon, "Charging" / "Time to full", and the charging hero, even when `UPower.onBattery` is still true. `UPower.onBattery` is still what we pass to `omarchy-powerprofiles-set` and to the charge-threshold detector. This reverses 924254ed ("Update battery icon promptly on power changes"), which preferred `UPower.onBattery` so plugging in showed charging before the battery state refreshed. pr.title: Keep the screensaver up until it has been focused once
pr.body: Fixes #12225. `omarchy-screensaver` polled `hyprctl activewindow` once a second and exited as soon as the screensaver was not focused. The first poll can land while the screensaver is not the active window, so it opens and immediately closes. The idle service then treats that close as a user dismissal and cancels the pending lock timer, so neither screensaver nor lock actually happens. The watchdog now remembers whether the screensaver has been the active window. Unfocused polls before that are ignored. Losing focus after that still dismisses, as does a keypress. A manual launch that never receives focus exits after about eight seconds. An idle-cycle launch (`omarchy-launch-screensaver --idle`) does not: the idle service would treat that exit as a dismissal and cancel the lock. Verified with a sourced unit test against a stub `hyprctl`. I did not idle this session to watch a live cycle, because that would blank the display and race the lock.

pr.title: Merge menu extensions before filling unspecified fields
pr.body: Fixes #12236. Fixes #11509. Fixes #11211. Fixes #10007. `omarchy-menu.jsonc` says reusing a shipped id keeps existing fields unless they are overridden. `mergeMenuSources` already did a field-wise merge, but `parseMenuJsonc` ran `normalizeItem` on each source first, so omitted `icon`, `label`, and `when` arrived as `""` (or the raw id, for `label`) and overwrote the stock values. The live menu now parses sources raw and normalizes once after the merge. An extension that only changes `action` keeps the shipped icon, label, and guards; an explicit empty string still clears a field. Kind is inferred from `action` then `target`, so converting an action into a link also needs `"action": ""`. The object key is the id; an `id` field inside the entry is ignored. Verified with the menu model tests, including action-only overrides of Logout and Hibernate, a label-only override of the shipped DNS rows, and an `id` field that must not hijack the object key.

pr.title: Schedule logout with systemd-run like reboot and shutdown
pr.body: Logout was scheduling `uwsm stop` with `nohup … &`. Reboot and shutdown already schedule the actual action with `systemd-run --user --on-active=2s` so it outlives the caller. Logout now does the same, and aborts before the OSD and before closing windows if scheduling fails. #12233 reports that menu > System > Logout shows the OSD and closes windows but never stops the session. That path runs `omarchy-system-logout` through Quickshell's `execDetached` inside the compositor cgroup, not in a terminal scope that is torn down when the script exits. This change does not demonstrate that the reported menu failure is fixed. #12233 should stay open until the menu path is confirmed. It does remove any dependence on the caller's lifetime, which is the failure mode for a terminal whose scope is stopped. I have not logged out of a live session to confirm either path. The power-command tests cover logout the same way they cover reboot and shutdown, and they stub `uwsm`, `systemctl`, and `omarchy-osd` so a run cannot stop the session or toast the desktop.

pr.body: Some installs carry Neovim treesitter query symlinks pointing into the retired omarchy-lazyvim package build dir (/src/omarchy-lazyvim/...). pr.title: List local audio outputs before network ones in the audio panel
pr.body: ## Problem The audio panel's output list follows PipeWire node registration order. When network outputs are present — AirPlay receivers from `module-raop-discover`, or `module-zeroconf-discover` tunnels — they are registered as soon as mDNS discovery finds them, which is usually before WirePlumber has brought up the local sound card. The built-in speakers then end up at the bottom, under a row of remote receivers (two Sonos speakers, in my case), and are the last thing you reach with the keyboard. ## Change - `Model.js`: add `isNetworkSink(node)` (matches the `raop_sink.`, `tunnel.` and `tunnel-sink.` node-name prefixes those modules use) and `sortSinks(list)`, a stable partition that keeps local sinks first and network sinks after them, preserving registration order within each group. - `Panel.qml`: run the available sinks through `sortSinks` before the existing "unshift the default if it is missing" step, so that behaviour is unchanged. - `test/shell.d/audio-test.sh`: cover detection and ordering, including that Bluetooth sinks stay in the local group. ## Testing - `./test/shell`: all files pass except `unowned-system-paths-test.sh`, which needs a sibling `omarchy-pkgs` checkout

pr.title: Fix SNI tray icons disappearing on shell restart
pr.body: Fixes #12214. When `omarchy-shell` restarts, Quickshell's `StatusNotifierWatcher` is destroyed along with the shell process. Already-running tray applications do not necessarily re-register their `StatusNotifierItem`, causing their icons to disappear from the new shell even though the applications are still running. ### Solution Introduce a standalone persistent `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` implemented with PyGObject/Gio and managed as a systemd user service for the graphical session. The watcher registry is now independent of the `omarchy-shell` UI lifetime: * `omarchy-sni-watcher` owns the persistent `StatusNotifierWatcher`. * `omarchy-shell` acts as the `StatusNotifierHost`. * Shell restarts no longer destroy the SNI registry. * When the shell reconnects, it can read `RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` from the existing watcher and restore the tray immediately. * Item and host registrations are tracked against their D-Bus service lifetime and removed automatically when the service disappears. * Repeated registrations are idempotent. * Path-form registrations used by some SNI/AppIndicator clients are handled by separating the originating bus name from the registered object path. pr.title: Show weather wind speed in m/s where that is the local convention
pr.body: The weather panel shows wind in km/h everywhere outside imperial countries, but much of the metric world reports wind in m/s: the Nordics, the Baltics, Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Czechia, China, Japan, and South Korea. Those countries now show m/s. The unit follows the same inference as `useImperial`: the country wttr.in reports takes precedence, falling back to the system locale's territory when no country is known yet (e.g. before wttr answers, or if it fails). Imperial still wins, so mph is unchanged. Everywhere else stays on km/h. The m/s value is converted from the existing km/h field at display time with one decimal, since whole m/s steps are coarse (1 m/s is 3.6 km/h). Neither fetch changes, so it works for both the wttr.in and Open-Meteo sources. The country name normalization is pulled out of `countryUsesImperial` so both lists share it. The right-click notification now matches the panel: `omarchy-weather-status` takes `--meters-per-second`, which the widget passes when the panel shows m/s, and converts wttr's km/h wind the same way (`↗14km/h` becomes `↗3.9m/s`). pr.title: fix(shell): PanelToolTip renders long text on one unbounded line
pr.body: ### The problem `shell/Ui/PanelToolTip.qml` sets `contentItem` to a bare `Text` with no `wrapMode` and no width constraint. Whatever a widget passes as `text` is laid out on a **single line** at whatever width it asks for. A long tooltip therefore runs off the edge of the screen. A bar widget anchored to the right has nowhere to run to, so the overflow lands off-display where it cannot be read at all. Every bar plugin inherits this, since `tooltipText` flows straight through `WidgetButton` into this component. ### The fix Cap the **control**, not the `Text`: ```qml property real maximumWidth: Style.space(320) width: Math.min(implicitWidth, maximumWidth) ``` `ToolTip.implicitWidth` still derives from the unwrapped text, so `Math.min()` reads a value that does not depend on the width it sets and no binding loop forms. The control then hands the `Text` its width, and `wrapMode: Text.Wrap` turns that cap into extra lines rather than clipped text. Capping the `Text` directly is the tempting version and it is the one that loops, because a wrapped `Text` binding its own `width` to its own `implicitWidth` is self-referential once the `Control` also assigns `availableWidth`. ### Measured Of

pr.title: Stop speed test workers outliving a killed parent
pr.body: Fixes #12195. ## Problem Dismissing the Speed Test overlay while a run is in progress leaks all 8 `omarchy-network-speedtest` traffic workers. `shell.hide()` calls the panel's `close()` (SIGTERM via `Process.running = false`, asynchronous) and then drops the id from `openPanelIds` in the same call, which unloads the panel `Loader` immediately. Quickshell's `Process` destructor SIGKILLs the still-running script, so its `trap cleanup EXIT` never runs and the background `traffic_worker` subshells are orphaned. They keep looping 64 MB transfers against fast.com until the signed URLs expire (~1 h), saturating the link the whole time (~250 Mbit/s of background upload on my 300/300 line, ~100 ms latency to the LAN gateway, every video player buffering). ## Fix Each worker polls the parent PID and tears down its own transfer as soon as the parent is gone, instead of relying on the parent's EXIT trap. This also covers shell restarts and crashes. ## Testing Ran the script directly and sent the parent: | signal | direction | orphans after 1 s | residual traffic | |---|---|---|---| | SIGTERM | up | 0 | 0 Mbit/s | | SIGKILL | up | 0 | 0 Mbit/s | | SIGKILL | down | 0 | 0 Mbit/s | Before the chan

pr.title: Point direct boot at the kernel Limine boots first
pr.body: Fixes #12145 Migration 1789325478 makes `linux-omarchy` the default kernel by putting it first in Limine's `BOOT_ORDER`. A direct boot EFI entry skips Limine, so the firmware kept starting `omarchy_linux.efi` and the new kernel was never booted. Each kernel now has its own `omarchy_<kernel>.efi`, which also made `omarchy-setup-direct-boot`'s `find … | head -1` pick an unpredictable UKI. - `omarchy-setup-direct-boot` picks the UKI of the first kernel in `BOOT_ORDER`. It reads the config files in limine-entry-tool's load order, so `/etc/default/limine` wins. - New `omarchy-setup-direct-boot --refresh` repoints an existing Omarchy entry at that UKI without prompting. It creates the new entry before deleting the old one, gives the new entry the old one's place in `BootOrder`, and sets `reboot-required`. It does nothing without UEFI or a direct boot entry, when the entry already points right, or when the entry points outside the `omarchy_*.efi` UKIs. Firmware that reports the path in upper case (as in the issue) is handled. - Migration `1789592128` runs the refresh, so machines that already completed 1789325478 get repointed. ## Testing - Added `test/shell.d/omarchy-setup-direct-boot-te

pr.title: fix(hibernate): create top-level @swap subvolume so btrfs hibernation works
pr.body: ## Required change **Make the swap subvolume a top-level btrfs subvolume (`@swap`), not a subvolume nested inside the root `@` (`@/swap`).** systemd ≥ 259 refuses to hibernate into a btrfs swapfile that lives on the root subvolume tree — it reports `CanHibernate` as unavailable (empty). The setup currently creates the swap subvolume with: ```sh btrfs subvolume create /swap # run while root @ is mounted ``` Because root is mounted as `@`, this creates `@/swap` — a subvolume *nested inside* `@`, which is still "on the root subvolume tree" from systemd's point of view. Hibernation is then silently unavailable even though `resume=` / `resume_offset=` are set. This PR instead creates a **top-level `@swap`** (its own subvolume id under subvolid 5) beside `@`, and mounts it at `/swap` with `nodatacow`: ```sh mount -t btrfs -o subvolid=5 "$ROOT_DEVICE" "$BTRFS_TOP" btrfs subvolume create "$BTRFS_TOP/@swap" # top level, not @/swap mount -t btrfs -o subvol=@swap,nodatacow "$ROOT_DEVICE" /swap ``` It also removes a leftover nested `@/swap` from a previous (broken) run so existing installs self-heal. ## Why Without a top-level swap subvolume, `systemctl hibernate` / the Power menu's Hibernate

pr.title: Move only application streams when switching the audio input
pr.body: `omarchy-audio-input-set-default` moves every source output to the newly selected source. A DSP filter chain's own capture stream is a source output too, and it carries no `application.name`. Retargeting it points the chain's input at the chain's own output. pr.title: Sync explicit Kitty faces on font set
pr.body: Fixes #9167. `omarchy font set` rewrote only `font_family` in `kitty.conf`, so an explicit `bold_font`/`italic_font`/`bold_italic_font` from a previous font (or manual edit) kept rendering those faces in the old font. pr.title: Add Nextcloud to the install menu
pr.body: Dropbox is the only file sync service Omarchy can set up today, which leaves everyone self-hosting their files installing the client by hand — and then wondering why it does not come back after a reboot. - `omarchy install service nextcloud` installs `nextcloud-client`, appends `o.launch_on_start("nextcloud --background")` to `~/.config/hypr/autostart.lua`, and opens it. The append is guarded by `grep -Fxq`, so re-running it never duplicates the line. - `omarchy remove service nextcloud` stops the client, removes that autostart line, and drops the package. Synced files are left alone. - Both show up under Install → Service and Remove → Services, next to Dropbox. The autostart append deliberately differs from `omarchy-install-service-sunshine` in one detail: sunshine writes `printf '\n%s\n'`, and the removal `sed` only takes the entry line, so every install/remove cycle leaves a stray blank line behind. Here the separating newline is added only when the file does not already end in one, which keeps the append safe on a file with no trailing newline while making the round-trip byte-exact.
